■ Q11. Error states
  Verdict: ⚠️ INCONSISTENT.
  Mechanisms in use:
    - `.dashboard-access-warning` (page.tsx:206, 438) — amber banner;
      on line 438 it's overridden inline to red for errors. Should be a
      separate `.dashboard-error` class.
    - `.settings-toast.error` (SettingsPanel:568) — red toast at top.
    - Inline red box (AccessUserManager:282-284, 464-466) — `padding:
      10px; background: rgba(255,0,64,0.1); border: 1px solid var(--red);
      color: var(--red); font-size: 11px; borderRadius: 4` — duplicated
      twice, no class.
    - `alert()` for errors (AccessUserManager:213, 216) — native dialog.
    - Native `confirm()` for destructive confirms (ContentManager:84,
      AccessUserManager:201, ThemeBuilder:102, SettingsPanel:545).
  Issues:
    - No standard `.error-banner` or `.error-toast` class.
    - Error states never auto-clear in MessagesPanel (FEAT-01 finding).
    - No retry button on error.
    - No error icon (just colored text).
    - Network errors shown as raw "network" string — not localized
      (FEAT-01-A7).

■ Q12. Empty states
  Verdict: ❌ WEAK.
  Current empty states:
    - `.dashboard-empty-state` (CSS line 3437-3444): `color: text-faint;
      text-align: center; padding: 40px; font-style: italic; font-size:
      13px` — italic gray text only.
    - `.settings-empty` (CSS line 3055-3061): `color: text-dim; font-
      size: 12px; text-align: center; padding: 20px; font-style: italic`
      — italic gray text only.
    - `.archive-empty` (CSS line 2423-2428): `color: text-dim; text-
      align: center; padding: 40px 20px; font-size: 0.9rem` — gray
      text only.
  Issues:
    - No icons (e.g., 📭, 🗂️, 👥).
    - No illustrations.
    - No call-to-action button (e.g., "Create your first user").
    - Italic style doesn't fit the terminal aesthetic (terminals don't
      italicize).
    - No distinction between "no data yet" and "no data after filter".
  Recommendation: add `.empty-state-icon`, `.empty-state-title`,
  `.empty-state-hint`, `.empty-state-cta` classes.

■ Q13. Toast notifications
  Verdict: ❌ NO global toast system.
  Current state:
    - SettingsPanel has `.settings-toast` (sticky top, 3s timeout, two
      variants success/error). Only component with a toast.
    - MessagesPanel: no toast (success is silent — FEAT-01 Q7).
    - ContentManager: uses `alert()` for success (line 116) and error
      (lines 107, 119).
    - AccessUserManager: uses `alert()` for error (lines 213, 216).
    - ThemeBuilder: no toast; save success is silent (only re-fetches).
  Issues:
    - No `<ToastProvider>` context, no `useToast()` hook.
    - SettingsPanel toast `position: sticky; top: 0` scrolls out of view.
    - Toast detection via `message.startsWith("✅")` (SettingsPanel:568)
      — fragile.
    - Toast has no close button.
    - Toast has no undo action (e.g., for delete).
    - Native `alert()` blocks the entire UI thread — jarring.
  Recommendation: build a single `<ToastProvider>` with fixed
  bottom-right stacking, auto-dismiss with manual close, support
  for action buttons (Undo, Retry). Migrate all `alert()`/`confirm()`
  calls to it.

■ Q14. RTL support
  Verdict: ⚠️ PARTIAL — public site has some RTL rules; admin panel
  has almost none.
  Public site RTL (personal.css lines 1393-1407):
    - `html[dir="rtl"] .nav-links { direction: rtl; }`
    - `html[dir="rtl"] .about-stats li::before { left: auto; right: 0; }`
    - `html[dir="rtl"] .skill-card::before { right: auto; left: 12px; }`
    - `html[dir="rtl"] .book-cover::after { left: auto; right: 8px; }`
    - `html[dir="rtl"] .footer-admin { direction: ltr; }`
    - `@media (max-width: 720px) { html[dir="rtl"] .nav-links { right:
      auto; left: 0; border-left: 0; border-right: 1px solid var(--green-
      dim); transform: translateX(-100%); } }`
  Admin panel RTL (personal.css lines 3447-3451):
    - `html[dir="rtl"] .dashboard-header, .dashboard-actions,
      .dashboard-message-actions { flex-direction: row-reverse; }`
  Logical properties (the correct approach) used only 3× in CSS:
    - `padding-inline-start: 20px` (line 2805, .settings-help-list)
    - `margin-inline-start: 8px` (line 3377, .dashboard-message-email)
    - `border-inline-start: 2px solid var(--green-dim)` (line 3396,
      .dashboard-message-replies)
  Components use ZERO logical properties — all use `marginLeft`,
  `marginRight`, `textAlign: "left"/"right"`, `padding: "6px 12px"`.
  These DO NOT flip in RTL.
  Concrete bugs in RTL:
    - AccessUserManager.tsx line 244-248: `<th style={{ textAlign:
      "left" }}>` ×5 — headers stick to left in Persian.
    - AccessUserManager.tsx line 477: `<tr style={{ textAlign: "right" }}>`
      — hardcoded right; doesn't flip back to left in LTR mode.
    - AccessUserManager.tsx line 519: `style={{ marginRight: 4 }}`
      — should be `marginInlineEnd: 4`.
    - ThemeBuilder.tsx line 175: `style={{ marginRight: 4 }}`
      — should be `marginInlineEnd: 4`.
    - ThemeBuilder.tsx line 228: `marginLeft: 8`
      — should be `marginInlineStart: 8`.
    - ContentManager.tsx: items use `.admin-message-head` with
      `justify-content: space-between` — does flip via flex, but the
      item title and metadata order is hardcoded LTR.
  Recommendation: migrate all inline `marginLeft/Right` to
  `marginInlineStart/End`; replace `textAlign: "left"/"right"` with
  `textAlign: "start"/"end"`; add explicit RTL rules for any remaining
  physical-direction styles.

■ Q15. Responsive design
  Verdict: ⚠️ PARTIAL — public site is well-handled; admin panel has
  gaps.
  Public site breakpoints (good):
    - `@media (max-width: 900px)`: hero-grid, about-grid, contact-grid
      → 1 column.
    - `@media (max-width: 720px)`: section padding reduced, statusbar
      compacted, nav becomes drawer.
    - `@media (max-width: 480px)`: container padding 16px, hero-cta
      stacks, btn full-width, terminal-body smaller.
    - `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`: animations disabled.
  Admin panel breakpoints:
    - `.dashboard-tabs` → `overflow-x: auto` at 768px (good).
    - `.settings-row` → 1 column at 600px (good).
    - `.dashboard-info-grid` → 1 column at 600px (good).
    - `.dashboard-container` → padding 16px at 768px (good).
    - `.dashboard-shell` → padding 8px at 768px (good).
  Gaps:
    - AccessUserManager Users table: 9 columns at fontSize 11px — no
      breakpoint to hide secondary columns (Hours, Days, Last Login)
      on mobile. Just `overflowX: auto` — horizontal scroll required.
    - AccessUserManager Logs table: 5 columns — same issue.
    - AccessUserManager form: `gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"` for
      hour start/end (line 335) — no breakpoint, squishes on mobile.
    - ThemeBuilder editor: `gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"` (line 139)
      — no breakpoint, color inputs + preview squish on mobile.
    - ThemeBuilder theme cards: `minmax(200px, 1fr)` — OK, but cards
      have inline `padding: 10` and tiny buttons (3px 6px) that are
      hard to tap on touch screens (minimum 44×44px recommended).
    - SettingsPanel provider editor: uses `.settings-row` (good) but
      the provider list has no skeleton during re-fetch after save.
    - No `@media (max-width: 380px)` for very small phones (iPhone SE
      1st gen = 320px).
    - Dashboard tabs: when overflow-x auto on mobile, no scroll
      indicator (e.g., fade gradient on right edge) — user can't tell
      more tabs exist off-screen.

================================================================================
TOP 10 BEAUTY ISSUES TO FIX (priority order)
================================================================================

1. **CRITICAL: Undefined CSS variable `--font-vazir` used 24× in
   personal.css** (lines 2763, 2789, 2809, 2836, 2846, 2878, 2902,
   2946, 2980, 3025, 3093, 3137, 3144, 3159, 3190, 3243, 3292, 3298,
   3316, 3327, 3423, 3443 + 2 more). Only `--font-vazirmatn`, `--font-
   mono`, `--font-fa` are defined (layout.tsx + :root). The entire
   admin panel (SettingsPanel, Dashboard, AccessUserManager, Messages)
   falls back to generic `monospace` (Courier New) instead of
   Vazirmatn. Severe readability regression for Persian users.
   Fix: rename all `var(--font-vazir, monospace)` →
   `var(--font-vazirmatn, var(--font-mono))`.

2. **CRITICAL: Undefined CSS variables `--primary`, `--primary-bright`,
   `--bg-panel2` referenced in 3 components** (AccessUserManager:237,
   255, 275, 468, 477, 548, 572; AparatClipManager:130, 224, 250, 288;
   FontSelector:38). personal.css only defines `--green`/`--green-bright`
   /`--bg-panel-2`. All h3 headings render in body text color (off-
   green) instead of bright green; table headers have transparent
   background. Breaks the green-on-black theme.
   Fix: rename `--primary` → `--green`, `--primary-bright` →
   `--green-bright`, `--bg-panel2` → `--bg-panel-2` in all 3 files.

3. **HIGH: ContentManager, ThemeBuilder, AccessUserManager use
   extensive inline styles** (counts: 17 / 38 / 49 respectively).
   SettingsPanel uses ZERO inline styles — the gold standard. Inline
   styles bypass theming (e.g., switching to "clean" theme doesn't
   update inline-styled elements), bypass RTL flipping (margin-Left vs
   marginInlineStart), and prevent :hover/:focus styling. The CSS file
   has dedicated `.content-manager-type-tab` classes (lines 2490-2513)
   that are NEVER USED by ContentManager.tsx.
   Fix: extract all inline styles to semantic CSS classes
   (`.content-manager-toolbar`, `.theme-builder-editor`,
   `.theme-builder-color-row`, `.theme-builder-preview`,
   `.users-table`, `.users-table-th`, `.users-table-td`, etc.).

4. **HIGH: Native `alert()` and `confirm()` dialogs used in 8 places**
   (ContentManager:84, 107, 116, 119; AccessUserManager:201, 213, 216;
   ThemeBuilder:102; SettingsPanel:545). These break the terminal
   aesthetic — native OS dialogs over a CRT-themed UI. Also: not
   localized (ContentManager's "Delete?" is English-only; ThemeBuilder's
   "Delete this theme?" is English-only).
   Fix: build a `<ToastProvider>` for transient feedback and a
   `<ConfirmDialog>` for destructive confirms; migrate all 8 call sites.

5. **HIGH: No real loading skeletons** — only `.dashboard-loading`
   (full-screen text "Loading_" with blink cursor) and `.settings-
   loading` (plain text "Loading..."). ContentManager, ThemeBuilder,
   AccessUserManager all show plain `<p>loading...</p>` during fetch.
   No shimmer animation, no placeholder cards, no skeleton rows. The
   200-500ms fetch window looks like a broken page.
   Fix: add `.skeleton-line`, `.skeleton-card`, `.skeleton-row`,
   `.skeleton-avatar` classes with shimmer gradient animation; apply
   to MessagesPanel, AccessUserManager, ContentManager, ThemeBuilder,
   SettingsPanel providers list.

6. **HIGH: ThemeBuilder live-preview scanlines bug** (line 195-203).
   The preview container has no `position: relative`, but the
   scanlines overlay uses `position: absolute; inset: 0`. Result:
   scanlines escape the preview box and cover the entire admin panel
   when the user toggles "CRT Scanlines" on. Confirmed bug.
   Fix: add `position: "relative"` to the preview container (or
   better: extract to a `.theme-builder-preview` class with
   `position: relative`).

7. **MEDIUM: Duplicate `@keyframes blink` in personal.css** (lines 385
   and 3336). Two definitions of the same keyframe name with different
   timing: first uses `50% { opacity: 0; }` (steps(2) style), second
   uses `0%, 50% { opacity: 1; } 51%, 100% { opacity: 0; }` (smooth).
   Second definition overrides first; the terminal cursor `.brand::
   before` (line 383) and chat cursor `.terminal-cursor` (line 629)
   end up using the second animation, looking different from the
   original design intent.
   Fix: rename one to `@keyframes blink-step` (steps-based) and the
   other to `@keyframes blink-smooth`; update references.

8. **MEDIUM: Inconsistent border-radius tokens** — base `--radius: 2px`
   (sharp terminal aesthetic), but admin panels hardcode `border-
   radius: 6px` (3×), `8px` (4×), `10px` (1×), `12px` (2×), `4px`,
   `1px`, `50%` (6×). The terminal sharp-corner aesthetic is lost in
   the admin area, which looks like Material Design. No `--radius-lg`,
   `--radius-pill` tokens.
   Fix: define `--radius: 2px; --radius-sm: 0; --radius-md: 4px;
   --radius-lg: 8px; --radius-pill: 999px` and migrate.

9. **MEDIUM: SettingsPanel toast is `position: sticky; top: 0` and
   uses brittle success detection** (line 2974-2983 CSS, line 568
   TSX). Sticky-top scrolls out of view in long settings lists (the
   Help card is far below the fold). `message.startsWith("✅")`
   classifies success vs error — works only because `t.saved =
   "✅ ذخیره شد"` and `t.error = "❌ خطا"`. Any future message
   without an emoji prefix, or with a different emoji, is mis-
   classified. Also no close button, no undo action.
   Fix: change to `position: fixed; bottom: 24px; right: 24px` (or
   `inset-inline-end: 24px` for RTL); track success/error via a
   dedicated state field `{ text: string, kind: "success" | "error" }`
   instead of string-prefix sniffing.

10. **MEDIUM: No defined spacing scale** — uses raw values 4/6/8/10/
    12/14/16/18/20/24/28/32/40/48/60/80 px ad-hoc. Same conceptual
    gap (e.g., card padding) varies: 20px (`.about-card`), 24px
    (`.contact-form`, `.dashboard-container`), 14px (`.osc-controls`),
    16px (`.signal-controls`), 10px (`.settings-provider-item`).
    No `--space-1`...`--space-8` tokens; hard to maintain visual
    rhythm.
    Fix: define `--space-1: 4px; --space-2: 8px; --space-3: 12px;
    --space-4: 16px; --space-5: 24px; --space-6: 32px; --space-7:
    48px; --space-8: 64px` and migrate all hardcoded values.

Overall beauty score: 6.5 / 10.

Public site (hero, sections, terminal, chat, RF visualizations): 8.5/10

Admin panel:

================================================================================
AUDIT RESULTS — 10 criteria
================================================================================

■ Q1. Does chat work end-to-end?
  Verdict: ✅ YES, with caveats (races + dedup gap).

  Happy path (works):
    - Visitor types → ChatSection.tsx:80-129 send()
    - POST /api/chat with {sessionId, message, lang, visitorId}
      (ChatSection.tsx:90-99)
    - Server: rate-limit check (route.ts:72), body validation
      (route.ts:79-97), api-enabled check (route.ts:99-115),
      get-or-create session (route.ts:117-131), save user msg
      (route.ts:134-136), build LLM history (route.ts:152-159),
      callLLMWithFallback (route.ts:164-185), save assistant msg
      (route.ts:192-194), return {ok, sessionId, reply, messageId}
      (route.ts:202-207)
    - Client: setSessionId + append reply (ChatSection.tsx:101-106),
      setLastPollTs(Date.now()) (ChatSection.tsx:108)
    - Polling for admin-side replies via /api/chat/messages
      (ChatSection.tsx:58-78)

  Caveats (correctness/robustness, NOT blockers):
    - ⚠️ ChatSection.tsx:24-32 — visitorId is populated in a
      useEffect that runs AFTER first render. send() at line 97
      reads `visitorId` from closure; if the user submits before
      the effect fires (e.g., SSR / very fast paste+enter),
      visitorId="" is sent. Server then defaults to "anon"
      (route.ts:89). Minor — first-message race only.
    - ⚠️ ChatSection.tsx:108 vs route.ts:192-194 — client bumps
      lastPollTs to Date.now() (client clock), but the saved
      assistant message uses server-clock createdAt. With clock
      skew (client behind server), the next poll (since=client_ts)
      can RE-fetch the same reply that was already appended at
      ChatSection.tsx:103-106 → duplicate assistant bubble. No
      message-id dedup anywhere in setMessages.
    - ⚠️ ChatSection.tsx:65-72 — polled messages are appended
      with no key on messageId; only array index `i` is used as
      React key (ChatSection.tsx:159). Two messages with identical
      content from the same ts would render fine, but duplicates
      from the Q1 race above would visibly stack.
    - ⚠️ ChatSection.tsx:78 — `lastPollTs` is in the polling
      effect's dep array, so EVERY new polled message triggers
      clearInterval + setInterval (ChatSection.tsx:77). Polling
      effectively restarts its 3s timer whenever a new message
      arrives — not broken, but churns timers and can stretch
      effective poll interval under steady traffic.

■ Q2. Does it poll for responses?
  Verdict: ✅ YES — setInterval 3000ms, fetches assistant msgs.

  Mechanism (ChatSection.tsx:58-78):
    - setInterval(3000) on /api/chat/messages?sessionId&since
    - Only starts once sessionId is set (line 59 guard)
    - Filters server-side by role:"assistant" (messages/route.ts:24-25)
      — so user-side echoes don't bounce back
    - Updates lastPollTs from data.serverTime on each new batch
      (ChatSection.tsx:73)

  Issues:
    - ⚠️ ChatSection.tsx:75 — `catch {}` swallows ALL poll errors
      silently. Network drop → user sees nothing, no retry, no UI.
    - ⚠️ No backoff: a downed /api/chat/messages is hit every 3s
      forever, generating 20 failing req/min per open chat tab.
    - ⚠️ messages/route.ts has NO rate limit (route.ts POST does,
      at route.ts:7-21). Poll endpoint is unauthenticated AND
      unrate-limited. Anyone with a sessionId can spam-poll.
      SessionIds are Prisma cuid/uuid so not guessable, but a
      visitor polling their OWN session is uncapped.
    - ⚠️ messages/route.ts:21-33 — no `take`/pagination. A session
      with 10k assistant messages returns all of them in one
      response since some arbitrary past `since`. Combined with
      the unbounded history (Q4) this is a memory bomb.
    - ⚠️ ChatSection.tsx:78 deps: as in Q1, restarting on every
      lastPollTs change.

■ Q3. Is visitorId forgeable?
  Verdict: ❌ YES — fully client-controlled, no signing, no HMAC.

  Evidence:
    - ChatSection.tsx:28 — `v = "v_" + Math.random().toString(36)
      .slice(2,10) + Date.now().toString(36)` generated in browser,
      stored in localStorage under "portfolio_visitor_id".
      Anyone can `localStorage.setItem("portfolio_visitor_id",
      "v_impersonate_victim")` and impersonate.
    - ChatSection.tsx:97 — sent in POST body as plain string.
    - route.ts:89 — `const visitorId = String(body.visitorId||"")
      .slice(0,100) || "anon";` — server accepts ANY string ≤100
      chars, no validation, no auth.
    - route.ts:127 — visitorId is written to the ChatSession row
      as a label. Admin dashboard trusts it for grouping.

  Impact (mitigations limit blast radius):
    - ❌ Visitor can rotate visitorId per request → admin dashboard
      fills up with N fake "new sessions" — pollutes audit trail.
    - ❌ Visitor can spoof another visitor's visitorId to make
      their messages appear grouped under the victim's identity
      in admin view.
    - ✅ Rate limit is per-IP (route.ts:11), NOT per-visitorId, so
      rotating visitorId does NOT bypass send-rate-limit.
    - ✅ No auth/authorization decision hinges on visitorId; it is
      purely a soft label. So forgeability does NOT escalate to
      account takeover or admin access.

  Severity: MEDIUM (audit-trail poisoning, no auth bypass).

■ Q4. Is chat history bounded?
  Verdict: ❌ NO — unbounded in 4 places.

  Evidence:
    - ❌ Client-side: ChatSection.tsx:16 — `messages` state grows
      forever. No slice/cap. Long-running tab + busy session =
      unbounded memory + DOM.
    - ❌ Server LLM context: route.ts:152-159 — `history` is built
      from `session.messages` (the FULL message list, no `take`,
      no truncation) and shipped to the LLM at
      providers.ts:170. Token blowup risk on long sessions;
      provider will either truncate silently (OpenAI) or 400
      (Anthropic).
    - ❌ Server DB: no cap on ChatMessage rows per session. A
      10k-message session is allowed.
    - ❌ Admin GET (route.ts:231-240): sessions are capped at 100
      (take:100) but `messages` include has no cap, so each of
      the 100 sessions returns ALL its messages. A pathological
      site can return 100 × ∞ rows in one admin call.
    - ❌ Poll endpoint (messages/route.ts:21-33): no `take`. A
      very-old `since=0` would return the whole session.

  Severity: HIGH (DB / memory growth, LLM token cost).

■ Q5. Is there auto-scroll?
  Verdict: ✅ YES — both components.

  ChatSection.tsx:48-52 — useEffect on [messages] sets
    bodyRef.scrollTop = scrollHeight.
  InteractiveTerminal.tsx:23-27 — same pattern on [lines].

  Caveats:
    - ⚠️ No "user scrolled up" detection — if a visitor scrolls
      up to read history and a new message arrives, they are
      snapped back to the bottom. Minor UX, not a bug.
    - ⚠️ ChatSection.tsx:166-173 — the typing indicator is also
      in `messages`-driven autoscroll scope (because `sending`
      adds a DOM node, but the effect fires on `messages`, not
      `sending`). Actually the typing bubble appears WITHOUT a
      messages change, so autoscroll does NOT fire when the
      typing indicator appears. The user sees the typing dots
      appear below the fold until the next messages update.
      Minor cosmetic issue.

  Severity: LOW (works for the happy path).

■ Q6. Is there a loading indicator?
  Verdict: ✅ YES — typing dots while `sending`.

  Evidence:
    - ChatSection.tsx:18 — `sending` state
    - ChatSection.tsx:85 — setSending(true) at start of send()
    - ChatSection.tsx:126 — setSending(false) in `finally`
    - ChatSection.tsx:166-173 — renders `.chat-typing` 3-dot
      bubble when sending
    - ChatSection.tsx:185 — input disabled while sending
    - ChatSection.tsx:190 — submit button disabled while sending

  Caveats:
    - ⚠️ No loading state for the FIRST poll fetch (sessionId
      set but no assistant reply yet). Acceptable since the POST
      reply is synchronous.
    - ⚠️ No streaming — visitor waits for the entire LLM response
      before seeing anything beyond the typing dots. For a 5s
      LLM call this is fine; for a 30s Ollama call it looks
      frozen.
    - ⚠️ No spinner/skeleton on initial component mount — the
      greeting (ChatSection.tsx:41-43) is set synchronously so
      this is fine in practice.

  Severity: NONE (criterion met).

■ Q7. Is there an error state?
  Verdict: ⚠️ PARTIAL — dead `error` state, errors shown as
  assistant messages instead.

  Evidence:
    - ChatSection.tsx:19 — `const [error, setError] = useState("")`
      is declared and mutated (line 86 clears it) but NEVER
      rendered. Dead code.
    - ChatSection.tsx:110-118 — error path appends a localized
      "..." message as role:"assistant". So the user sees what
      looks like an AI reply saying "... Error. Try again."
    - ChatSection.tsx:120-124 — generic catch appends

    - No `role="alert"` anywhere — errors are not announced to

■ Q8. Is there an empty state?
  Verdict: ✅ YES — greeting message on first mount.

  Evidence:
    - ChatSection.tsx:35-45 — useEffect on [lang] sets a single

    - All three locales covered (en/de/fa) at lines 37-39.
    - Greeting is contextual and inviting ("Patched through.
      I'm the site's AI concierge. What brings you here today?")

  Caveats:
    - ⚠️ Greeting effect depends only on [lang], but checks

■ Q9. Is there rate limit feedback?
  Verdict: ✅ YES — but minimally informative.

  Server side:
    - route.ts:7-9 — RATE_WINDOW_MS = 60_000, RATE_MAX = 8.
    - route.ts:11-21 — rateLimit(ip) tracks hits per IP in a
      Map. Returns false when ≥8 in the last minute.
    - route.ts:12-14 — dev bypass: in non-prod, "::1",
      "127.0.0.1", "unknown" always pass.
    - route.ts:72-77 — returns 429 {ok:false, error:"rate_limit"}

  Client side:
    - ChatSection.tsx:110-113 — branches on `err === "rate_limit"`
      and shows localized "... Channel busy. Hold a sec." (all 3
      langs covered at line 113).

  Issues:
    - ⚠️ No Retry-After header, no countdown, no "wait Xs". User
      just sees "hold a sec" and is left to guess.
    - ⚠️ Rate limit is per-IP only (route.ts:11), not per-session
      or per-visitorId. Shared NAT (corporate wifi, mobile carrier
      CGNAT) means 8 visitors behind one IP collectively hit the
      cap. Bug.
    - ⚠️ The dev bypass at route.ts:12-14 lets "unknown" IPs
      through in dev — fine for local dev, but if a reverse
      proxy ever forwards an empty x-forwarded-for in production,
      that request is treated as "unknown" and bypasses the limiter.
      Should be scoped to `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"`
      ONLY (which it is), so production is safe. ✅
    - ⚠️ Poll endpoint /api/chat/messages has NO rate limit.
      A malicious visitor polling at 100ms intervals can hammer
      the DB. Combined with Q2's no-auth, this is the larger
      rate-limit gap.
    - ⚠️ ChatSection.tsx:112-113 — rate-limit feedback is
      appended as an assistant message, not a dedicated banner.
      Looks like the AI said "... Channel busy." Minor UX.
    - ⚠️ No client-side cooldown — visitor can keep hitting
      Enter and generating 429s. The disabled-while-sending
      guard (ChatSection.tsx:82) only blocks concurrent sends,
      not rapid-fire retries after a 429.

  Severity: MEDIUM (per-IP limit too coarse, no poll rate limit,
  weak UX).

■ Q10. Is AI disabled gracefully when no provider?
  Verdict: ⚠️ PARTIAL — two distinct "disabled" paths, one works
  (kill switch), the other leaks a placeholder (no-provider demo).

  Two failure modes:

  (A) Admin kill switch (`apiEnabled` setting):
    - route.ts:99-115 — checks isApiEnabled() (settings.ts:44-47,
      reads "apiEnabled" from SiteSetting table; default "true").
      If disabled, returns 503 with:
        {ok:false, error:"api_disabled", message:<localized>}
    - Server-side: ✅ correct, NO db writes happen — user message
      is NOT saved, no session is created. Clean.
    - Client-side: ❌ ChatSection.tsx:109-118 — the handler does
      NOT branch on `err === "api_disabled"`. It falls into the
      generic else, which checks `err === "rate_limit"` (false)
      and shows the generic "... Error. Try again." The server's
      localized `data.message` ("Chat is temporarily disabled.")
      is NEVER READ. Bug — kill-switch UX is wrong.

  (B) No providers configured (`callLLMWithFallback`):
    - providers.ts:47-55 — when getEnabledProviders() returns [],
      the function does NOT throw. It RETURNS a hardcoded demo
      message:
        "Hi! I'm a demo AI assistant. To enable real AI
         responses, the site admin needs to configure an AI
         provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, OpenRouter, or
         Ollama) from the admin panel → Settings → AI Providers."
        providerId: "demo"
    - route.ts:170-185 — this demo string flows into `reply`,
      which is then SAVED to the DB as an assistant message
      (route.ts:192-194) AND returned to the visitor.
    - So a brand-new deploy with no providers configured will
      save the demo text as if it were a real AI reply on every
      visitor message → pollutes admin logs with N copies of the
      same placeholder. Bug.
    - The demo message is English-only (providers.ts:52) — Persian
      and German visitors get English. No localization. Bug.

  (C) All providers FAIL at call time:
    - providers.ts:69 — throws "All providers failed. ..."
    - route.ts:176-185 — caught, returns a localized fallback
      reply ("I'm having trouble connecting right now...").
      ✅ This case is handled gracefully.
    - The fallback is saved to DB (route.ts:192-194) — same
      "save placeholder as if real" issue as (B), but at least
      the placeholder is localized and informative.

  Summary:
    - Kill switch (A): server ✅, client ❌ (drops localized msg)
    - No-provider (B): server ❌ (saves demo placeholder as if
      it were a real reply, EN-only)
    - All-fail (C): ✅ handled

  Severity: MEDIUM (functional but UX/audit-trail wrong).

================================================================================
SUMMARY MATRIX
================================================================================

  visitor can amplify.

  case (providers.ts:49-55) saves an English-only demo placeholder
  to the DB as if it were a real AI reply. Both make the site
  look "alive" when it's actually broken.

  the four unbounded-history spots and the poll rate-limit gap)
  plus M1+M2 (close the two AI-disabled UX holes). These five
  fixes lift the audit from "PARTIAL/FAIL" to "PASS" on criteria
  #3, #4, #7, #10.

File: src/components/ContentManager.tsx

  — calls `JSON.parse(e.specs)`. If `e.specs` is `"invalid json"`,

  returns `{ ok: false, error: "server_error" }` HTTP 500 → frontend

    - Frontend: in saveItem, before POST, attempt

================================================================================
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================
The site ships with a tri-lingual content model (en/de/fa) and a working
lang switcher, but the i18n implementation is partial and inconsistent.
- The DB schema stores all 3 langs for SiteText, Book, Article, Tutorial,
  Skill, NavItem. ✅
- LabEquipment and AiInstruction models are NOT localized (single-language
  columns). ❌
- The homepage lang switcher does NOT persist across refresh. ❌
- Many UI strings are hardcoded English (terminal commands, clips section,
  DevTools warning, statusbar, lab equipment rack, admin buttons). ❌
- Many UI strings are hardcoded Persian only (user-login page entire file,
  AccessUserManager, AparatClipManager, FontSelector — these components
  accept NO `lang` prop). ❌
- German (de) translations are missing from most inline ternary strings
  (lang === "fa" ? X : Y — falls through to English when de is selected). ❌
- RTL is applied via `document.documentElement.dir = "rtl"` for fa, but
  CSS uses physical properties (margin-left, padding-left, border-left,
  text-align:right) extensively. Only 8 selectors in personal.css get
  explicit RTL overrides; the rest are NOT mirrored. ❌
- The ArchiveGrid component ignores the `lang` prop when rendering item
  titles/descriptions — it always uses item.titleEn, item.descEn, etc. ❌

strings bypass it:

Q2. Is RTL applied when fa selected?
------------------------------------
PARTIALLY. The `<html dir="rtl">` attribute IS set on client mount:
  - page.tsx:106-109 — `document.documentElement.dir = tt.dir` (en/de = "ltr", fa = "rtl")
  - user-dashboard/page.tsx:96, 119 — panel sets dir based on lang
  - SettingsPanel.tsx:276, 290 — panel sets dir based on lang

BUT:
  - layout.tsx:111 — initial SSR HTML is `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">` (hardcoded).
    JS overrides it after hydration (suppressed via suppressHydrationWarning on
    <html> and <body>). Initial paint is always LTR for ALL visitors, including
    Persian. Causes FOUC for RTL users.
  - personal.css:170-172 — only sets `font-family: var(--font-fa)` on RTL body.
    NO other global RTL adjustments (e.g. body { direction: rtl } is implicit
    via dir attribute, but physical margins/paddings are not flipped).
  - Only 8 selectors get explicit RTL overrides in the entire CSS:
      - personal.css:1394 — `html[dir="rtl"] .nav-links { direction: rtl; }`
      - personal.css:1395 — `html[dir="rtl"] .about-stats li::before { left: auto; right: 0; }`
      - personal.css:1396 — `html[dir="rtl"] .skill-card::before { right: auto; left: 12px; }`
      - personal.css:1397 — `html[dir="rtl"] .book-cover::after { left: auto; right: 8px; }`
      - personal.css:1398 — `html[dir="rtl"] .footer-admin { direction: ltr; }`
      - personal.css:1400-1406 — mobile nav-links RTL override (transform/position)
      - personal.css:3447-3451 — dashboard-header/actions/message-actions flex-direction: row-reverse
  - Every other element with physical CSS (left:/right:/margin-left:/padding-left:/
    border-left:/text-align:left|right) is NOT mirrored in RTL. See Q9 for full list.

Q5. Does TextEditor save all 3 languages?
-----------------------------------------
YES. ✅
  - TextEditor.tsx:31-48 — saveText sends `valueEn: val.en, valueFa: val.fa, valueDe: val.de` in the POST body.
  - /api/admin/text/route.ts:54-70 (set action) — upserts all 3 fields:
      `valueEn: String(body.valueEn || "")`,
      `valueFa: String(body.valueFa || "")`,
      `valueDe: String(body.valueDe || "")`
  - /api/admin/text/route.ts:74-96 (bulk_set action) — same for each item.
  - prisma/schema.prisma:338-344 — SiteText model has all 3 fields
    (valueEn String @default(""), valueFa String @default(""), valueDe String @default("")).
  - TextEditor.tsx:113-154 — UI renders 3 textareas (EN, FA, DE) per key.
  - TextEditor.tsx:133 — FA textarea has `dir="rtl"`. ✅ (proper RTL for the textarea)

Q6. Does homepage display in correct language?
----------------------------------------------
PARTIALLY. ✅ for the static UI labels (via UI[lang]); ❌ for archive content.

✅ What works:
  - page.tsx:101 — `const tt = UI[lang]` picks the right translation bundle.
  - page.tsx:103 — `tx(key, fallback)` helper reads DB-first, falls back to UI[lang] constant.
  - /api/content/route.ts:25-34 — returns textsByLang.en/fa/de (all 3 langs).
  - page.tsx:546 — name: `siteContent.settings?.["name_" + lang] || PERSONAL.fullName[lang]` (DB-first, correct).
  - page.tsx:471-495 — navItems: picks `item[label${Lang}]` dynamically (correct).
  - page.tsx:624-626 — skills: picks `s[category${Lang}]` dynamically (correct).
  - page.tsx:845 — tutorial modal title: `activeTutorial.title[lang]` (correct for static fallback data).

❌ What doesn't work:
  - ArchiveGrid.tsx:138-141 — Article rendering uses `item.typeEn`, `item.titleEn || item.titleFa`, `item.venueEn`, `(item.summaryEn || "").slice(0, 120)` — ALWAYS English, ignores `lang` prop.
  - ArchiveGrid.tsx:157 — Book cover title: `item.titleEn || item.titleFa` — always En, no De.
  - ArchiveGrid.tsx:162, 164-165 — Book body uses `item.publisherEn`, `item.titleEn || item.titleFa`, `(item.descEn || "").slice(0, 100)` — always En.
  - ArchiveGrid.tsx:185-187 — Tutorial card uses `item.levelEn`, `item.titleEn || item.titleFa`, `(item.descEn || "").slice(0, 80)` — always En.
  - ArchiveGrid.tsx:52 — sort by title uses `(a.titleEn || "").localeCompare(b.titleEn || "")` — only English titles considered for sorting.
  - page.tsx:547 — tagline uses `PERSONAL.tagline[lang]` from local content.ts, NOT from DB settings.tagline_en/fa/de (which the SettingsPanel saves to). So tagline edited in admin panel NEVER appears on the homepage.
  - page.tsx:547 — fullName same issue: page uses PERSONAL.fullName[lang] only as fallback when DB has no `name_${lang}` setting; OK for name but inconsistent with tagline.
  - LabEquipment displayed via LabEquipmentRack shows `eq.name` and `eq.description` (single column, no lang variants). Schema LabEquipment (prisma/schema.prisma:145-160) has no En/Fa/De fields. Equipment names always show in whatever single language the admin typed.
  - page.tsx:697-699 — Clips section title uses inline `lang === "fa" ? "ویدیوها" : "Clips"` (no de).
  - page.tsx:348 — reCAPTCHA error uses `lang === "fa" ? "لطفاً تأیید ربات را انجام دهید." : "Please complete the robot check."` (no de).
  - /api/content/route.ts:46-49 — equipment returned as `...e` (spread, no lang selection). Same single-column issue.
  - AparatClipManager clips (page.tsx:716-720) — `clip.title` and `clip.description` rendered directly (no localization, AparatClip schema not in Prisma model — likely stored as JSON or single column).

Q7. Does language persist across refresh?
----------------------------------------
NO for the public homepage; YES for admin panel. ❌ (asymmetric)

Public homepage (page.tsx):
  - page.tsx:55 — `const [lang, setLang] = useState<Lang>(DEFAULT_LANG)` — DEFAULT_LANG = "en" (content.ts:9).
  - page.tsx:519-528 — lang switcher just calls `setLang(l)`. NO localStorage.setItem for lang.
  - page.tsx:113-120 — only theme is persisted via `localStorage.getItem("portfolio_theme")` / `setItem("portfolio_theme", theme)`.
  - Grep confirms: page.tsx has NO `site_lang`, `portfolio_lang`, or any other lang localStorage key.
  - Result: visitor selects FA, refreshes page → reverts to EN, dir reverts to LTR. ❌

Admin panel:
  - user-dashboard/page.tsx:93 — `localStorage.getItem("panel_lang") as Lang` (defaults to "fa").
  - user-dashboard/page.tsx:117 — `localStorage.setItem("panel_lang", newLang)`.
  - SettingsPanel.tsx:273 — same load logic.
  - SettingsPanel.tsx:288 — same save logic.
  - Result: admin's panel language persists across refresh. ✅

Note: The two language stores are completely separate. A visitor's homepage
lang and an admin's panel lang are stored in DIFFERENT localStorage keys
(panel_lang vs nothing). There is no shared language context.

Q8. Are there text overflow issues in RTL?
------------------------------------------
POTENTIALLY YES, due to insufficient RTL handling and lack of `dir="auto"`.

Positional elements that don't flip in RTL (will appear on wrong side):
  - personal.css:991 — `.to-top { bottom: 8px; right: 8px; }` — to-top button stays on right in RTL (should be left).
  - personal.css:1221 — `bottom: 24px; right: 24px;` — fixed-position element stays on right.
  - personal.css:738 — `.skill-card::before { top: 8px; right: 12px; }` — "//" badge stays on right (overridden for RTL on line 1396).
  - personal.css:818 — `.chat-prompt { top: 0; bottom: 0; left: 8px; }` — chat prompt "tx>" indicator stays on left in RTL (should be right).
  - personal.css:1132 — `top: -1px; left: -1px; right: -1px;` — modal bar positioning.

Borders that don't flip:
  - personal.css:1296 — `.admin-message { border-left: 3px solid var(--green); }` — accent border stays on left in RTL.
  - personal.css:1584 — `.chat-msg-assistant .chat-msg-text { border-left: 2px solid var(--green); }` — accent border stays on left in RTL (should be right).
  - personal.css:1685 — `.admin-session { border-left: 3px solid var(--green); }` — same.

Paddings/margins that don't flip:
  - personal.css:887 — `.article-row:hover { padding-left: 24px; }` — stays on left in RTL.
  - personal.css:986 — `.tutorial-play::before { margin-left: 3px; }` — stays on left.
  - personal.css:774 — `.tags li::before { margin-right: 2px; }` — stays on right (the dot before tags).
  - personal.css:1681 — `.admin-stat strong { margin-right: 4px; }` — stays on right.
  - personal.css:1713 — `margin-right: 6px;` — stays on right.
  - personal.css:1952 — `.admin-reply-status { margin-left: 8px; }` — stays on left.

Inline-style physical CSS:
  - NavMenuManager.tsx:124 — `marginLeft: 8` (physical, not logical)
  - Multiple components use inline `style={{ padding: "12px 16px" }}` etc. (mostly OK — symmetric).

Text alignment:
  - personal.css:2482 — `.equipment-spec-val { text-align: right; }` — stays right-aligned in both LTR and RTL (could be OK or could be wrong depending on intent).
  - No `text-align: left` issues detected except via default.

Mixed-content bidi (NO `dir="auto"` anywhere):
  - All chat-msg-text, article-summary, book-description, etc. containers lack `dir="auto"`. Mixed Persian + English + numbers will display with incorrect bidi ordering for embedded LTR runs.
  - InteractiveTerminal.tsx:186 — terminal-bar-title "guest@portfolio — bash — 80x24" is LTR string shown in RTL container without `dir="ltr"` override — may render with reversed dash order.

Long text overflow:
  - personal.css:1395-1397 — about-stats/skill-card/book-cover pseudo-elements ARE overridden. ✅
  - But admin-message, admin-session, chat-msg-assistant border-left is NOT flipped. ❌
  - No `word-break: break-word` on `.equipment-spec-val` could cause long spec values to overflow in narrow RTL columns (the rule on line 2483 has word-break, but text-align: right + max-width: 60% could push beyond container in RTL).

Layout.tsx SSR FOUC for RTL:
  - layout.tsx:111 — SSR HTML is `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">`. Persian visitor's first paint is LTR, then JS switches to RTL after hydration (with suppressHydrationWarning masking the warning). Causes brief visual flash.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q1. Does it run prisma db push before seeding?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Verdict: YES — with caveats.

  Evidence:
    install.sh:134  TABLES=$(sqlite3 db/custom.db "SELECT count(*) FROM
                   sqlite_master WHERE type='table';" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
    install.sh:135  if [ "$TABLES" = "0" ] || [ -z "$TABLES" ]; then
    install.sh:137    node node_modules/prisma/build/index.js db push
                       --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -3
    install.sh:143  ADMIN_EXISTS=$(sqlite3 db/custom.db "SELECT count(*) FROM
                       AccessUser WHERE username='admin';" ...)
    install.sh:144  if [ "$ADMIN_EXISTS" = "0" ] || [ -z "$ADMIN_EXISTS" ]; then
    install.sh:146-149  python3 seed scripts run HERE (after push)

  Order is correct: db push (line 137) runs BEFORE any seeding (lines 146-149).

  Caveats:
    (a) Line 135: push only runs when table count is 0. If schema.prisma gains
        a NEW model and the DB already has SOME tables, the new table is NEVER
        created. Re-running install.sh on an upgraded schema will not migrate
        it. Condition should be "if AccessUser table missing" not "if zero
        tables".
    (b) Line 137: hardcoded path `node_modules/prisma/build/index.js`. No
        existence check. If prisma isn't installed at that path (e.g., the
        "pre-built standalone" doesn't ship node_modules/prisma), the command
        fails. Piped to `tail -3`, so the error is truncated; combined with
        `set -e` the script would exit, but the piped `tail` masks the exit
        code (pipefail not set), so it may continue silently with empty DB.
    (c) Line 137: `--accept-data-loss` always passed. Safe for fresh install
        but DANGEROUS on upgrades — silent data loss if schema change drops
        a column. No prompt, no log entry beyond `tail -3`.
    (d) Line 137: does not run `prisma generate`. If @prisma/client needs to
        be regenerated (rare for standalone), it isn't.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q2. Does it check if admin exists before seeding?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Verdict: YES — double-protected.

  Evidence:
    install.sh:143  ADMIN_EXISTS=$(sqlite3 db/custom.db
                     "SELECT count(*) FROM AccessUser WHERE username='admin';"
                     2>/dev/null || echo "0")
    install.sh:144  if [ "$ADMIN_EXISTS" = "0" ] || [ -z "$ADMIN_EXISTS" ]; then
    install.sh:146-149  seeds run only inside this branch
    install.sh:151-153  else branch: "✅ دیتابیس آماده (admin user exists)"

  Cross-check (seed_access_users.py:90-96): the python script ALSO checks for
    existing admin via `SELECT id, username FROM AccessUser WHERE username=?`
    and skips with `"Admin user already exists ... Skipping."` So even if
    install.sh's gate is bypassed, the python script is idempotent.

  Caveats:
    (a) Line 143: SQL is run via `sqlite3` CLI on `db/custom.db` directly.
        If the AccessUser table doesn't exist (e.g., prisma db push at line
        137 failed silently), the query returns no rows but `2>/dev/null`
        swallows the error and `|| echo "0"` returns "0". The seeding branch
        runs, but seed_access_users.py:69-88 also has its own table-existence
        check and runs prisma db push itself. So there's a redundant safety
        net for this specific case. Other seeds (seed_content.py,
        seed_equipment.py, seed_texts.py) are NOT audited here — they may
        fail if tables are missing.
    (b) Lines 146-148: ALL four seeds run if admin is missing. If admin was
        manually deleted from a previously-seeded DB, all four seeds re-run
        — including seed_content.py / seed_equipment.py / seed_texts.py,
        which may duplicate content if they don't internally check for
        existing rows (only seed_access_users.py was audited; others are
        not in audit scope).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q3. Does it generate strong SESSION_SECRET?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Verdict: YES — 256-bit entropy, but no openssl presence check.

  Evidence:
    install.sh:93  SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
    install.sh:111 SESSION_SECRET="$SECRET"
    install.sh:119 echo "  ✅ SESSION_SECRET قوی تولید شد (hex 64 chars)"

  32 bytes → 64 hex chars → 256 bits of entropy. Strong enough.

  Caveats:
    (a) Line 93: openssl is NOT installed by step 3 (line 68 installs only
        nginx sqlite3 python3 ufw certbot python3-certbot-nginx). On most
        Debian/Ubuntu installs openssl is pre-installed, but not guaranteed
        on minimal/container images. If openssl is missing:
        - command substitution returns empty (no error under `set -e` for
          plain assignment).
        - .env gets `SESSION_SECRET=""` (line 111).
        - The success message at line 119 still prints.
        This is a SILENT SECURITY FAILURE — empty session secret = predictable
        sessions = admin impersonation.
    (b) Line 93: entropy source is /dev/urandom (via openssl). On a freshly
        booted VM with low entropy, urandom still returns 32 bytes (Linux
        getrandom() blocks until sufficient entropy, but only at boot).
        Not a practical concern.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q4. Does it generate webhook secrets?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Verdict: YES.

  Evidence:
    install.sh:98  BALE_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
    install.sh:99  TG_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
    install.sh:115 BALE_WEBHOOK_SECRET="$BALE_SECRET"
    install.sh:116 TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET="$TG_SECRET"

    install.sh:302-303 printed in final output (when DOMAIN_FOUND)
    install.sh:305-306 printed in final output (no domain, with placeholder)

  16 bytes → 128 bits each. Adequate for webhook HMAC verification.

  Caveats:
    (a) Same openssl-missing risk as Q3. If openssl is missing, both webhook
        secrets are empty strings. Empty webhook secret + an unauthenticated
        webhook endpoint = anyone can post to /api/bale/webhook.
    (b) 128-bit is less than SESSION_SECRET's 256-bit. Not a bug, but
        inconsistent entropy policy.

Q5. Does it create non-root systemd user?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Verdict: YES — properly.

  Evidence:
    install.sh:180  if ! id -u ehsansite &>/dev/null; then
    install.sh:181    useradd -r -s /bin/false -d "$SITE_DIR" ehsansite
                       2>/dev/null || true
    install.sh:183  chown -R ehsansite:ehsansite "$SITE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
    install.sh:192  User=ehsansite
    install.sh:193  Group=ehsansite
    install.sh:202  NoNewPrivileges=true
    install.sh:203  ProtectSystem=full
    install.sh:204  ProtectHome=true
    install.sh:205  ReadWritePaths=$SITE_DIR
    install.sh:206  PrivateTmp=true

  `useradd -r` (system user, no aging, UID < 1000), `-s /bin/false` (no shell
  login), `-d "$SITE_DIR"` (home dir set to site dir). Service runs as
  ehsansite:ehsansite. Hardening directives (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem,
  ProtectHome, PrivateTmp) are all present and correct.

  Caveats:
    (a) Line 181: `|| true` masks useradd failure. If useradd fails (e.g.,
        UID exhaustion, read-only /etc/passwd), the script continues. Then
        chown at line 183 fails (also `|| true`), and systemd at line 214
        fails to start the service because User=ehsansite doesn't exist.
        The error surfaces only at the curl check (line 230) as
        "⚠ چک کن: journalctl -u personal-site -n 20".
    (b) Line 181: `-d "$SITE_DIR"` does not create the home directory
        (no -m). $SITE_DIR already exists (it's the project dir). Fine.
    (c) Line 183: chown runs BEFORE the systemd service file is written
        (line 185). The service file at /etc/systemd/system/personal-site.service
        is owned by root (default), which is correct. The .env file inside
        $SITE_DIR is now owned by ehsansite. The systemd ExecStart at line 195
        runs `node server.js` from WorkingDirectory=$SITE_DIR as ehsansite —
        can read .env. ✓
    (d) Line 183: `chown -R` on the entire $SITE_DIR. If $SITE_DIR contains
        node_modules, this chowns thousands of files. Slow but not broken.

Q6. Does it set chmod 600 on .env and db?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Verdict: YES in the primary path; PARTIAL in the standalone copy path.

  Evidence:
    install.sh:95   chmod 700 db            (directory, before .env creation)
    install.sh:118  chmod 600 .env          (after heredoc at 105-117)
    install.sh:128  chmod 700 db            (redundant — already 700 from 95)
    install.sh:130  chmod 600 db/custom.db  (after touch at 129)
    install.sh:131  rm -f db/custom.db-journal db/custom.db-wal db/custom.db-shm

  Caveats:
    (a) Line 166: in the `.next/standalone` branch (line 164 elif),
        `cp .env .next/standalone/.env` copies .env to standalone, but does
        NOT re-run chmod. GNU cp without -p uses umask: source mode 600 &
        ~umask(022) = 600. Permissions ARE preserved on default umask. But
        if the user's umask is 000 (rare, containerized), the dest would be
        600 — still fine. If umask is 077, also fine. So in practice OK, but
        the explicit chmod is missing for defense-in-depth.
    (b) Line 167: `cp -r db .next/standalone/db 2>/dev/null || true`.
        cp -r on Linux preserves mode bits from source. So db/custom.db
        keeps 600, db dir keeps 700. ✓. But `|| true` masks any failure
        (e.g., disk full) — the standalone dir would then lack a db, and
        systemd would fail to start with a confusing "database not found"
        error.
    (c) Line 162 (standalone branch, `[ -f server.js ]`): `cp .env .env`
        is a NO-OP that ERRORS on GNU coreutils:
          `cp: '.env' and '.env' are the same file` (exit 1)
        With `set -e` (line 15), this TERMINATES THE SCRIPT at line 162
        before reaching steps 8, 9, 10. Confirmed via test:
          $ cp _test_env _test_env → exit=1
        This is a CRITICAL BUG — see defect D1 below.
    (d) Line 131: `rm -f db/custom.db-journal db/custom.db-wal db/custom.db-shm`
        removes SQLite WAL/journal files. On first install (service not yet
        running), this is safe. On RE-RUN (service may be active from prior
        install), deleting WAL files mid-flight can CORRUPT THE DATABASE.
        No `systemctl stop personal-site` before this. Idempotency hazard.

  nginx-ehsanmorad.conf:14-29 server block for ehsanmorad.ir proxies to
  http://localhost:3000 with proper WebSocket upgrade headers (lines 26-27).
  Three identical server blocks for the three domains (lines 15-29, 32-46,
  49-63).

  Caveats:
    (a) Line 223: `cp ... 2>/dev/null || true`. If the source file
        `nginx-ehsanmorad.conf` is missing (e.g., script run from wrong dir,
        or file deleted), cp fails silently. The symlink at line 224 then
        points to a non-existent file. `nginx -t` at line 226 would FAIL
        (broken symlink), but `&&` short-circuits so `systemctl reload`
        doesn't run. HOWEVER, the script does NOT exit — `nginx -t 2>&1 &&
        systemctl reload nginx` is a single command; if `nginx -t` fails,
        only the reload is skipped. Under `set -e`, the failed `nginx -t`
        WOULD exit the script. Actually: `cmd1 && cmd2` under set -e: if
        cmd1 fails, the && expression's exit code is cmd1's, and set -e
        triggers. So the script exits at line 226 if nginx config test
        fails. But line 227 "✅ Nginx تنظیم شد" never runs in that case.
        So this is OK — except the user sees no clear error, just the
        script stops mid-step-9.
    (b) Line 224: `ln -sf` is idempotent. ✓
    (c) Line 225: removes the default site. Good — frees port 80 for our
        server_name. But if the user had a different default site they
        wanted to keep, it's gone. No backup.
    (d) nginx-ehsanmorad.conf has NO `client_max_body_size` directive —
        default is 1MB. Contact form file uploads (if any) over 1MB would
        fail with 413 Request Entity Too Large. Not in audit scope but
        noted.
    (e) nginx-ehsanmorad.conf has NO rate limiting, NO gzip, NO caching
        headers. Minimal config. Not a bug, just minimal.
    (f) The script does NOT reload-or-restart nginx if nginx -t fails. A
        failed reload leaves nginx serving the OLD config. Acceptable.

Q8. Does it set up HTTPS with certbot?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Verdict: YES — with caveats.

  Evidence:
    install.sh:243  DOMAIN_FOUND=""
    install.sh:244  for domain in ehsanmorad.ir ehsan-morad.ir ehsanmorad.id.ir; do
    install.sh:245    if host "$domain" &>/dev/null; then
    install.sh:246      DOMAIN_FOUND="$domain"
    install.sh:247      break
    install.sh:248    fi
    install.sh:249  done
    install.sh:251  if [ -n "$DOMAIN_FOUND" ]; then
    install.sh:254    certbot --nginx -d "$DOMAIN_FOUND" -d "www.$DOMAIN_FOUND"
                       --non-interactive --agree-tos
                       --register-unsafely-without-email 2>&1 | tail -5
    install.sh:255    if certbot ... ; then
                       echo "  ✅ HTTPS فعال شد"; SITE_URL="https://$DOMAIN_FOUND"
    install.sh:257    else ... "⚠ certbot ناموفق بود"; SITE_URL="http://$DOMAIN_FOUND"
    install.sh:262  else  (no domain) SITE_URL="http://31.70.76.10:3000"

  Caveats:
    (a) Line 244: hardcoded list of 3 domains. If the user has a different
        domain, it's never detected. No interactive prompt, no env var
        override, no CLI arg. The script cannot be used for any domain
        not in this hardcoded list.
    (b) Line 245: `host "$domain"` requires `bind-utils`/`dnsutils`. Not
        installed by step 3 (line 68). On most Debian/Ubuntu `host` is
        present via `bind9-host`/`dnsutils` package as a dependency of
        other tools, but not guaranteed. If `host` is missing, the for-loop
        silently fails (each iteration: command not found → non-zero →
        `if` branch skipped), DOMAIN_FOUND stays empty, and HTTPS is
        skipped even if the domain actually resolves.
    (c) Line 247: `break` on FIRST matching domain. If multiple domains
        in the list resolve to this server, only the first gets a cert.
        The nginx config (nginx-ehsanmorad.conf) has server blocks for
        all three, so the others would serve over HTTP only.
    (d) Line 254: `--register-unsafely-without-email` means NO expiry
        notifications. Let's Encrypt certs expire in 90 days; without
        email, the only warning is in `certbot renew --dry-run` output
        (which the script doesn't configure). The systemd timer for
        auto-renewal IS installed by the certbot package, but no
        verification here.
    (e) Line 254: no `--redirect` flag. certbot will install the cert
        but won't automatically redirect HTTP → HTTPS. Users hitting
        http://domain will stay on HTTP. The nginx config (lines 15-29)
        only has `listen 80` server blocks — no `listen 443`. After
        certbot --nginx runs, it modifies the config to add 443 + SSL
        directives, but without --redirect the port-80 block stays
        serving HTTP. Minor security gap.
    (f) Line 254: NOT idempotent. Re-running the script re-runs certbot
        for the same domain. Let's Encrypt rate limit is 5 duplicate
        certs per week per domain. After 5 re-runs within 7 days,
        certbot fails with rate limit. The script catches this (line
        257 else branch) and falls back to http://, but the user is
        not warned that they've hit a rate limit.
    (g) Line 254: `2>&1 | tail -5` masks certbot's exit code (pipefail
        not set). The `if certbot ...; then` at line 254 checks the
        exit code of `tail`, not certbot. tail always exits 0. So the
        `if` branch ALWAYS succeeds, even if certbot failed. The
        else branch (line 257) is DEAD CODE. **BUG**.

  Verdict: PARTIAL — hardcoded IP, inconsistent placeholders, plaintext password.

  Evidence:
    install.sh:281  echo "    $SITE_URL"
    install.sh:284  echo "    $SITE_URL/user-login"
    install.sh:285  echo "    username: admin"
    install.sh:286  echo "    password: admin123"

    install.sh:303  echo "    Telegram: https://$DOMAIN_FOUND/api/telegram/webhook?secret=$TG_SECRET"
    install.sh:264  SITE_URL="http://31.70.76.10:3000"  (no-domain fallback)
    install.sh:305  echo "    Bale:     http://YOUR_IP:3000/api/bale/webhook?secret=$BALE_SECRET"
    install.sh:306  echo "    Telegram: http://YOUR_IP:3000/api/telegram/webhook?secret=$TG_SECRET"

  Caveats:
    (a) Line 264: hardcoded IP `31.70.76.10`. If the server's actual public
        IP differs (e.g., user runs this on a different server), the printed
        URL is WRONG. Should auto-detect via `curl -s ifconfig.me` or
        `hostname -I | awk '{print $1}'` or `ip route get 1.1.1.1`.
    (b) Lines 305-306: literal placeholder `YOUR_IP` instead of the actual
        IP. Inconsistent with line 264 which uses a real (if hardcoded) IP.
        User must manually substitute. Should be `http://$(curl -s
        ifconfig.me):3000/api/...` or reuse the same detection as (a).
    (c) Lines 285-286: prints `username: admin` / `password: admin123` to
        stdout. If the user redirects output to a log file or runs the
        script via a CI/CD pipeline, the default credentials are written
        to disk in plaintext. Minor security concern — admin password is
        weak AND printed. The warning at line 287 tells user to change it,
        but the plaintext leak is still there.
    (d) Line 281: if HTTPS failed (Q8 caveat g — dead else branch),
        SITE_URL is "https://..." even though HTTPS isn't actually set up.
        User clicks the URL, gets a cert error.
    (e) Line 284: `$SITE_URL/user-login` — correct path. Verified against
        src/app/user-login/page.tsx (exists, not audited here).
    (f) Webhook URLs (lines 302-303, 305-306) include the secret in the
        query string. This is the intended pattern (the webhook route
        verifies `?secret=` against the env var), but printing the secret
        to stdout is the same plaintext-leak concern as (c).

Q11. Does it work idempotently?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Verdict: NO — multiple idempotency failures.

  Per-step analysis:
    Swap (29-39):    ✓ checks `swapon --show | grep -q swap` first
    Node.js (46-59): ✓ checks `command -v node` and version >= 20
    Nginx (66-75):   ✓ checks `command -v nginx`
    Firewall (82-85):✓ `ufw allow` and `ufw --force enable` are idempotent
    .env (105-117):  ✗ MAJOR — regenerated EVERY run:
        - Line 93:  SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)        → NEW secret each run
        - Line 98:  BALE_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16)    → NEW secret each run
        - Line 99:  TG_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16)      → NEW secret each run
        - Line 105: cat > .env << EOF                      → OVERWRITES .env
        Effect: every re-run invalidates ALL existing admin sessions (users
        logged in get bounced) AND breaks any configured Bale/Telegram
        webhooks (the secret stored in the bot config no longer matches
        the new BALE_WEBHOOK_SECRET/TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env).
        ReCAPTCHA values ARE preserved (lines 102-103), so that's the only
        idempotent part of .env regeneration.
    DB chmod (127-131): ✓ touch + chmod are idempotent
    DB WAL rm (131):    ✗ `rm -f` on journal/wal/shm. If service is running
        (re-run scenario), this can corrupt the DB. No `systemctl stop` first.
    prisma db push (134-140): ✓ idempotent (only runs if 0 tables)
    Seeding (143-153):  ✓ idempotent (gated on ADMIN_EXISTS check)
    Standalone prep (160-173): ✗ CRITICAL — line 162 `cp .env .env` errors
        on GNU coreutils (verified: exit 1). Under `set -e`, the script
        EXITS at line 162 in standalone mode (when server.js exists).
        Steps 8, 9, 10 NEVER RUN. Re-running also hits this. (Defect D1)
    systemd (180-216): ✓ idempotent (useradd checks existence, service file
        is overwritten with `cat >`, daemon-reload + restart are idempotent)
    Nginx (223-227): ✓ idempotent (cp + ln -sf)
    certbot (251-261): ✗ NOT idempotent — re-issues cert every run. Let's
        Encrypt rate limit: 5 duplicate certs per 7 days. After 5 re-runs
        in a week, certbot fails. Should check `certbot certificates |
        grep "Domains:"` first.
    Final output: ✓ idempotent (just echoes)

  Top idempotency bugs:
    ID1 (line 93, 98, 99, 105): SESSION_SECRET + webhook secrets regenerated
         on every run → invalidates sessions + breaks webhooks.
    ID2 (line 131): WAL files removed mid-flight if service is running.
    ID3 (line 162): cp .env .env exits 1 under set -e → script aborts in
         standalone mode before reaching steps 8/9/10.
    ID4 (line 254): certbot re-issues cert every run → rate-limit risk.

Q12. Does it handle missing domain?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Verdict: PARTIAL — has fallback but no real detection or user input.

  Evidence:
    install.sh:243-249  probes 3 hardcoded domains via `host` DNS lookup
    install.sh:251      if [ -n "$DOMAIN_FOUND" ]; then HTTPS path
    install.sh:262      else: "⚠ دامنه‌ای DNS ست نشده. فعلاً HTTP."
    install.sh:264      SITE_URL="http://31.70.76.10:3000"  ← hardcoded IP
    install.sh:301-307  webhook URLs: use $DOMAIN_FOUND or "YOUR_IP" placeholder

  Caveats:
    (a) Line 244: ONLY 3 hardcoded domains checked. User cannot supply a
        custom domain via CLI arg, env var, or interactive prompt. If the
        user owns "example.com" and points it at this server, install.sh
        will report "no domain found" and skip HTTPS.
    (b) Line 264: fallback IP `31.70.76.10` is hardcoded. Not detected
        from the server's actual public IP. Wrong on any other server.
        Should be: `PUBLIC_IP=$(curl -s --max-time 5 ifconfig.me || echo
        "YOUR_SERVER_IP")` or similar.
    (c) Lines 305-306: webhook URLs use literal `YOUR_IP` placeholder when
        no domain — inconsistent with line 264 which has a real IP. User
        has to manually substitute, but the SITE_URL line above has a
        concrete IP. Confusing.
    (d) Line 262-264: when no domain is found, the script still proceeds
        to install everything (systemd, nginx) and reports success. The
        nginx config (nginx-ehsanmorad.conf) has server_name for the 3
        hardcoded domains. If user accesses by IP, nginx serves the first
        server block (default when no default_server is set, since line
        225 removed /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default). The proxy works
        but server_name mismatch can cause redirects to wrong domain.
    (e) No `set -e` exit on missing domain — script continues. Good (the
        user can still access via IP) but the messaging is incomplete:
        user is told "HTTP only" but not "to enable HTTPS, point your
        domain's A record at <server IP> and re-run install.sh".
    (f) certbot is correctly SKIPPED when no domain (line 251 if). ✓

DEFECTS / OBSERVATIONS (file:line) — NOT FIXED per task scope
================================================================================

  CRITICAL:
  D1  install.sh:162 — `cp .env .env` is a no-op that ERRORS on GNU coreutils
      ("cp: '.env' and '.env' are the same file", exit 1). Under `set -e`
      (line 15), the script TERMINATES HERE in standalone mode (when server.js
      exists). Steps 8 (systemd), 9 (nginx), 10 (HTTPS) NEVER RUN. Verified
      via test: `cp _test_env _test_env` → exit 1.
  D2  install.sh:254 — `certbot ... 2>&1 | tail -5` followed by `if certbot
      ...; then`. The `if` checks the exit code of `tail` (always 0), NOT
      certbot. The else branch (line 257) is DEAD CODE — HTTPS failures
      report as success. Should use `set -o pipefail` or capture certbot's
      exit separately.
  D3  install.sh:93, 98, 99 — openssl is NOT installed by step 3 (line 68)
      and NOT presence-checked. If openssl is missing, SESSION_SECRET,
      BALE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET all become empty strings.
      Script prints "✅ SESSION_SECRET قوی تولید شد" anyway. Silent security
      failure.

  HIGH:
  D4  install.sh:105 — .env OVERWRITTEN on every run via `cat > .env << EOF`.
      SESSION_SECRET (L93), BALE_SECRET (L98), TG_SECRET (L99) regenerated
      each run. Invalidates admin sessions and breaks configured webhooks.
      ReCAPTCHA values (L102-103) are preserved. Should detect existing
      .env and skip regeneration, or selectively preserve secrets.
  D5  install.sh:131 — `rm -f db/custom.db-journal db/custom.db-wal
      db/custom.db-shm` runs unconditionally. On re-run with service active
      (started by prior install), deleting WAL files mid-flight can corrupt
      the SQLite database. No `systemctl stop personal-site` before this.
  D6  install.sh:254 — certbot re-issues cert on EVERY run. Let's Encrypt
      rate limit: 5 duplicate certs per 7 days per domain. After 5 re-runs,
      certbot fails. Should check `certbot certificates` for existing cert
      first.
  D7  install.sh:137 — hardcoded path `node_modules/prisma/build/index.js`.
      No existence check. If prisma isn't installed at that path (e.g.,
      standalone bundle doesn't ship node_modules/prisma), command fails.
      Piped to `tail -3` (no pipefail), so failure may be masked — DB
      tables never created, seeding fails downstream.

  MEDIUM:
  D8  install.sh:264 — fallback IP `31.70.76.10` is hardcoded. On any other
      server, printed URL is wrong. Should auto-detect via
      `curl -s ifconfig.me` or `hostname -I`.
  D9  install.sh:285-286 — prints `username: admin` / `password: admin123`
      to stdout. Plaintext default credentials in logs. Combined with the
      warning at L287 (change password), the leak is mitigated but not
      eliminated.
  D10 install.sh:244 — only 3 hardcoded domains checked. No CLI arg, env
      var, or interactive prompt for custom domain. Script cannot be used
      for any domain not in {ehsanmorad.ir, ehsan-morad.ir, ehsanmorad.id.ir}.
  D11 install.sh:245 — `host` command requires dnsutils/bind-utils, NOT
      installed by step 3 (line 68). If `host` is missing, all domain
      probes silently fail → HTTPS skipped even if domain resolves.
  D12 install.sh:254 — no `--redirect` flag. certbot installs cert but
      doesn't auto-redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Port-80 server block in
      nginx-ehsanmorad.conf keeps serving HTTP.
  D13 install.sh:254 — `--register-unsafely-without-email`. No expiry
      notifications. Certs expire in 90 days; only `certbot renew` (system
      timer) saves them. No verification the timer is active.
  D14 install.sh:135 — prisma db push only runs when TOTAL table count is
      0. If schema gains a new model and DB already has some tables, the
      new model's table is NEVER created. Condition should be "if
      AccessUser table missing".
  D15 install.sh:166 — in `.next/standalone` branch, `cp .env
      .next/standalone/.env` does NOT re-run `chmod 600`. Relies on umask
      preserving 600. Defense-in-depth gap; chmod should be explicit.
  D16 install.sh:223 — `cp nginx-ehsanmorad.conf ... 2>/dev/null || true`.
      If the source file is missing, cp fails silently. The symlink at
      line 224 points to a non-existent file. `nginx -t` (line 226) then
      fails, and under `set -e` the script exits — but with no clear error
      message (the user sees only "nginx: configuration file test failed"
      if it reaches nginx -t at all).

  LOW:
  D17 install.sh:15 — `set -e` is set but many commands use `|| true` or
      `2>/dev/null`, masking real failures. Inconsistent error handling.
  D18 install.sh:230 — `sleep 5` before curl check. If Next.js standalone
      takes longer than 5s to boot (cold cache, slow disk), the curl check
      fails with "⚠ چک کن" even though the service will be ready shortly.
      Should retry with backoff.
  D19 install.sh:195 — `ExecStart=$(which node) server.js`. `which node`
      evaluated at script-run time. If node is later moved/updated, the
      service file has a stale path. Should hardcode `/usr/bin/node` or
      use `ExecStart=node` (relies on systemd's PATH, which is minimal).
  D20 install.sh:8 (package.json:8) — inconsistency: package.json "start"
      uses `bun .next/standalone/server.js`, but install.sh:195 systemd
      ExecStart uses `node server.js`. If bun-specific features are used
      in server.js, node won't run it. Not verified here.
  D21 install.sh:7-13 — comment claims "npm install نمی‌خواد (همه‌چیز
      pre-built هست)" but the script REQUIRES `node_modules/prisma/build/
      index.js` to exist (line 137) AND `node_modules/bcryptjs` to exist
      (seed_access_users.py:30, invoked at install.sh:149). The "pre-built
      standalone" claim is inconsistent with these node_modules deps.
  D22 install.sh:305-306 — webhook URLs use literal `YOUR_IP` placeholder
      when no domain, but SITE_URL at line 264 has a real (if hardcoded)
      IP. Inconsistent — user must substitute manually for webhooks but
      not for SITE_URL.
  D23 install.sh:7-13 (comment block) — claims "systemd با user غیر root"
      and "HTTPS setup با certbot (اگه دامنه ست شده)". Both true. But the
      comment also says "فایروال + Nginx" — ufw is configured but ONLY
      ports 22/80/443 (lines 82-84). If the user needs other ports (e.g.,
      for SSH on a non-standard port), ufw blocks them. Not a bug, just
      a constraint.
  D24 install.sh:29-39 — swap step creates a 2GB swapfile at /swapfile.
      If the server already has swap (just under a different name or as a
      swap partition), the `swapon --show | grep -q swap` check at line 30
      catches it and skips. ✓. But if /swapfile already exists from a
      prior run AND swap is active, the check passes (skips). If
      /swapfile exists but isn't active, fallocate at line 31 fails (file
      exists), then chmod/mkswap/swapon would re-use the existing file.
      Mostly OK but `fallocate` doesn't have `|| dd` fallback path
      triggered by file-exists, only by fallocate failure.
  D25 install.sh:51, 56 — `curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x
      | bash -`. Piping curl to bash is a security concern (MITM can inject
      arbitrary commands). Standard practice but worth noting. Also: Node
      22 LTS — at time of audit this is current; will need updating when
      Node 22 EOLs.
  D26 install.sh:46-59 — Node.js version check: `NODE_VER=$(node -v | sed
      's/v//' | cut -d. -f1)` then `[ "$NODE_VER" -ge 20 ]`. If node -v
      returns something unexpected (e.g., "v22.0.0-pre" or a non-numeric
      tag), `cut -d. -f1` may return "22-pre" and `[ "22-pre" -ge 20 ]`
      errors with "integer expression expected". Edge case.
  D27 install.sh:73 — `apt install -y sqlite3 python3 ufw certbot
      python3-certbot-nginx 2>/dev/null || true`. The `2>/dev/null || true`
      masks apt failures (e.g., apt lock held by another process). If apt
      fails, sqlite3/python3 may be missing, and downstream steps (line
      134 sqlite3 query, line 146-149 python3 seeds) fail with confusing
      errors.
