  - The AccessUserManager component exposes the following admin
    actions on a user row (per PUT body fields in
    admin/users/[id]/route.ts:37-69):
      - displayName, role, password, allowedHourStart/End,
        allowedDays, permissions, expiresAt, active, deactivatedReason.
    There is NO `forceLogout` / `revokeSessions` field, no UI
    button, and no API endpoint for it.
  - The DELETE handler (admin/users/[id]/route.ts:100-126) removes
    the AccessUser row entirely (cascade-deleting AccessLog rows).
    This effectively "logs out" the deleted user — BUT:
      * verifySessionToken (access-auth.ts:78-96) does NOT consult
        the DB, so the cookie is still cryptographically valid.
        The eviction only happens because checkAdminAuth
        (admin-auth.ts:23) calls findUnique and gets null.
      * This is a NUCLEAR option: you delete the user entirely,
        losing their audit history (AccessLog rows cascade-delete
        per schema.prisma:423). Not a targeted session revocation.
  - The PUT active=false handler (admin/users/[id]/route.ts:60-65)
    similarly "logs out" the user (DB-side active=false → checkAdminAuth
    rejects) but the cookie is still cryptographically valid, and:
      * ALL of the user's sessions are evicted simultaneously
        (no per-device granularity), and
      * The user can be re-activated, at which point any captured
        cookie becomes valid again (because verifySessionToken
        doesn't consult the DB and checkAdminAuth only checks
        active + role).
  - There is NO Session table (schema.prisma has none) and NO
    per-session identifier (no jti in token — see Q9). Therefore
    there is NO mechanism to revoke a SPECIFIC session — e.g.,
    "log out the admin's phone but keep the admin's laptop logged in"
    is impossible in the current design.
  - Admin's own password change (admin/security/route.ts:56-100)
    does NOT even log out OTHER admins or OTHER sessions of the
    SAME admin (see Q2).

PoC (force-logout impossible):
  # Scenario: admin's cookie was stolen. Admin wants to evict the
  # attacker WITHOUT deleting their own account.
  #
  # Options in current codebase:
  #   (a) Change own password — DOES NOT evict attacker (see Q2/Q7).
  #   (b) Deactivate own account — evicts attacker AND admin (Q3),
  #       and re-activating later re-admits the attacker's captured
  #       cookie.
  #   (c) Delete own account — evicts attacker AND admin AND loses
  #       all audit history. Not viable.
  #
  # There is NO option (d): "revoke this specific session" — the
  # data model doesn't support it.

Cross-reference: V17.3-SEC-02 Q14/F-2 (no tokenVersion column →
  no force-logout possible), V17.4-SEC-04 #7 (PARTIAL rating on
  deactivation/role-change — same defect class).

================================================================
SUMMARY TABLE
================================================================
Q#  | Status    | Severity | Brief
----+-----------+----------+--------------------------------------------------
1   | FAIL      | HIGH     | Logout only deletes client cookie. No server-side
    |           |          | revocation, no tokenVersion bump, no denylist.
    |           |          | Captured cookies still verify for 24h.
2   | FAIL      | CRITICAL | Password change writes ONLY passwordHash. No
    |           |          | invalidation. HMAC payload doesn't bind password.
3   | PARTIAL   | MED      | Deactivation IS effective at API layer (DB re-read
    |           |          | on every request rejects !active). But cookie
    |           |          | still passes middleware format-check; no hard
    |           |          | eviction; no targeted session kill.
4   | PARTIAL   | MED      | Role change IS effective at API layer (DB re-read).
    |           |          | But cookie stays cryptographically valid; no
    |           |          | forced re-auth; no per-session revocation.
5   | FAIL      | HIGH     | No `tokenVersion` column on AccessUser. Confirmed
    |           |          | by grep (zero source matches).
6   | FAIL      | HIGH     | No `passwordChangedAt` column on AccessUser.
    |           |          | Confirmed by grep (zero source matches). Token
    |           |          | also has no `iat` to compare against.
7   | FAIL      | CRITICAL | Stolen cookie remains 100% valid for up to 24h
    |           |          | after victim changes password. Password rotation
    |           |          | as breach-response is INEFFECTIVE.
8   | FAIL      | HIGH     | Token embeds NO IP, NO UA, NO fingerprint.
    |           |          | IP/UA captured only for forensic AccessLog rows.
    |           |          | Stolen cookie usable from any IP / UA.
9   | FAIL      | MED      | No rotation primitives. Cookie issued once at
    |           |          | login, never re-issued. No jti, no iat, no
    |           |          | sliding expiration, no rotation on privilege
    |           |          | change or sensitive action.
10  | FAIL      | HIGH     | No force-logout endpoint. No session table.
    |           |          | No per-session identifier. Admin can only
    |           |          | delete or deactivate the entire user (evicts
    |           |          | ALL sessions, loses audit history on delete).

================================================================
ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONS (not in the 10 questions but relevant)
================================================================

----- F-A. verifySessionToken is fully stateless  [CRITICAL, root cause] -----
Location: src/lib/access-auth.ts:78-96
Analysis:
  - The function decodes base64, splits on ".", parses expiresAt, and
    verifies the HMAC. It returns { userId, expiresAt } on success.
  - It NEVER touches the database. It does NOT verify the user still
    exists, is still active, has the same role, or has not had their
    password changed.
  - This single design choice is the ROOT CAUSE of Q1, Q2, Q5, Q6,
    Q7, and Q10. All DB-backed checks (active, role, existence)
    happen in the per-route guards (checkAdminAuth / checkAdminSession
    / checkAccess / verify route's inline check). Those guards:
      * DO catch deactivation (Q3) and role change (Q4) at the API
        layer — hence the PARTIAL ratings.
      * DO NOT catch password change (Q2) — because passwordHash is
        not part of the HMAC and is not consulted by the guard.
      * DO NOT provide targeted session revocation (Q10) — because
        there is no per-session identifier.
  - Fixing this would require either:
      (a) Adding a `tokenVersion Int @default(0)` to AccessUser and
          embedding it in the HMAC payload, then loading the user
          row inside verifySessionToken (or its caller) and
          rejecting when token.v !== user.tokenVersion. Bump
          tokenVersion on logout / password change / deactivation /
          role change.
      (b) OR introducing a Session table (sessionId, userId, ip,
          userAgent, createdAt, expiresAt, revokedAt) and consulting
          it on every request.

----- F-B. Middleware gate is FORMAT-ONLY  [HIGH, defense-in-depth gap] -----
Location: src/middleware.ts:70-93
Analysis:
  - hasValidSession() decodes the cookie, checks parts.length === 3,
    checks expiry, and verifies userId.length > 0.
  - It does NOT (and per the code comment CANNOT) verify the HMAC
    because SESSION_SECRET is not available in the Edge runtime.
  - A forged cookie of the form `base64("anystring.9999999999.anyhex")`
    passes the middleware gate at /user-dashboard and /api/admin/*
    (middleware.ts:181-193). The API handler's checkAdminAuth then
    rejects it (because the HMAC fails verification). So the
    end-to-end security property holds, but the middleware layer
    is effectively a no-op for security beyond expiry.
  - This is the same defect flagged in prior audit V17.3-SEC-02 Q3/F-1
    (middleware session validation is FORMAT-ONLY). Still NOT fixed.
  - Implication for THIS audit: even when deactivation (Q3) /
    role-change (Q4) have been applied DB-side, the middleware
    doesn't redirect the affected user away from /user-dashboard.
    The user lands on the page and the client must handle the
    degraded /api/user/verify response. No hard redirect.

----- F-C. logout endpoint doesn't write AccessLog  [LOW, audit-trail gap] -----
Location: src/app/api/user/logout/route.ts:7-11
Analysis:
  - The AccessLog schema explicitly lists "logout" as a valid action
    value (schema.prisma:424), and AccessUserManager.tsx:575 styles
    it. But the logout endpoint never calls logAccess. So logout
    events are NOT recorded in the audit trail.
  - Contrast with login/route.ts:103 which DOES log "login_success".
  - Forensic impact: an attacker who steals a cookie and uses it
    leaves NO logout trail (because they don't call /api/user/logout
    — they just stop using it). But a legitimate user who clicks
    "Logout" ALSO leaves no trail. Inconsistent audit trail.

----- F-D. logout endpoint doesn't pass `request`  [LOW] -----
Location: src/app/api/user/logout/route.ts:7
Analysis:
  - `export async function POST()` takes no arguments. The handler
    cannot read request headers, so it cannot log IP/UA even if
    it wanted to (cf. F-C). Next.js will pass `request` if declared
    in the signature; the current signature prevents any future
    audit-logging addition without a signature change.

----- F-E. SESSION_SECRET gating is good but single-secret  [LOW, informational] -----
Location: src/lib/access-auth.ts:20-43
Analysis:
  - getSecret() rejects placeholder values and short secrets (<32 chars).
    Good.
  - But there's a single global SESSION_SECRET. Rotating the secret
    (e.g., after a suspected leak) invalidates ALL sessions of ALL
    users simultaneously (because the HMAC key changes). That's a
    blunt instrument: it's the only existing way to force a global
    logout today, but it's all-or-nothing. Combined with Q10 (no
    targeted force-logout), this means the only "force-logout" knob
    an admin has today is rotating SESSION_SECRET — which is a
    full-system restart of authentication.
  - Also: there's no key-id in the token, so a key rotation cannot
    be done "gracefully" (accepting tokens signed by either the old
    or new key for a transition window). All outstanding tokens
    die instantly.

----- F-F. cookie `secure` flag tied to NODE_ENV  [LOW, deployment risk] -----
Location: src/app/api/user/login/route.ts:118
Analysis:
  - `secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"`. In any non-
    production deployment (staging, preview, dev), the cookie is
    sent over plain HTTP — capturable on the wire. If a staging
    instance is accidentally exposed to the internet without TLS,
    cookies are leaked. Prior audit V17.3-SEC-02 Q8 flagged
    HSTS-behind-proxy issues; this compounds.

================================================================
FIX-PRIORITY ORDER (advisory only — DO NOT APPLY per task instructions)
================================================================
1. Q5 + Q6 + Q2 + Q7 + Q1 + Q10 (single root cause) — Add
   `tokenVersion Int @default(0)` AND `passwordChangedAt DateTime?`
   to AccessUser (schema.prisma:380-415). Embed `tokenVersion` and
   `iat` in the session token HMAC payload (access-auth.ts:67-72).
   In verifySessionToken (or its caller — F-A), load the user row
   and reject when token.v !== user.tokenVersion OR
   token.iat < user.passwordChangedAt. Bump tokenVersion on:
     - logout (logout/route.ts:7-11 — currently a no-op DB-side)
     - password change (admin/security/route.ts:88-91)
     - deactivation (admin/users/[id]/route.ts:60-65)
     - role change (admin/users/[id]/route.ts:48)
     - DELETE user (admin/users/[id]/route.ts:123)
   Add an admin "Force logout" button in AccessUserManager.tsx
   that bumps tokenVersion for the target user. [CRITICAL]
2. Q8 — Optionally embed a UA-fingerprint (or rotate-per-IP) into
   the token HMAC. At minimum, store IP/UA in a new Session table
   at login and compare on every request (reject on mismatch with
   a re-auth requirement). Be aware that X-Forwarded-For is
   spoofable (prior audit V17.3-SEC-02 Q11/F-9 still open). [HIGH]
3. Q9 — Add `iat` to the token; add a sliding-refresh (re-issue
   token with extended expiresAt on every N-th request, with a
   hard cap of 24h since first-issue). Add `jti` for per-session
   identification (needed for Q10 targeted revocation). [MED]
4. F-A — Make verifySessionToken stateful (load user row). This
   is the architectural change that makes #1 above actually work. [CRITICAL]
5. F-B — Move session validation to a runtime that can access
   SESSION_SECRET, OR have middleware delegate to an API-layer
   check on every protected route (current pattern already does
   this via checkAdminAuth — so F-B is informational). [LOW]
6. F-C — Call logAccess(userId, "logout", ip, ua) in
   logout/route.ts:7-11 (requires changing the signature to
   accept `request: NextRequest`). [LOW]
7. F-D — Same as F-C: signature change to accept request. [LOW]
8. F-E — Add a key-id to the token header for graceful SESSION_SECRET
   rotation. [LOW]
9. F-F — Consider `secure: true` always (rely on HTTPS termination
   at the edge even in dev — prior audit V17.3-SEC-02 Q8 HSTS issue
   compounds here). [LOW]

Final verdict:
  Of the 10 audit questions:
    - 7 FAIL (Q1, Q2, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q10)
    - 2 PARTIAL (Q3, Q4 — effective at API layer only, cookie
      remains cryptographically valid)
    - 1 FAIL (Q9 — no rotation primitives)
  Severity distribution:
    - CRITICAL: Q2, Q7 (2)
    - HIGH:     Q1, Q5, Q6, Q8, Q10 (5)
    - MED:      Q3, Q4, Q9 (3)
    - LOW:      F-C, F-D, F-E, F-F (4)
  Root cause: verifySessionToken (access-auth.ts:78-96) is fully
  stateless and the token payload (access-auth.ts:67-72) binds
  NOTHING except userId + expiresAt. There is no tokenVersion,
  no passwordChangedAt, no iat, no jti, no IP, no UA. The DB-backed
  per-route guards compensate for deactivation and role-change
  (Q3, Q4 PARTIAL) but cannot compensate for password change (Q2),
  stolen-cookie-after-rotation (Q7), targeted session revocation
  (Q10), or any form of session rotation (Q9).

----- 1. loadItems  [PARTIAL — silent failure, no error path] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:13-21

Code:
  13:  const fa = lang === "fa";  const loadItems = async () => {
  14:    setLoading(true);
  15:    try {
  16:      const res = await fetch(`/api/admin/nav`, { credentials: "include" });
  17:      const data = await res.json();
  18:      if (data.ok) setItems(data.items || []);
  19:    } catch {}
  20:    setLoading(false);
  21:  };

Findings:
  - (F1-a) Line 13 — `const fa = lang === "fa";  const loadItems = ...`
    puts two statements on one line (poor readability; ESLint
    semi-style inconsistency). Cosmetic only.
  - (F1-b) Line 16 — credentials: "include" ✓ present on GET.
  - (F1-c) Line 17 — `await res.json()` is called WITHOUT first
    checking `res.ok` or `res.status`. If the server returns a 401
    JSON `{ ok:false, error:"unauthorized" }`, line 18's `if (data.ok)`
    silently falls through and `items` remains `[]`. The user sees
    an empty list with no explanation. The 401 also produces no
    banner, no redirect to /login, nothing.
  - (F1-d) Line 17 — if the response body is not valid JSON (e.g.,
    502 HTML error page from a reverse proxy), `res.json()` throws
    → caught by line 19's empty `catch {}` → swallowed silently.
    `items` stays `[]`, `loading` flips to false, user has no idea
    why the list is empty.
  - (F1-e) Line 19 — `catch {}` with NO error state set. Same
    anti-pattern flagged in V17.4-SEC-12 elsewhere (silent failure
    → user blames self, support has no diagnostic).
  - (F1-f) Line 20 — `setLoading(false)` runs unconditionally after
    try/catch. Good (no finally needed), but means loading flag is
    set false even on error — so the "loading..." placeholder
    disappears and reveals an empty list, reinforcing the illusion
    of "no items" rather than "load failed".
  - (F1-g) No AbortController / timeout on the GET fetch. If the
    request hangs (network drop, server stall), `loading` stays
    `true` forever and the entire panel is stuck on the
    "loading..." <p> at line 85. Consistent with V17.4-SEC-12 Q8
    (no fetch timeouts anywhere in the app).
  - (F1-h) Line 28: `useEffect(() => { loadItems(); }, []);` —
    missing `loadItems` in deps. ESLint react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
    would warn. Currently harmless because loadItems only references
    state setters (stable identity), but if loadItems is ever
    refactored to capture `items` or `editing`, this becomes a
    stale-closure bug.
  - (F1-i) No retry mechanism. A single transient network blip
    leaves the panel in empty state until the user manually
    refreshes the page.

----- 2. save (create+update)  [FAIL — no response check, no error
                                          path, no per-action loading] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:30-44

Code:
  30:  const save = async (item: any) => {
  31:    const isNew = !item.id;
  32:    const action = isNew ? "create" : "update";
  33:    const payload: any = { action };
  34:    if (!isNew) payload.id = item.id;
  35:    payload.data = { ...item };
  36:    delete payload.data.id; delete payload.data.createdAt; delete payload.data.updatedAt;
  37:    await fetch("/api/admin/nav", {
  38:      method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  39:        credentials: "include",
  40:      body: JSON.stringify(payload),
  41:    });
  42:    setEditing(null);
  43:    loadItems();
  44:  };

Findings:
  - (F2-a) Lines 37-41 — `await fetch(...)` return value is
    COMPLETELY IGNORED. No `res.ok` check, no `await res.json()`.
    If the server returns 401 (session expired), 400 (missing_id /
    invalid_body), or 500 (server_error — route.ts:68), the client
    still:
       * closes the editor (line 42 — `setEditing(null)`),
       * reloads the list (line 43 — `loadItems()`),
    creating the ILLUSION that the save succeeded. The user walks
    away thinking the menu was updated. THE SAVE ACTUALLY FAILED
    SILENTLY. This is the worst UX bug in the file.
  - (F2-b) Lines 30-44 — NO try/catch wrapping the fetch. If the
    network drops mid-POST, `await fetch` throws TypeError
    ("Failed to fetch"). The promise rejection propagates up to
    the onClick handler in line 112 (the save button). React
    logs "Unhandled promise rejection" to console but shows
    nothing to the user — the editor doesn't close, the list
    doesn't refresh, the user clicks "save" again and again with
    no feedback. Also no global window.onerror / promise rejection
    handler visible in this file.
  - (F2-c) Line 31 — `const isNew = !item.id;` — relies on
    falsy `item.id`. If a future change ever passes `id: ""` or
    `id: 0` (currently cuid strings, so safe), the check breaks
    silently. Should be `item.id == null` for intent clarity.
  - (F2-d) Lines 33-36 — payload construction uses `any` types
    throughout. No type safety. If `item` ever contains a
    circular reference or a non-serializable field (e.g., a
    Date object, though dates are stripped at line 36), the
    `JSON.stringify` at line 40 throws → caught by no one (no
    try/catch in save) → unhandled rejection.
  - (F2-e) Line 36 — `delete payload.data.id; delete
    payload.data.createdAt; delete payload.data.updatedAt;`
    — client-side strip is REDUNDANT with server-side strip

    trust one or the other. Harmless.
  - (F2-f) Line 39 — credentials: "include" ✓ present.

    `loadItems()` completes. For a fast network, this is

    toggle, nothing happens, clicks again — that's two toggle
    POSTs in flight, which on the server do `cur.visible =
    !cur.visible` twice (route.ts:60) → no-op net change. The
    user ends up more confused than before.
  - (F4-e) NO per-action loading state on the toggle button.
    No disabled-state during the round-trip. Same as F3-f.
  - (F4-f) NO "toggling..." label or spinner. Combined with
    F4-d, this makes the toggle button feel non-responsive.

----- 5. move (reorder)  [FAIL — race condition, no error path,
                                       non-atomic, default-order bug] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:65-81

Code:
  65:  const move = async (id: string, dir: -1 | 1) => {
  66:    const idx = items.findIndex(i => i.id === id);
  67:    const newIdx = idx + dir;
  68:    if (newIdx < 0 || newIdx >= items.length) return;
  69:    // Swap orders
  70:    const a = items[idx];
  71:    const b = items[newIdx];
  72:    await Promise.all([
  73:      fetch("/api/admin/nav", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  74:        credentials: "include",
  75:        body: JSON.stringify({ action: "update", id: a.id, data: { order: b.order } }) }),
  76:      fetch("/api/admin/nav", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  77:        credentials: "include",
        body: JSON.stringify({ action: "update", id: b.id, data: { order: a.order } }) }),
  78:    ]);
  79:    loadItems();
  80:    ...
  80:    loadItems();
  81:  };

Findings:
  - (F5-a) Lines 72-78 — `Promise.all` over TWO fetches. If
    fetch #1 succeeds (a.order := b.order) but fetch #2 fails
    (network drop, server 500, etc.), Promise.all REJECTS →
    unhandled (no try/catch at the move() level). The DB now has
    TWO items with the SAME order value (a.order was overwritten
    to b.order, but b.order was never overwritten to a.order).
    Subsequent list loads sort by order asc (route.ts:13) →
    the duplicate-order pair is ordered by Prisma's secondary
    sort (insertion id order, typically). Visual order becomes
    nondeterministic and persists until the admin manually
    re-edits. NON-ATOMIC reorder → state corruption on partial
    failure.
  - (F5-b) Lines 72-78 — NO try/catch wrapping Promise.all.
    Network drop → unhandled promise rejection propagates to
    onClick at line 129/130. Same anti-pattern as F2-b/F3-b/F4-b.
  - (F5-c) DEFAULT-ORDER BUG: line 83 — `const empty = { ...,
    order: 99 };` — every newly-created menu item gets order=99.
    After creating two items, BOTH have order=99. move() between
    them does:
        a.order := b.order (= 99)
        b.order := a.order (= 99)
    → both still 99 → no-op → `loadItems()` re-sorts by order asc
    → secondary sort decides visual order. The "↑/↓" buttons
    appear to do nothing. The user clicks again, nothing happens,
    gives up. This bug compounds with F2-g (no per-action loading
    → multiple parallel saves with default order=99).
    ROOT CAUSE: no auto-incrementing max-order+1 logic on create.
    Fix (NOT applied): `payload.data.order = items.length`
    (or `Math.max(...items.map(i=>i.order), -1) + 1`) when isNew.
  - (F5-d) Lines 66-67 — `idx + dir` may overflow to -1 if idx
    === 0 and dir === -1, or to items.length if idx ===
    items.length-1 and dir === 1. Line 68 catches both. ✓ But
    line 66 — `findIndex` returns -1 if id not found (e.g.,
    stale UI after a parallel delete from another tab). Then
    idx === -1, newIdx === -2 or 0. newIdx < 0 (true for -2)
    → return at line 68. Safe. (For dir === +1 from idx === -1,
    newIdx === 0, `newIdx >= items.length` may be false →
    proceeds → `items[-1]` at line 70 is `undefined` → `a.id`
    throws TypeError → unhandled rejection. Edge case: stale
    id not in current items list AND dir === +1. Realistic if
    another admin (or the same admin in another tab) deleted the
    item between loadItems render and the move click.)
  - (F5-e) Lines 73-78 — INDENTED inconsistently (lines 73-74
    use 6-space indent, lines 75-77 use 4-space). Cosmetic.
  - (F5-f) Lines 73-78 — credentials: "include" ✓ on BOTH
    fetches. ✓
  - (F5-g) Lines 73-78 — NO response check on either fetch
    (same as F2-a). If the server returns 401 (session expired)
    on either POST, Promise.all silently resolves (fetch resolves
    with the 401 Response, doesn't reject — only network errors
    reject). loadItems() runs, items are unchanged (or
    partially changed per F5-a if one POST actually succeeded).
    User sees no error.
  - (F5-h) Lines 129-130 — the "↑" and "↓" buttons use
    `disabled={i === 0}` / `disabled={i === items.length - 1}`
    respectively. ✓ Good — prevents clicking past the ends.
    But disabled is computed from the CURRENT items array, not
    from the in-flight state. If the user clicks "↑" on item
    idx=2 (disabled=false at click time), then before the
    fetch resolves, clicks "↑" on the same row again (now
    visually at idx=2 still — loadItems hasn't run yet), the
    second click fires a second move(id, -1) — which now
    references items[2] and items[1] (unchanged from
    first click's pre-state). Two parallel move()s with
    overlapping swaps → race on the DB orders. No lock / no
    debounce.
  - (F5-i) Lines 65-81 — NO per-row in-flight loading state.
    The "↑/↓" buttons are not disabled during the round-trip.
    Combined with F5-h, enables multi-click races.

----- 6. href scheme validation  [FAIL — NO validation client-side;
                                                server defaults to "#"] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:105 (input field),
           src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:35 (save payload),
           src/app/api/admin/nav/route.ts:36 (server default)

Code:
  NavMenuManager.tsx:105:
    <input placeholder="Link (e.g. #about or https://...)"
           value={editing.href || ""}
           onChange={e => setEditing({ ...editing, href: e.target.value })}
           style={inputStyle} />
  NavMenuManager.tsx:35-36:
    payload.data = { ...item };
    delete payload.data.id; delete payload.data.createdAt; delete payload.data.updatedAt;
  route.ts:36:
    href: String(d.href || "#"),

Findings:
  - (F6-a) NavMenuManager.tsx:105 — placeholder says "(e.g. #about
    or https://...)" — DOCUMENTATION only. NO enforcement. The
    input is an uncontrolled-text <input> with no `pattern`,
    no `type="url"`, no onBlur validation, no onChange
    sanitization. Any string can be entered: "javascript:
    alert(document.cookie)", "data:text/html,<script>...",
    "vbscript:msgbox", "file:///etc/passwd", "  " (whitespace),
    "FTP://" (uppercase, mixed case), etc.
  - (F6-b) NavMenuManager.tsx:35-36 — payload.data.href is sent
    to the server VERBATIM. No client-side allowlist check.
  - (F6-c) route.ts:36 — server only does `String(d.href || "#")`
    — coerces to string, defaults empty/falsy to "#". Accepts
    ANY non-empty string as-is. NO scheme allowlist.
  - (F6-d) STORED XSS surface (DB-side): the unsafe href is
    PERSISTED to the DB (navItem.href column) as raw string.
    ANY consumer of this column OTHER than page.tsx:478-487
    (which has the safeHref scheme allowlist at render time)
    is vulnerable. Currently page.tsx IS the only known
    consumer, and IT validates — so the active XSS surface
    is mitigated at the render layer. BUT:
      * Defense-in-depth gap: storage accepts poison, render
        sanitizes. If a future refactor moves the render
        away from the safeHref block (e.g., a new admin
        preview, a JSON-LD generator, a sitemap generator,
        an RSS feed, a Bale/Telegram bot that emits the
        href as a clickable link), the unsafe href escapes
        into a click-executeable context.
      * The stored href "javascript:alert(1)" is technically
        a stored-payload XSS waiting for a consumer that
        renders href as `<a href={...}>` without the safeHref
        guard. The NavMenuManager.tsx itself does NOT render
        href as a clickable <a> — line 124-126 shows it as
        text inside a <span> ("{item.href} {item.target ===
        '_blank' ? '(new tab)' : ''}"), so the admin preview
        is safe. The risk is the OTHER consumers.
  - (F6-e) ROUTE accepts ANY string for `target` too
    (route.ts:37: `String(d.target || "_self")`). NavMenuManager
    only offers "_self" / "_blank" via the <select> at line 106,
    but the API would accept target="_self\" onerror=alert(1) \"
    if someone POSTs directly. The NavMenuManager client never
    sends such values, but the server doesn't reject them.
  - (F6-f) RECOMMENDED (not applied) client-side validation:
       * Allow: ^(#?\/[a-zA-Z0-9\-_/.]*)$ (anchor or relative
         path), ^mailto:..., ^tel:..., ^https?:\/\/ (with
         new URL() parse check).
       * Reject: javascript:, data:, vbscript:, file:, blob:,
         about:, view-source:, anything with control chars
         (\x00-\x1f, \x7f-\x9f), leading whitespace, mixed-
         case "JaVaScRiPt:" (case-insensitive prefix check).
       * Show inline error message in the editor (currently
         no error display element exists at all — see item 9).
  - (F6-g) Cross-reference: V17.4-SEC-12 Q5 (no sanitization
    of stored content elsewhere in app). Same pattern: store
    raw, sanitize at render. page.tsx:478-487 is the only
    thing standing between stored-poison and click-executeable
    XSS. If that block is ever refactored out, the NavMenuManager
    becomes the injection vector.

----- 7. credentials: 'include'  [PASS — present on all 6 fetches] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:16, 39, 50, 59, 74, 77

Findings:
  - (F7-a) Line 16  — loadItems GET — `credentials: "include"` ✓
  - (F7-b) Line 39  — save POST      — `credentials: "include"` ✓
  - (F7-c) Line 50  — del POST       — `credentials: "include"` ✓
  - (F7-d) Line 59  — toggle POST    — `credentials: "include"` ✓
  - (F7-e) Line 74  — move POST #1   — `credentials: "include"` ✓
  - (F7-f) Line 77  — move POST #2   — `credentials: "include"` ✓
  - (F7-g) All 6 fetch calls correctly include credentials. ✓
  - (F7-h) The server (route.ts:27) calls `checkAdminAuth(req,
    password)` which at admin-auth.ts:17-31 ignores the
    `password` arg and reads the session cookie via
    `getSessionFromRequest(request)`. So credentials:"include"
    is the SOLE auth mechanism — and it IS correctly applied.
    Cross-ref: V17.4-SEC-12 F-D (dead `password` param) — same
    dead param pattern visible at route.ts:9 and route.ts:26
    on the server side. The CLIENT (NavMenuManager) correctly
    does NOT send any password field in either GET query or
    POST body. ✓
  - (F7-i) NOTE: `credentials: "include"` sends cookies cross-
    origin if the API is on a different origin. For same-origin
    (the default in this Next.js app), `same-origin` would
    suffice and be more conservative. `include` is correct
    here but slightly broader than necessary.
  - (F7-j) NOTE: `credentials: "include"` requires the server
    to send `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` AND a
    specific (non-`*`) `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` if cross-
    origin. For same-origin Next.js API routes, no CORS
    headers are needed. Current setup is fine.

----- 8. Loading state  [PARTIAL — initial load only;
                                     no per-action, no timeout] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:11, 14, 20, 85

Code:
  11:  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  14:    setLoading(true);
  20:    setLoading(false);
  85:  if (loading) return <p style={{...}}>loading...</p>;

Findings:
  - (F8-a) Line 11 — initial state `true`. ✓ Correct — first
    paint shows "loading..." until items are fetched.
  - (F8-b) Lines 14, 20 — loadItems sets loading true at start,
    false at end. ✓ Correct lifecycle for initial load.
  - (F8-c) Line 85 — `if (loading) return <p>loading...</p>`
    — the ENTIRE component returns JUST the loading <p>.
    This means during initial load, the "new item" button at
    line 90 is NOT visible. The user can't prepare a new menu
    item while the existing list loads. Minor UX issue (loading
    is usually <500ms for a small list).
  - (F8-d) NO per-action loading states. The single `loading`
    boolean is shared across all 5 actions (loadItems, save,
    del, toggle, move). save/del/toggle/move do NOT call
    `setLoading(true)` — they don't disable the UI during
    their round-trips. This means:
      * User clicks "save" → editor closes immediately (line 42
        `setEditing(null)`) BEFORE the POST resolves. List
        reload happens AFTER the POST resolves (line 43).
        Between click and reload, the UI is in a transient
        state where the new item isn't visible but the editor
        is gone. If the network is slow, this looks like
        "did I save?".
      * User clicks "delete" → confirm() → POST fires →
        during the POST, the row is still visible AND still
        clickable (no disabled state on row buttons). User
        can click "edit" / "hide" / "↑" / "↓" on the row
        being deleted → race conditions.
      * User clicks "↑" → during the round-trip, user can
        click "↑" again (see F5-h).
  - (F8-e) NO timeout on any fetch. If the server hangs
    (e.g., DB connection exhausted), `loading` stays `true`
    forever on initial load — the panel is stuck on the
    "loading..." <p> with no way to retry. Consistent with
    V17.4-SEC-12 Q8 (no AbortController anywhere).
  - (F8-f) NO skeleton / shimmer / spinner — just plain text
    "loading...". For a 0-item list, the user can't tell
    whether it's loading or genuinely empty (since F8-c hides
    the count badge during load — actually no, the count
    badge is at line 91 which is below the `if (loading)`
    return at line 85, so it's NOT shown during load either;
    that's correct).
  - (F8-g) loadItems() is called after EVERY action (save,
    del, toggle, move). After the action's POST resolves,
    loadItems() fires a GET, sets loading=true, then waits.
    During this GET, line 85 kicks in → the ENTIRE list +
    editor disappears, replaced by "loading...". If the
    user was mid-edit (e.g., editing a different row while
    a parallel action completed), their in-progress edits
    are LOST (setEditing state preserved, but the editing
    form at lines 94-116 is unmounted because line 85
    returns early).
    THIS IS A DATA-LOSS BUG: parallel actions trigger
    loadItems() → unmounts the editor → unsaved edits lost.
    Trigger: open editor on item A, click "hide" on item B
    → toggle() → loadItems() → loading=true → editor
    unmounts → editing state preserved but the form's
    controlled inputs (lines 100-105) lose focus and any
    in-progress keystrokes since the last setEditing call
    are actually preserved (because editing state is in
    React state, not the DOM) → but the user SEES the form
    disappear mid-typing → confusion → likely abandons.
    Severity: MED UX bug.
  - (F8-h) No global "is any action in progress" flag. The
    `loading` boolean conflates "fetching list" with "no
    actions pending". A separate `saving`/`deleting`/
    `toggling`/`moving` set of booleans (or a single
    `busyAction` enum) would be cleaner.

----- 9. Errors shown  [FAIL — NO error display path;
                                     all errors swallowed] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:19, 37-41, 48-52,
           57-61, 72-78 (all action handlers), and the render
           block at lines 87-138

Findings:
  - (F9-a) NO error state in useState. Only `items`, `loading`,
    `editing` are tracked. No `error` state, no `lastError`
    string, no error boundary wrapper.
  - (F9-b) Line 19 — loadItems's `catch {}` is EMPTY. Network
    error, JSON parse error, server 500 — all swallowed. No
    console.error, no toast, no banner, no error state set.
    Items stay `[]`, loading flips false, user sees empty
    list (line 118 `items.map(...)` returns no rows). NO
    indication of failure.
  - (F9-c) Lines 37-41 (save) — NO try/catch. If fetch throws,
    rejection propagates to onClick at line 112, React logs
    to console, user sees... nothing. Editor stays open,
    list doesn't reload. User has no idea the save failed.
  - (F9-d) Lines 48-52 (del) — same as F9-c. Network error →
    unhandled rejection → silent failure. Item remains in
    list (line 53 `loadItems()` only runs if fetch resolves).
  - (F9-e) Lines 57-61 (toggle) — same as F9-c/F9-d.
  - (F9-f) Lines 72-78 (move) — Promise.all rejects on ANY
    fetch failure → unhandled → silent. Worse: partial
    state corruption (see F5-a) — items may end up with
    duplicate orders, but the user sees no error.
  - (F9-g) SERVER-RETURNED ERRORS ARE NEVER READ. None of
    the 5 action handlers `await res.json()` or check
    `res.ok`. So even when the server returns a structured
    error like `{ ok: false, error: "unauthorized" }` (401,
    route.ts:28), `"missing_id"` (400, route.ts:44/51/57),
    `"not_found"` (404, route.ts:59), `"invalid_action"`
    (400, route.ts:64), or `"server_error"` (500,
    route.ts:68) — the client treats them all as success
    and calls loadItems().
  - (F9-h) NO error UI in render. Lines 87-138 contain
    ONLY:
      * new-item button (line 90),
      * item count badge (line 91),
      * editor form (lines 94-116),
      * items list (lines 118-136).
    There is NO banner, NO toast, NO inline error message,
    NO error icon. If any action fails, the user gets
    ZERO feedback.
  - (F9-i) The 401 case (session expired) is particularly
    bad: every action silently fails, the list appears
    unchanged (because loadItems() also gets 401 →
    data.ok === false → items stay as the old cached list
    at line 18). The admin thinks the panel is broken
    and starts clicking everything, generating more 401s
    in a tight loop. NO redirect to /login. NO "session
    expired, please re-login" message.
  - (F9-j) Cross-ref: V17.4-SEC-12 noted the same pattern
    elsewhere in the codebase. The NavMenuManager is
    consistent with the app's existing (poor) error-
    handling convention — but that convention is itself
    broken.

----- 10. Successes shown  [FAIL — NO success display path;
                                              save/del/toggle/move
                                              all rely on
                                              implicit list-reload] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:42-43, 53, 62, 79-80
           (the four action handlers' "success" paths), and the
           render block at lines 87-138

Findings:
  - (F10-a) NO success state in useState. No `lastSuccess`
    string, no `flash` message, no toast queue.
  - (F10-b) Lines 42-43 (save success path): `setEditing(null);
    loadItems();` — the editor CLOSES and the list RELOADS.
    The user infers success from "the editor closed and the
    list now contains the new item". BUT per F2-a, the fetch
    may have FAILED silently — the editor still closes, the
    list still reloads, the user infers success even though
    the item wasn't saved. The "success" signal is identical
    to the "failure" signal: editor closes + list reloads.
    NO POSITIVE CONFIRMATION that the POST returned 200 with
    `{ ok: true }`.
  - (F10-c) Line 53 (del success path): `loadItems();` — the
    list reloads. If the delete succeeded, the item
    disappears from the list. If the delete FAILED (per
    F3-a), the item stays in the list. The user has to
    visually diff the list before/after to know whether
    the delete worked. NO "Item deleted" message, NO toast,
    NO undo button. NO disabled state during the round-trip
    (per F3-f).
  - (F10-d) Line 62 (toggle success path): `loadItems();` —
    same as F10-c. If toggle succeeded, the dot at line 121
    flips ●↔○. If toggle failed, the dot stays the same.
    User must visually diff to confirm.
  - (F10-e) Lines 79-80 (move success path): `loadItems();` —
    same as F10-c/F10-d. If move succeeded, the row visually
    moves up/down in the list. If move failed (per F5-a/F5-g),
    the row stays put. User must visually diff. AND per F5-a
    partial failure, the list might be in a corrupted state
    with duplicate orders — which `loadItems()` will sort by
    order asc (route.ts:13), breaking the visual order the
    admin expected. NO "moved" message, NO toast.
  - (F10-f) NO success toast / banner / inline message
    anywhere in the render block (lines 87-138). Same as
    F9-h but for success.
  - (F10-g) NO optimistic UI updates. save() doesn't add the
    new item to `items` until loadItems() completes. toggle()
    doesn't flip the visible state until loadItems() completes.
    move() doesn't swap the rows until loadItems() completes.
    This means there's a 50-500ms delay between click and
    visible feedback. Combined with F10-c/F10-d/F10-e (no
    toast), the panel feels sluggish and unresponsive.
  - (F10-h) NO sound, NO haptic, NO animation on success.
    Cosmetic, but contributes to the lack of positive
    confirmation.
  - (F10-i) The "successful save" UX (editor closes + list
    reloads) is INDISTINGUISHABLE from the "failed save"
    UX (editor closes + list reloads) — see F10-b. This
    is the single most dangerous UX bug in the file:
    the user cannot tell success from failure.

ADDITIONAL FINDINGS (not in the 10 checklist items)
================================================================

----- F-A. TypeScript `any` everywhere  [LOW, maintainability] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:10, 12, 30, 35, 83

Code:
  10:  const [items, setItems] = useState<any[]>([]);
  12:  const [editing, setEditing] = useState<any | null>(null);
  30:  const save = async (item: any) => {
  35:    payload.data = { ...item };
  83:  const empty = { labelEn: "", labelFa: "", labelDe: "", href: "#",
                    target: "_self", visible: true, order: 99 };

Analysis:
  - The Prisma schema (referenced at V17.4-SEC-12 audit) has a
    `navItem` model with explicit fields. NavMenuManager.tsx
    uses `any[]` for items and `any | null` for editing, losing
    all type safety. Field typos (e.g., `item.labelEN` instead
    of `item.labelEn`) won't be caught at compile time — they'll
    silently produce undefined at runtime. The `empty` constant
    at line 83 has the right shape but is not typed against the
    Prisma model.
  - Fix (NOT applied): import the Prisma-generated
    `NavItem` type and use `useState<NavItem[]>([])` /
    `useState<Partial<NavItem> | null>(null)`.

----- F-B. No keyboard shortcuts / no form submission via Enter  [LOW, UX] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:100-105

Analysis:
  - The editor inputs at lines 100-105 are plain <input> elements
    not wrapped in a <form>. Pressing Enter while focused on an
    input does nothing. The user must click the "save" button at
    line 112 with the mouse. Minor accessibility/UX issue.
  - The <select> at line 106 also lacks form context.

----- F-C. No drag-and-drop reorder  [LOW, UX] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:129-130

Analysis:
  - Reordering is via "↑" / "↓" buttons only. For menus with
    many items, drag-and-drop would be faster. The current
    "swap two adjacent orders" model also breaks for non-
    adjacent moves (admin must click ↑/↓ N times to move an
    item from position 10 to position 1). No "move to top" /
    "move to bottom" buttons either.

----- F-D. No empty-state message  [LOW, UX] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:118-136

Analysis:
  - When `items.length === 0` (after a successful load of an
    empty list — e.g., a fresh install with no menu items yet),
    the render block produces:
        <div>
          <button>+ new item</button>
          <span>0 items</span>
          {/* no rows */}
        </div>
    The user sees a button and a count but no explanatory
    message. Compare with a "No menu items yet. Click '+ new
    item' to create one." hint that would be friendlier.
  - The count badge "0 items" at line 91 IS shown — that's
    a minor positive.

----- F-E. Stale-closure risk in useEffect  [LOW, latent] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:28

Code:
  28:  useEffect(() => { loadItems(); }, []);

Analysis:
  - ESLint `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warns: `loadItems` is
    missing from the deps array. Today this is safe because
    `loadItems` only references state setters (`setItems`,
    `setLoading`) which have stable identity. But if `loadItems`
    is ever refactored to capture `items` (e.g., to merge
    instead of replace), the stale-closure bug becomes real:
    the initial load would use the empty initial `items`, and
    subsequent calls (e.g., after a save) would use a stale
    snapshot. The fix (NOT applied) is to use the
    `useCallback(() => { ... }, [])` pattern or to inline the
    load logic into the useEffect.

----- F-F. Dead `password` param on server (cross-ref V17.4-SEC-12 F-D) -----
Location: src/app/api/admin/nav/route.ts:9, 26-27

Code:
  9:  const password = url.searchParams.get("password") || "";
  10:  const authCheck = await checkAdminAuth(req, password); ...
  26:  const password = String(body.password || "");
  27:  const authCheck = await checkAdminAuth(req, password); if (!authCheck.ok) { ... }

Analysis:
  - Same pattern as V17.4-SEC-12 F-D (chat route.ts:222). The
    server reads `password` from query (GET, line 9) and body
    (POST, line 26), passes it to `checkAdminAuth(req,
    password)`, which at admin-auth.ts:17 IGNORES the second
    argument (`_password?: string`).
  - The CLIENT (NavMenuManager.tsx) correctly does NOT send any
    `password` field (no `?password=xxx` in the GET URL at
    line 16, no `password:` in any POST body at lines 33-35,
    51, 60, 75, 77). ✓ Client is clean.
  - SERVER has the dead param — admins who manually craft
    requests with `?password=xxx` leak their (now-unused)
    password into NGINX/Vercel access logs (per V17.4-SEC-12
    F-D analysis). Server-side dead-code cleanup is the fix
    (NOT applied — out of audit scope for this file).

----- F-G. No CSRF token (defense in depth)  [LOW, defense-in-depth] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx (all POST calls)

Analysis:
  - The API relies solely on the session cookie (sent via
    `credentials: "include"`). If the app is ever exposed to
    cross-origin contexts (e.g., embedded in an iframe, served
    from a different origin than the API, or if SameSite=Lax
    is changed to SameSite=None for any reason), CSRF becomes
    possible. Currently SameSite=Lax (default for session
    cookies in modern browsers) blocks cross-origin POSTs
    without an explicit SameSite=None+Secure override, so
    CSRF is mitigated. No explicit CSRF token is sent in the
    body or as a header. Defense-in-depth gap, not an active
    vulnerability.
  - Cross-ref: V17.4-SEC-04 #6 (chat CSRF noted). Same
    pattern: cookie-only auth, no CSRF token. The chat audit
    rated this LOW for CSRF specifically (SameSite=Lax
    mitigates), which applies here too.

----- F-H. No rate limiting on these admin POSTs (cross-ref
          V17.4-SEC-12 Q7/F-5, V17.3-SEC-02 Q4/F-5)  [LOW] -----
Location: src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx (all POST calls);
           src/app/api/admin/nav/route.ts (POST handler)

Analysis:
  - The client (NavMenuManager) can fire POSTs as fast as the
    user can click. Combined with F2-g/F3-f/F4-e/F5-i (no per-
    action loading state, no disabled buttons during round-
    trip), an admin (or attacker with admin session) can
    generate a tight loop of POSTs by spamming clicks.
  - The server route.ts has NO rate limit. Consistent with
    V17.4-SEC-12 Q7 / V17.3-SEC-02 Q4/F-5 (/api/admin/* not
    rate-limited).
  - Impact: an attacker who steals an admin session cookie
    could enumerate navItem ids and delete them all in a tight
    loop. Or spam create with default order=99 (per F5-c),
    flooding the DB.
  - Cross-ref: prior audits recommend per-route rate limits
    on /api/admin/*. Not implemented.

FINAL VERDICT
================================================================
Of the 10 audit items:
  - 1 PASS  (item 7 — credentials:include correctly applied on
             all 6 fetches; client correctly omits the dead
             `password` param).
  - 2 PARTIAL (items 1 loadItems, 8 loading state — initial load
             works but no error path / no per-action state /
             no timeout).
  - 7 FAIL (items 2,3,4,5,6,9,10).

The 4 FAIL-without-feedback items (2 save, 3 del, 4 toggle,
5 move) ALL share the same root-cause pattern:

  PATTERN-A (response-not-checked): the `await fetch(...)`
  return value is completely ignored in save/del/toggle/move.
  No `res.ok` check, no `await res.json()`. Server-returned
  errors (401/400/404/500) are treated as success, the UI
  proceeds as if the action succeeded, and the only feedback
  is the eventual list reload — which may show stale data
  (because the action failed silently).

  PATTERN-B (no-try-catch): all 4 action handlers lack
  try/catch around the fetch. Network errors throw and
  propagate as unhandled promise rejections. React logs
  to console but the UI shows nothing.

  PATTERN-C (no-error-state / no-success-state): no
  useState for error or success. No toast / banner /
  inline message in the render block. Success and failure
  are INDISTINGUISHABLE to the user (item 10 = item 9
  in terms of UI feedback — both = "list reloads, no
  message").

These three patterns compound: when an action fails, the
user has NO way to know — the UI looks the same as success.
Worst case (F2-a "illusion of success"): admin creates a
menu item, sees the editor close and list reload, walks
away — the item was never persisted (401, session expired),
and on next visit the item is gone. Admin blames themselves
or the system, no diagnostic trail.

The reorder bug F5-c (default order=99 for all new items →
↑/↓ buttons appear to do nothing) compounds with F2-g (no
per-action loading → admin clicks "save" multiple times →
multiple items with order=99 → move between them is no-op).

The href scheme validation gap F6-d is mitigated at the
render layer by page.tsx:478-487's safeHref block, but the
DB stores raw unsanitized href. Defense-in-depth gap: any
future consumer that renders href as `<a href={item.href}>`
without the safeHref allowlist becomes a stored-XSS sink.

Cross-references (worklog):
  - V17.4-SEC-12 Q8 (no AbortController / timeout on fetch):
    applies here too — loadItems() and all 4 action handlers
    can hang indefinitely. F8-e.
  - V17.4-SEC-12 F-D (dead `password` param): server-side
    route.ts:9 and route.ts:26 carry the same dead param.
    Client correctly omits it. F-F.
  - V17.4-SEC-12 Q5 (no sanitization of stored content):
    applies here — href is stored raw, sanitized at render
    only. F6-d.
  - V17.4-SEC-12 Q7 / V17.3-SEC-02 Q4/F-5 (no rate limit on
    /api/admin/*): applies here — server route.ts has no
    rate limit. F-H.
  - V17.4-SEC-04 #6 (CSRF cookie-only): applies here.
    SameSite=Lax mitigates. F-G.

Q1. reCAPTCHA mandatory + fail-closed?
================================================================
Status: PASS

Server (route.ts):
  - route.ts:98-105 — token presence + minimum length (>=10) required.
    Missing/invalid -> 400 "captcha_required". Logged as "captcha_missing".
  - route.ts:106-124 — siteverify POST to
    https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify with
    process.env.RECAPTCHA_SECRET || "".
      * route.ts:117 — `captchaOk = !!verifyData.success`
      * route.ts:118-120 — on success=false, logs "captcha_failed" with
        Google's error-codes.
      * route.ts:121-124 — on network EXCEPTION (fetch reject / JSON
        parse fail), the catch block logs "captcha_failed" but does NOT
        set `captchaOk = true`. It stays at its default `false`.
  - route.ts:125-130 — `if (!captchaOk) return 400 captcha_failed`.
    This is the fail-closed gate: ANY exception during verification
    leaves captchaOk = false, and the request is rejected.

Client (page.tsx):
  - page.tsx:349-355 — pre-flight check `grecaptcha.getResponse()`; if
    empty, sets form-status error and aborts fetch. Defense-in-depth only
    (server is authoritative).
  - page.tsx:794-802 — reCAPTCHA widget rendered only after mount to
    avoid hydration mismatch; placeholder div otherwise. Reasonable.

Notes (informational, not defects):
  - reCAPTCHA v2 (checkbox) is used. v3 (score-based, action-typed)
    would be stronger but is overkill for a contact form.
  - route.ts:112 — `process.env.RECAPTCHA_SECRET || ""`. If env var is
    unset in production, siteverify sends empty secret -> Google returns
    success=false -> ALL contact submissions rejected. This is fail-
    closed (safe) but means the form is completely non-functional
    without the env var configured. Worth a deploy checklist note.

Verdict: ✅ Mandatory + fail-closed verified.

Q2. Honeypot field sent?
================================================================
Status: PASS

Client (page.tsx):
  - page.tsx:768-775 — hidden input `name="website"`, tabIndex=-1,
    autoComplete="off", aria-hidden="true", off-screen via inline style
    (left:-9999px, width:1, height:1, overflow:hidden).
  - page.tsx:367 — sent in JSON body as `website:
      (e.target as HTMLFormElement).website?.value || ""`.

Server (route.ts):
  - route.ts:81 — `website = String(body.website || "").trim()`.
  - route.ts:82-87 — if `website` is non-empty (truthy), logs
    "honeypot_triggered" to SecurityLog (with `website.slice(0, 50)` —
    capped, route.ts:84) and returns `{ ok: true }` (HTTP 200) — fake
    success so the bot doesn't learn it was caught. Good practice.

Notes (informational, not defects):
  - Inline `style` for hiding the field could be stripped by an
    over-aggressive CSS minifier or by accessibility agents that strip
    styles. A `<input type="hidden">` is more robust but easier for
    bots to skip; the off-screen text input is the standard honeypot
    pattern and is acceptable.
  - Field name "website" is a common honeypot name — sophisticated bots
    that recognize common honeypot names will skip it. A random per-
    session name would be marginally stronger; not necessary.

Verdict: ✅ Honeypot sent + checked + fail-closed (silently rejected).

Q3. Time-trap (V17.4 fixed — verify useState, not Date.now() on render)?
================================================================
Status: PASS — V17.4 fix verified

V17.4 fix verification (page.tsx):
  - page.tsx:80 — `const [formLoadTime, setFormLoadTime] = useState(0);`
  - page.tsx:82-103 — `useEffect(() => { setMounted(true);
      setFormLoadTime(Date.now()); ... }, [])`. Single dependency array
      `[]` -> runs once on mount. ✅ NOT called on every render.
  - page.tsx:777 — `<input type="hidden" name="_t" value={formLoadTime} />`
    Bound to state, not inline `Date.now()` on render. ✅
  - page.tsx:369 — submit handler reads `_t` from the form DOM:
    `_t: (e.target as HTMLFormElement)._t?.value || Date.now()`.
      * The `|| Date.now()` fallback only fires if the `_t` field is
        missing from the form (DOM tampering, ad-blocker stripping
        hidden inputs, etc.). In that case `_t = Date.now()` (current
        time) -> server computes `Date.now() - Date.now() ≈ 0 < 2000`
        -> blocked as "too_fast" (route.ts:90-93). Fail-closed. ✅

Server (route.ts):
  - route.ts:89 — `const submittedAt = Number(body._t || 0);`
  - route.ts:90 — `if (submittedAt && Date.now() - submittedAt < 2000)`.
  - route.ts:91-92 — logs "time_trap_triggered", returns 400 "too_fast".

FINDING 3.1 [LOW] — Server truthiness bypass:
  - route.ts:90's `submittedAt &&` short-circuit means a bot that
    sends `body._t = 0` (or omits `_t` entirely) makes `submittedAt = 0`
    (falsy) -> the time-trap check is SKIPPED entirely -> request
    passes the time-trap stage.
  - Compare to client fallback (page.tsx:369): missing `_t` is replaced
    with `Date.now()` which then fails the <2000 check (blocked). The
    server's behavior is inconsistent with the client's intent.
  - Impact: defense-in-depth gap only. reCAPTCHA + honeypot + rate
    limit carry the primary load, so this gap is LOW. But a bot that
    sends `_t: 0` bypasses the time-trap entirely.

FINDING 3.2 [LOW] — Threshold UX risk:
  - 2000ms is aggressive. A human with browser autofill who clicks
    submit immediately after page load (e.g., a returning visitor
    whose browser pre-fills name/email) would be blocked. Not a
    security issue, but a product/UX tuning concern.

FINDING 3.3 [LOW] — Time-trap not enforced client-side:
  - The client doesn't check `_t` before submit. A bot using the
    legitimate client (e.g., headless Chrome via Playwright) would
    have a real `formLoadTime` from the useEffect, so it WOULD pass
    the time-trap if it waits >2s. Server-side enforcement is the
    only real gate. (This is fine — server-side is what matters — but
    worth noting that client-side `_t` is purely a "bot that didn't
    run JS" detector.)

Verdict: ✅ V17.4 useState fix verified. 3 LOW findings (truthiness
  bypass, threshold UX, client-only enforcement).

Q4. Rate limit works (V17.4 added cleanup)?
================================================================
Status: PASS — cleanup verified; XFF spoofing inherited from chat route

V17.4 cleanup verification (route.ts):
  - route.ts:6-7 — `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000` (10 min),
    `RATE_LIMIT_MAX = 3`.
  - route.ts:8 — `const hits = new Map<string, number[]>();`
  - route.ts:11-20 — `setInterval` every 5 min: iterates all keys,
    filters out timestamps older than the window, deletes keys whose
    filtered arrays are empty. Uses `.unref?.()` so the timer doesn't
    block Node.js shutdown. ✅ Memory-leak fix verified.
  - route.ts:22-33 — `rateLimit(ip)`: filters existing timestamps
    within window; if `arr.length >= MAX` returns false; otherwise
    pushes current timestamp and updates Map. Correct sliding-window
    implementation.
  - route.ts:24 — Dev bypass for `::1`, `127.0.0.1`, `unknown` IPs
    ONLY when `NODE_ENV !== "production"`. In production, `unknown` IP
    does NOT bypass (the `&&` short-circuits). ✅

FINDING 4.1 [LOW-MED] — X-Forwarded-For spoofing (inherited):
  - route.ts:48-51 — IP is read as `x-forwarded-for` first entry,
    then `x-real-ip`, then `"unknown"`. XFF takes precedence.
  - Same defect flagged in V17.3-SEC-02 Q11/F-9 and V17.4-SEC-12 Q7
    for the chat route. An attacker with a rotating proxy can send
    `X-Forwarded-For: <random-ip>` per request -> each request gets
    a fresh Map key -> rate limit never triggers.
  - Mitigation only if NGINX is configured to overwrite (not append
    to) XFF with the real client IP — that's a deployment concern,
    not a code concern, but the code TRUSTS whatever XFF it receives.
  - On Vercel Edge, the platform overwrites XFF with the real client
    IP -> not exploitable there. On self-hosted (project's target per
    install.sh), depends on NGINX config.

FINDING 4.2 [LOW] — No global rate cap:
  - Only per-IP. A botnet of 10k IPs can submit 30k messages per 10
    minutes. Combined with no body-size cap (Q8) and the synchronous
    DB write at route.ts:159, this is a resource-exhaustion surface.
  - No per-email or per-session counter either.

FINDING 4.3 [LOW] — Per-process state, not shared:
  - The Map is module-scoped, in-memory. On Vercel Edge each instance
    has its own Map -> effective limit is `3 × instance_count` per IP.
    On self-hosted Node.js (single process), it's 3 per IP per 10 min
    as intended. Acceptable for the project's deployment model but
    worth documenting.

FINDING 4.4 [LOW] — Rate-limit hit logged nowhere:
  - When `rateLimit(ip)` returns false (route.ts:62-67), the request
    is rejected with 429 "rate_limit" but NO logSecurityEvent is
    called. Compare to honeypot (route.ts:84), time-trap (route.ts:91),
    and captcha failures (route.ts:100, 119, 122) which ARE logged.
    A persistent attacker hitting the rate limit 1000x in 10 min
    leaves NO trace in SecurityLog. Forensics gap.

Verdict: ✅ Cleanup works (memory leak fixed). XFF spoofing inherited
  from chat route (LOW-MED). 3 LOW additional findings (no global cap,
  per-process state, rate-limit hits not logged).

Q5. Bot detection?
================================================================
Status: PARTIAL — UA-based heuristic is weak

Server (route.ts):
  - route.ts:52 — `userAgent = req.headers.get("user-agent") || ""`.
  - route.ts:55-60 — `if (/bot|crawl|spider|slurp|wget|curl/i.test(
      userAgent) && userAgent.length < 80)` -> 403 "Blocked".

FINDING 5.1 [LOW] — Bizarre length gate (`< 80`):
  - The `&& userAgent.length < 80` check defeats the regex for real
    crawlers. Real Googlebot UA is ~76-145 chars depending on variant;
    a real Googlebot with the long-form UA passes the check (regex
    matches "bot" but length gate fails -> NOT blocked). The intent
    appears to be "block obvious curl/wget but allow legit crawlers
    to index the page" — but the contact endpoint shouldn't be
    crawled at all. Either block all bots unconditionally, or drop
    the UA heuristic entirely (reCAPTCHA + honeypot + time-trap carry
    the load).
  - An attacker using `curl/8.0.1` (10 chars) IS blocked. An attacker
    using `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36
    (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36` (120 chars) is
    NOT blocked. Trivial bypass.

FINDING 5.2 [LOW] — Empty UA bypasses:
  - A request with NO User-Agent header -> `userAgent = ""` (route.ts:52).
    The regex `/bot|.../i.test("")` is `false` -> NOT blocked. Some
    bot frameworks (and many HTTP libraries when explicitly configured)
    send empty UA. No "missing UA" rejection.

FINDING 5.3 [LOW] — Keyword list is tiny + case-handling reliance:
  - The regex is case-insensitive (the `i` flag), so case doesn't
    bypass — but the keyword list is just 6 literal substrings:
    `bot|crawl|spider|slurp|wget|curl`. Bots with UA "python-requests/
    2.31.0", "Go-http-client/1.1", "axios/1.6.0", "node-fetch",
    "HeadlessChrome" (Playwright default) are NOT caught.

Compensating controls: reCAPTCHA v2 + honeypot + time-trap + rate
limit + spam patterns. The UA heuristic is the weakest link; without
it the contact form would still be reasonably protected. The UA check
is mostly cosmetic.

Verdict: ⚠️ PARTIAL. UA-based detection is weak (3 LOW findings).
  Compensated by reCAPTCHA + honeypot + time-trap + rate limit.

Q6. Spam patterns?
================================================================
Status: PARTIAL — minimal pattern set

Server (route.ts):
  - route.ts:35-44 — `isSpammy(text)` checks 3 regexes against
    lowercased `message`:
      1. `\b(viagra|cialis|casino|lottery|prize|winner|bitcoin
         investment)\b` — keyword list (7 keywords).
      2. `(https?:\/\/[^\s]+){3,}` — 3+ URLs.
      3. `(.)\1{10,}` — 11+ identical chars in a row.
  - route.ts:152-157 — if `isSpammy(message)` returns 422
    "spam_detected".

FINDING 6.1 [LOW] — Keyword list tiny + easily bypassed:
  - 7 English keywords. Trivial bypasses: "v1agra", "c1al1s",
    "Casin0", "vi@gra", Unicode homoglyphs (CіALIS with Cyrillic і),
    zero-width-character insertion ("via­gra"), whitespace
    insertion ("vi agra"). No Levenshtein / fuzzy matching.

FINDING 6.2 [LOW] — English-only:
  - Site supports FA/DE/EN (page.tsx:21) but spam keywords are
    English-only. Persian spam ("کازینو", "جایزه", "برنده") and
    German spam ("Geld verdienen", "Casino") bypass entirely.

FINDING 6.3 [LOW] — isSpammy only checks `message`:
  - route.ts:152 — `if (isSpammy(message))`. Name and email fields
    are NOT checked. A spammer can put spam URLs / keywords in the
    `name` field (e.g., `name: "Visit http://casino.com"`) and
    bypass. The name field is sliced to 100 chars (route.ts:77) so
    it's bounded, but the content is unfiltered.

FINDING 6.4 [LOW] — URL count regex only:
  - Pattern #2 counts URLs by `https?://` occurrences. URLs without
    scheme (e.g., "www.casino.com", "casino.com") aren't counted.
    A spammer who omits the scheme can pack dozens of links without
    triggering.

FINDING 6.5 [LOW] — Repeated-char regex is permissive:
  - Pattern #3 `(.)\1{10,}` catches "aaaaaaaaaaa" but not
    "abcabcabcabc" (repeating 3-char pattern). No general "low
    entropy" check.

FINDING 6.6 [LOW] — No third-party / ML spam API:
  - No Akismet, no OOPSpam, no ML classifier. Adequate for a
    personal site; weak for production anti-spam.

Verdict: ⚠️ PARTIAL. 6 LOW findings. The patterns catch the laziest
  bots but bypass is trivial for any determined spammer.

Q7. Email validation?
================================================================
Status: PARTIAL — basic regex only

Server (route.ts):
  - route.ts:132 — `const emailRe = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;`
  - route.ts:140-145 — if regex fails, 400 "invalid_email".

Client (page.tsx):
  - page.tsx:331 — same regex.
  - page.tsx:338-342 — pre-flight check.
  - page.tsx:784 — `<input type="email" maxLength={200} required>`

FINDING 7.1 [LOW] — Regex permissive:
  - Accepts single-char TLDs (`a@b.c`), accepts very long TLDs
    (`a@b.abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz`), accepts domain with multiple
    consecutive dots is rejected (good — `[^\s@]+` doesn't allow
    dots-only local part), but `a@b.c.d.e.f.g` (many subdomains) is
    accepted. No TLD length validation (should be >= 2). No overall
    length check at the regex level (length cap of 200 chars at
    route.ts:78 handles this, but the regex itself doesn't enforce
    RFC 5321's 254-char limit).

FINDING 7.2 [LOW] — No DNS MX lookup:
  - `fakeuser@nonexistent-domain.xyz` passes the regex. For a
    contact form this is overkill to enforce, but worth noting that
    no deliverability check is performed. The forwardEmail flow
    (route.ts:171-188 via formsubmit.co) would silently fail to
    deliver, but the message is still stored in DB + sent to Bale.

FINDING 7.3 [LOW] — No normalization:
  - Gmail treats `User.Name@gmail.com` == `username@gmail.com` ==
    `username+spam@gmail.com`. The contact form treats them as 3
    distinct emails -> 3 rate-limit slots per IP. Combined with XFF
    spoofing (Q4.1), a spammer has effectively unlimited submissions.

FINDING 7.4 [LOW] — No disposable-email-domain check:
  - mailinator.com, 10minutemail.com, guerrillamail.com, etc. are
    accepted. For a contact form this is a UX tradeoff (legitimate
    users sometimes use disposables for privacy); not a security
    defect, but a spam vector.

FINDING 7.5 [LOW] — Regex compiled inside handler:
  - route.ts:132 — `const emailRe` is declared inside the POST
    handler, so it's re-compiled on every request. Minor perf issue
    (V8 caches regexes anyway), not security.

Verdict: ⚠️ PARTIAL. 5 LOW findings. Basic format check only; no
  deliverability, normalization, or disposable-domain checks.

Server (route.ts):
  - route.ts:77 — `name = String(body.name || "").trim().slice(0, 100)`
  - route.ts:78 — `email = String(body.email || "").trim().slice(0, 200)`
  - route.ts:79 — `message = String(body.message || "").trim().slice(0, 5000)`
  - route.ts:81 — `website = String(body.website || "").trim()` — NO slice.
  - route.ts:84 — honeypot logged with `website.slice(0, 50)` (capped at
    log time, but the in-memory `website` variable is unbounded).
  - route.ts:99 — `recaptchaToken.length < 10` rejected — MINIMUM only,
    no MAXIMUM.

Client (page.tsx):
  - page.tsx:780 — `<input maxLength={100}>` for name.
  - page.tsx:784 — `<input maxLength={200}>` for email.
  - page.tsx:788 — `<textarea maxLength={5000}>` for message.

FINDING 8.1 [LOW] — No max length on recaptchaToken:
  - route.ts:99 only checks `< 10`. A malicious client can send a
    10MB string as `recaptchaToken`. The siteverify POST at route.ts:108-
    114 forwards it as URLSearchParams body to Google -> URL-encodes
    to a ~30MB body -> 30MB POST to Google. No DoS impact on the
    contact server (it just forwards), but the request to Google may
    be rejected by Google's own size limits -> captchaOk = false ->
    request blocked. So effectively self-protecting, but the in-memory
    allocation of the body still happens.

FINDING 8.2 [LOW-MED] — No request body size limit:
  - route.ts:69 — `await req.json().catch(() => null)` buffers the
    ENTIRE body in memory before ANY field-level slicing. A 100MB
    JSON body -> 100MB allocation, THEN route.ts:77-79 slices the
    fields down. The slice happens too late to prevent the allocation.
  - Same defect flagged in V17.4-SEC-12 F-B on the chat route.
  - Mitigation: middleware body-size check (per prior audit
    V17.3-SEC-02 Q6), but that audit noted the middleware trusts
    Content-Length and is bypassable via chunked encoding.
  - Combined with the per-process rate limit (3/10min per IP), the
    attacker needs many IPs to exhaust memory; with XFF spoofing
    (Q4.1), they have effectively unlimited IPs.

FINDING 8.3 [LOW] — Honeypot field has no server-side length cap:
  - route.ts:81 — `website = String(body.website || "").trim()` —
    no `.slice()`. A bot could send a 50MB `website` string to
    exhaust memory BEFORE the route.ts:82 truthiness check fires
    (the variable `website` holds the full 50MB string). The
    subsequent `website.slice(0, 50)` at route.ts:84 only caps
    what's logged to DB, not the in-memory variable.
  - Bounded by FINDING 8.2 (whole body is already in memory from
    req.json()), so this is a sub-case, not an independent vector.

FINDING 8.4 [LOW] — Silent truncation, not rejection:
  - route.ts:77-79 silently truncates over-long fields. A user
    pasting a 10KB message gets it silently cut to 5KB without
    warning. UX issue, not security. Some apps prefer reject-over-
    truncate to surface the issue.

FINDING 8.5 [INFO] — Minimum message length:
  - route.ts:146 — `message.length < 10` rejected with 400
    "message_too_short". Good — prevents "hi" / "test" spam.
  - No MIN on name (1 char ok) or email (regex enforces structure).

Verdict: ✅ PASS with caveats. Field-level caps exist on name/email/
  message (server + client). No body-size limit (LOW-MED, inherited
  from middleware weakness). recaptchaToken + honeypot unbounded (LOW).

================================================================
Q9. IP/UA stored (privacy)?
================================================================
Status: FAIL — privacy/GDPR concern

Server (route.ts):
  - route.ts:48-51 — IP from `x-forwarded-for` first entry, then
    `x-real-ip`, then `"unknown"`.
  - route.ts:52 — UA from `user-agent` header, defaults to `""`.
  - route.ts:160 — `db.contactMessage.create({ data: { name, email,
      message, ip, userAgent } })` — BOTH raw IP and FULL UA string
      stored indefinitely in the ContactMessage table.

Schema (prisma/schema.prisma):
  - schema.prisma:34-43 — ContactMessage model: `ip String?`,
    `userAgent String?`, no TTL, no retention field, no auto-purge.
  - schema.prisma:452-458 — SecurityLog: `ip String?`, also no TTL.

FINDING 9.1 [MED — privacy/GDPR] — Indefinite retention of IP + UA:
  - IP addresses are personal data under GDPR (Article 4(1)) and
    Iranian data-protection regulations. The full UA string is even
    more identifying (OS version, browser version, locale, sometimes
    device model — effectively a fingerprint).
  - No retention policy, no auto-purge, no consent notice, no
    hashing or last-octet truncation. The contact form silently
    collects + indefinitely stores this data on every submission.
  - Site is FA-primary (page.tsx:21 LANGS), so GDPR may not directly
    apply, but Iranian data-protection law (SPIPA / Cyber Crime Law
    Art. 50) has similar requirements. Even if no law applies, this
    is a data-minimization failure.
  - Recommended (NOT applied — read-only audit):
      * Truncate IP to /24 (IPv4) or /64 (IPv6) before storing.
      * Truncate UA to coarse bucket ("browser=Chrome,os=Windows")
        or drop entirely.
      * Add a 30-day auto-purge cron.
      * Add a consent checkbox: "I agree my message + technical
        info will be stored to respond to my inquiry."

FINDING 9.2 [LOW] — IP also logged to SecurityLog on every failure:
  - route.ts:84 (honeypot), route.ts:91 (time-trap), route.ts:100
    (captcha missing), route.ts:119 (captcha failed), route.ts:122
    (captcha network error). Same indefinite-retention issue
    (SecurityLog has no TTL).

FINDING 9.3 [LOW] — No GDPR consent checkbox:
  - page.tsx:766-808 — form has name/email/message/captcha fields
    but NO consent checkbox before the submit button. A user
    submitting their email + IP + UA without explicit consent is a
    compliance gap if any EU user could reach the site.

FINDING 9.4 [LOW — data minimization] — Full UA stored:
  - Could be reduced to a coarse bucket ("browser=Chrome, os=
    Windows") to retain analytics value without identifying
    individuals. Currently stored raw — every unique UA string
    is a near-unique fingerprint.

FINDING 9.5 [INFO] — No PII encryption at rest:
  - Email addresses (route.ts:160) stored in plaintext in Postgres.
    Acceptable for a small site, but if the DB is compromised (SQL
    injection elsewhere, backup leak, server theft), all contact
    emails are exposed. Application-level encryption of the email
    column would mitigate. Not a defect per se, just a defense-in-
    depth note.

FINDING 9.6 [INFO] — IP forward to formsubmit.co:
  - route.ts:175-185 forwards `name`, `email`, `message` to
    formsubmit.co (third-party). Does NOT forward IP/UA. ✅ Good
    data minimization at the forward boundary.
  - But: formsubmit.co receives the user's email + message in
    plaintext over HTTPS. Their privacy policy applies. Not a
    code defect; the operator should disclose this to users.

Verdict: ❌ FAIL. Indefinite retention of IP + full UA with no
  consent notice, no retention policy, no minimization (MED
  privacy/GDPR). 4 additional LOW/INFO findings.

Q10. HTML injection?
================================================================
Status: PASS on contact route side; depends on admin-panel rendering

Server (route.ts):
  - route.ts:159-161 — `db.contactMessage.create({ data: { name,
      email, message, ip, userAgent } })` — RAW user input stored
      to DB with NO server-side HTML escaping. The DB stores raw
      strings.
  - route.ts:190-194 — server response `{ ok, id, receivedAt }` —
    NO user-controlled data echoed back. ✅ No reflected XSS.
  - route.ts:101-130, 135-156 — all error responses return
    hardcoded error strings, no echo of user input. ✅
  - route.ts:119 — reCAPTCHA error-codes logged to SecurityLog via
    `JSON.stringify(verifyData["error-codes"] || [])`. The error
    codes come from Google's siteverify response — well-known
    strings ("invalid-input-response", "timeout-or-duplicate",
    etc.). Not user-controlled in a way that could inject HTML.
    Safe.

Client (page.tsx):
  - page.tsx:28-31 — `MessageRow` type defined (id, name, email,
    message, ip, createdAt) — used by the admin panel.
  - The PUBLIC contact form (page.tsx:766-808) does NOT render
    stored messages — only the admin panel does, and the admin
    panel rendering code is OUT OF SCOPE for this audit (per task
    instructions: only contact route + page.tsx contact form).
  - page.tsx:730 — `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html:
      sanitizeEmbed(clip.embedCode) }}` — this is for Aparat
      video-clip embeds, NOT contact data. The embed code passes
      through sanitizeEmbed. Out of scope for this audit anyway.
  - page.tsx:147 — `document.body.innerHTML = ...` — anti-theft
    domain-lock block, hardcoded template literal, no user input.
    Safe.

FINDING 10.1 [MED — depends on admin-panel rendering] — Stored
  XSS surface in admin panel (UNVERIFIED):
  - The contact route stores raw `name`, `email`, `message` to DB
    (route.ts:159-161) with NO escaping. If the admin panel
    (separate route, not in scope for this audit) renders these
    via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or any non-escaped path, it
    would be **stored XSS in the admin panel**.
  - This is the SAME pattern flagged in V17.4-SEC-12 Q5 for chat
    messages (LLM reply stored raw + served raw -> stored XSS).
    The contact-route side is safe (server doesn't render, just
    stores); the rendering side needs separate verification.
  - Recommended (NOT applied): audit the admin panel rendering of
    MessageRow fields; ensure React's default escaping is used
    (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML on these fields).

FINDING 10.2 [LOW — depends on bale.ts] — Bale markdown injection:
  - route.ts:164-168 — `notifyNewContactMessage({ id, name, email,
    message })` called on every successful submission. bale.ts is
    NOT in scope for this audit, but the prior audit V17.4-SEC-12
    Q10 documented that `notifyNewChat` (bale.ts:88-105) sends the
    visitorId to the admin's Bale chat with `parse_mode: "Markdown"`
    via `*Visitor:* ${visitorId}`. If `notifyNewContactMessage`
    follows the same pattern (sends `name` / `email` / `message`
    as Markdown), then an attacker who sets `name` to
    `[CEO Ehsan](http://evil.com/phish)` injects a clickable
    phishing link into the admin's Bale chat.
  - Verification needed: read bale.ts:notifyNewContactMessage to
    confirm whether it uses parse_mode: "Markdown" and interpolates
    user-controlled fields raw.

FINDING 10.3 [LOW] — Forward to formsubmit.co is plaintext JSON:
  - route.ts:175-185 — `name`, `email`, `message` sent as JSON
    body to formsubmit.co over HTTPS. No escaping, but
    formsubmit.co presumably renders them safely. Not the
    operator's concern (assuming formsubmit.co's rendering is
    safe — they are a reputable form-forwarding service).

Verdict: ✅ PASS on contact route + public form side. 1 MED finding
  (admin-panel stored XSS surface — depends on admin-panel
  rendering, out of scope) + 1 LOW finding (Bale markdown injection
  — depends on bale.ts, out of scope). 1 LOW INFO (formsubmit.co
  forward).

        returns a non-JSON body (e.g., NGINX 502 HTML), `res.json()` throws →
        caught at line 51 → `setItems([])`. Same silent failure.

Findings:
  F3.1 [HIGH] ContentManager.tsx:83-92 — NO try/catch wrapper at all. If fetch
        throws (network failure, server returns non-JSON before the await
        completes... actually fetch only throws on network errors, not on HTTP
        error statuses), the promise rejection propagates unhandled. The
        `loadItems()` at line 91 is skipped. Browser console shows an
        "Unhandled promise rejection" warning. User sees nothing happen.

  F3.2 [HIGH] ContentManager.tsx:86-90 — response NOT inspected. The server
        may return 401 (unauthorized), 400 (missing_id from
        content/route.ts:90,102 or equipment/route.ts:65,76), 404 (not_found
        from content/route.ts:111), or 500 — all silently treated as success.
        `loadItems()` runs unconditionally. If the cookie expired, the delete
        silently fails AND the list reload returns 401 → items go empty (see
        F1.2/F1.3). User is shown an empty list and assumes the item was
        deleted (when actually the cookie expired and nothing was deleted).

  F3.3 [LOW] ContentManager.tsx:84 — `confirm("Delete?")` blocks the JS thread.
        Native browser dialog, no styling, not localized (FA/EN users both see
