     (aimed at sighted inspectors) but worth noting.

O-13. Anti-theft detection easily bypassed:
     page.tsx:183-193 — DevTools detection uses 160px
     width/height threshold. Docked DevTools below 160px height
     (e.g., bottom-docked at 100px) does NOT trigger the
     warning. Pre-existing observation, also noted in prior
     audit V17.5-SEC-03 F-C (worklog:88542-88577).

O-14. Domain lock + dev message leak source paths:
     page.tsx:158-160 — error message tells the attacker to
     edit `src/app/page.tsx → authorizedDomains` and `src/lib/
     canvas-protect.ts → AUTHORIZED_DOMAINS` and to rebuild
     via `docker-compose up -d --build`. This reveals the
     project structure + build system to anyone running the
     site on an unauthorized domain. Pre-existing; minor info
     leak.

O-15. Honeypot field uses inline style instead of CSS class:
     page.tsx:773 — `<input style={{ position:"absolute",
     left:"-9999px", top:"auto", width:1, height:1, overflow:
     "hidden" }} />`. A dedicated `.honeypot-field` CSS class
     would be cleaner and would not be inlined on every form
     render. Also, bots that inspect computed styles can
     detect `position:absolute; left:-9999px` as a known
     honeypot pattern — using a CSS class with a less
     suspicious name (e.g., `.url-field`) would be slightly
     more robust. Low-impact.

NOTE-17 (MED, header-only check):
The middleware checks ONLY the `Content-Length` request header.
Two bypass vectors:

(a) Chunked transfer encoding: an attacker sends
    `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and streams a multi-MB body without
    a Content-Length header. The middleware's `contentLength`
    parseInt returns 0 (line 197) - the check is skipped.
    Next.js's body parser may have its own limit (default ~1MB for
    `bodySizeLimit` in route segment config), but no route in this
    codebase declares `export const bodyParser = { sizeLimit: ... }`
    or `export const runtime = 'nodejs'` overrides. The default
    Next.js 16 body size limit is 1MB for the App Router - but
    this is framework-dependent, not enforced by this codebase.

(b) Lying Content-Length: an attacker sends `Content-Length: 100`
    but streams 10MB. Next.js will likely close the connection
    when the body exceeds the declared length, but the middleware
    check itself trusts the header.

Defense-in-depth would also call `request.body` with a hard cap
via a stream-size guard. Not implemented.

----------------------------------------------------------------
8. X-FORWARDED-FOR SPOOFING - CRITICAL FINDING
----------------------------------------------------------------
CRITICAL.

The codebase trusts the FIRST element of the `x-forwarded-for`
header as the client IP in EVERY place where IP is extracted:

(a) src/middleware.ts:145-146
    `const ip = req.headers.get("x-forwarded-for")?.split(",")[0]?.trim()
                || req.headers.get("x-real-ip") || "unknown";`
    Used for rate limiting (line 148: `checkRateLimit(`${pathname}:${ip}`, max)`)

(b) src/lib/access-auth.ts:175-181  (getClientIp)
    `const forwarded = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for");
     if (forwarded) return forwarded.split(",")[0].trim();`
    Used by login/route.ts:56, admin/security/route.ts:48,79,94,
    user/verify/route.ts:30.

(c) src/app/api/contact/route.ts:48-51
    Same pattern, used for rate limit + DB-stored ip field
    (contact/route.ts:160 stores spoofed IP in db.contactMessage.ip)

(d) src/app/api/chat/route.ts:78-81
    Same pattern, used for rate limit + DB-stored ip field
    (chat/route.ts:139 stores spoofed IP in db.chatSession.ip)

(e) src/app/api/track/route.ts:12
    Same pattern, stored in db.pageView.ip

(f) src/lib/security.ts:8-17  (isIpBlocked)
    Reads blockedIp table by `ip` - but the IP is the spoofed one.
    So an attacker spoofs XFF to a new value on every request and
    is NEVER blocked.

IMPACT - Critical bypass of all rate limits + IP blocking:

- Login brute-force: attacker sends `X-Forwarded-For: <random>` per
  request -> each request hits a fresh `loginAttempts` bucket ->
  unlimited password guesses. The 5/15min limit is fully defeated.
- Contact rate limit: same - 3/10min defeated.
- Chat rate limit: same - 8/1min defeated.
- IP auto-block (security.ts:43-52, blocks after 3 "suspicious_message"
  events in 1h): the attacker rotates XFF -> never accumulates 3
  events on a single spoofed IP -> never blocked.
- Manual admin block (admin/security-dashboard/route.ts:66-75):
  admin blocks the spoofed IP, attacker rotates to a new XFF ->
  block is ineffective.
- Analytics / log poisoning: db.pageView.ip, db.contactMessage.ip,
  db.chatSession.ip, db.accessLog.ip all store the spoofed value.
  Audit trails are corrupted.

ROOT CAUSE:
The codebase is designed to run behind nginx (nginx-ehsanmorad.conf)
or the Caddy reverse proxy (Caddyfile). Both proxies DO set
X-Forwarded-For correctly (nginx: `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For
$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;` at nginx-ehsanmorad.conf:14,20,26;
Caddy sets it automatically).
The correct defense is:
  - Configure nginx/Caddy to OVERWRITE (not append to) the
    client-supplied X-Forwarded-For. nginx's `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`
    APPENDS the client's IP to the existing header - so if the
    client sends `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4`, the header becomes
    `1.2.3.4, <real-client-ip>`. The codebase takes the FIRST
    element (1.2.3.4) - the SPOOFED value, NOT the real client IP.
  - The fix: take the LAST element of X-Forwarded-For (which is the
    real client IP as set by the trusted proxy), or use `x-real-ip`
    (which nginx sets to `$remote_addr` - the actual TCP peer).
  - Alternatively, configure nginx to STRIP the inbound
    X-Forwarded-For header before adding its own:
    `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;`

CONFIRMATION - the current nginx config is VULNERABLE:
  nginx-ehsanmorad.conf:14 - `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For
  $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;`
  This appends $remote_addr to any client-supplied XFF. So a client
  sending `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4` causes nginx to forward
  `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, <real-ip>`. The codebase's
  `.split(",")[0].trim()` takes `1.2.3.4` - the attacker-controlled
  value. CRITICAL.

This finding invalidates findings #1, #2, #3 partially - the rate
limits exist but are bypassable. Findings #1-3 are "PASS-WITH-NOTE"
only because the rate limit code itself is correct; the bypass
is via the IP-extraction flaw documented here.

9. EXPENSIVE SYNC OPS - MULTIPLE FINDINGS
----------------------------------------------------------------
PARTIAL - some bounded, some not.

(a) src/app/api/chat/route.ts:177-185 - LLM call with NO timeout
    `callLLMWithFallback([...])` (providers.ts:44-70) iterates
    enabled providers, calling fetch() to OpenAI/Anthropic/Groq/
    Ollama. NO `signal: AbortController.timeout(...)` anywhere.
    Default Node.js fetch has NO timeout - a slow/hung provider
    keeps the request (and the chat handler's DB transaction)
    open indefinitely.
    MED-HIGH. An attacker can trigger many concurrent chat
    requests, each hanging on a slow LLM provider, exhausting
    the Next.js worker's connection pool.

(b) src/app/api/contact/route.ts:107-115 - reCAPTCHA verify
    fetch() to https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify
    with NO timeout. Same issue. MED.
    Mitigation: the route is rate-limited (3/10min) - but that's
    bypassable via finding #8. So 1000 concurrent slow reCAPTCHA
    requests = 1000 pending fetches.

(c) src/app/api/contact/route.ts:170-188 - formsubmit.co forward
    fetch() with NO timeout, fired via async import. Wrapped in
    .catch(() => {}) so it can't crash the request - but it CAN
    leave a dangling fetch that consumes a socket for the default
    Node.js socket timeout (~5 min). MED.

(d) src/lib/bale.ts:48-58 - sendBaleMessage fetch() to Bale API,
    NO timeout. Called from notifyNewContactMessage and
    notifyNewChat (both async, fire-and-forget via import().then()).
    Can leak dangling sockets. MED.

(e) src/lib/telegram.ts:26-37 - same as Bale. MED.

(f) src/app/api/admin/email/route.ts:74-92 - formsubmit.co fetch,
    NO timeout. Admin-only. LOW.

(g) src/app/api/chat/route.ts:179-180 - `await seedDefaultProviders()`
    called on EVERY chat request. seedDefaultProviders
    (providers.ts:202-249) checks `db.aiProvider.count()` first
    (line 203) and returns immediately if count > 0. So steady-state
    cost is one DB count() per chat request. LOW (acceptable).

(h) src/app/api/admin/content/route.ts:117-135 - bulk_import action:
    `for (const item of items) { await model.create({ data }); }`
    NO count limit on `items`. Body is 1MB-capped, but 1MB of JSON
    can hold ~10k small items. Each iteration is a sequential DB
    write -> 10k writes x ~5ms = 50s of blocking. HIGH.
    Same pattern at admin/text/route.ts:74-95 (bulk_set) and
    admin/equipment/route.ts:91-123 (bulk_import).

(i) src/lib/security.ts:27-57 - recordSuspiciousActivity
    - First call: logSecurityEvent (INSERT to securityLog)
    - Then: db.securityLog.count(...) (full scan of securityLog
      table for type+ip+createdAt filter)
    - Then if threshold: db.blockedIp.upsert + logSecurityEvent
    3-4 DB round trips per call. Called from contact/route.ts:84,91,
    100,119,122 (4 sites in contact flow alone). For a contact
    submission: 4 x recordSuspiciousActivity = up to 16 DB round
    trips. MED. The count() filter on createdAt >= hourAgo
    requires an index on (type, ip, createdAt) - schema.prisma
    should be checked.

(j) src/app/api/admin/security-dashboard/route.ts:76-79 -
    clear_logs action: `db.securityLog.deleteMany({})` with no
    WHERE. SQLite will scan the entire securityLog table and
    delete all rows. For a table with 1M rows, this can take
    seconds. Admin-only but unbounded. LOW-MED.

(k) src/app/api/admin/clear/route.ts:33-57 - chat_all / message_all
    actions delete all rows across multiple tables. Admin-only.
    LOW.

(l) /api/admin/users/logs/route.ts:33-43 - findMany with
    `take: limit` where limit is capped at 500 (line 29). PASS OK.

10. UNBOUNDED DB QUERIES - MULTIPLE FINDINGS
----------------------------------------------------------------
PARTIAL - some have take, some don't.

(a) src/app/api/admin/users/route.ts:38-58 - findMany() with NO
    `take`. Returns ALL accessUser rows. If an admin creates
    thousands of users, this query returns all of them in one
    response. HIGH.
    Fix: add `take: 100` and pagination.

(b) src/app/api/admin/content/route.ts:31-43 - 5 findMany() calls
    in a loop with NO `take`:
      for (const [name, model] of Object.entries(models)) {
        results[name + "s"] = await model.findMany({ orderBy: { order: "asc" } });
      }
    Each model (book, article, tutorial, skill, aiInstruction) is
    queried unbounded. HIGH if any model grows large.
    Same GET also calls `findMany()` on labEquipment in
    content/route.ts:11-21 (the public /api/content route) -
    `db.labEquipment.findMany({ where: { visible: true } })` -
    unbounded but `visible: true` filters. LOW-MED.

(c) src/app/api/admin/text/route.ts:18-33 - `db.siteText.findMany()`
    with NO `take` - but siteText is a small fixed set of strings.
    LOW.

(d) src/app/api/admin/clips/route.ts:16-18 - `db.aparatClip.findMany()`
    with NO `take` - small set. LOW.

(e) src/app/api/admin/nav/route.ts:11-14 - findMany with NO take -
    small set. LOW.

(f) src/app/api/admin/themes/route.ts:16-19 - findMany with NO take
    - small set. LOW.

(g) src/app/api/admin/providers/route.ts:22-24 - findMany with NO
    take - small set. LOW.

(h) src/app/api/messages/route.ts:20-32 - findMany with `take: 100`
    PASS OK.

(i) src/app/api/admin/security-dashboard/route.ts:21-27 -
    findMany with `take: 50` (blockedIps) and `take: 50` (recentLogs)
    PASS OK. Counts (lines 23-26) are bounded by COUNT semantics.

(j) src/app/api/admin/stats/route.ts:16-28 - findMany with
    `take: 10` (topPages) and `take: 20` (recentViews) PASS OK.

(k) src/app/api/chat/messages/route.ts:21-33 - findMany with
    NO `take`. Filter is `sessionId + role=assistant + createdAt>since`.
    A long chat session could have thousands of messages - all
    returned in one response. MED.
    Fix: add `take: 200` and paginate via `since`.

(l) src/app/api/admin/security-dashboard/route.ts:23-24 -
    db.securityLog.count({ where: { type: "suspicious_message" } })
    and `{ type: "failed_login" }`. Full table count with a type
    filter. If securityLog grows to millions of rows (it's
    appended to on every contact submission and never auto-trimmed),
    this count() can take seconds. MED.

(m) src/app/api/track/route.ts:20-28 - db.pageView.create({ ... }).
    No rate limit (see NOTE-26 below). Every POST creates a row.
    Unbounded writes -> unbounded table growth. HIGH (separately
    tracked as a DoS vector - see finding #11 / #12 cross-ref).

(n) /api/content (public, content/route.ts:11-21) - 9 parallel
    findMany calls with NO take on each. All public, no rate limit.
    An attacker can hammer this endpoint and force 9 DB queries per
    request. MED.

----------------------------------------------------------------
11. REQUEST TIMEOUT - NOT IMPLEMENTED
----------------------------------------------------------------
FAIL (HIGH).

No request timeout is configured anywhere in the codebase:

(a) next.config.ts - no `serverActions.timeout`, no
    `experimental.serverActions` config. Next.js 16 default for
    server actions is 30s but this only applies to server actions,
    not API routes.

(b) No AbortController or signal passed to ANY fetch() call in:
    - lib/providers.ts:100-118 (OpenAI), 127-147 (Anthropic),
      152-167 (Ollama), 172-191 (Groq)
    - lib/bale.ts:49-58
    - lib/telegram.ts:27-37
    - api/contact/route.ts:108-115 (reCAPTCHA), 175-185 (formsubmit)
    - api/admin/email/route.ts:75-84 (formsubmit)
    - api/bale/webhook/route.ts:41 (sendBaleMessage via import)
    - api/telegram/webhook/route.ts:22 (sendTelegramMessage)

(c) Caddyfile - no `timeout` or `read_timeout` directives. Caddy
    default reverse_proxy timeout is 0 (no timeout) for HTTP
    requests. Vulnerable to slowloris-style attacks via the
    reverse proxy.

(d) nginx-ehsanmorad.conf - no `proxy_read_timeout`,
    `proxy_send_timeout`, `proxy_connect_timeout`, or
    `client_body_timeout` directives. nginx defaults:
    proxy_read_timeout 60s, proxy_send_timeout 60s,
    proxy_connect_timeout 60s, client_body_timeout 60s.
    These defaults DO bound the proxy->upstream time - so nginx
    would terminate a hung /api/chat request after 60s. But this
    is ONLY if nginx is the entry point. The Dockerfile + Caddyfile
    path has NO such bound.

(e) Dockerfile / docker-compose.yml - no NODE_OPTIONS or
    --max-http-header-size flags. No UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE tuning.

IMPACT: A single hung /api/chat request (slow LLM provider) holds
a Node.js event-loop slot + a DB connection + an HTTP socket for
an unbounded duration. Concurrent hung requests can exhaust the
default Node.js UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=4 -> all subsequent DNS/SSL/fs
operations queue up -> server appears hung. HIGH.

The /api/contact route is also vulnerable - the reCAPTCHA verify
fetch and the formsubmit forward fetch can both hang.

----------------------------------------------------------------
12. MEMORY LEAKS - MOSTLY OK
----------------------------------------------------------------
PASS-WITH-NOTE.

(a) Rate-limit Maps: 4 Maps (loginAttempts, contact hits, chat hits,
    middleware rateLimitMap). All 4 have setInterval cleanup every
    5 min with .unref?.() (login/route.ts:24-32, contact/route.ts:
    11-20, chat/route.ts:12-21, middleware.ts:58-65). PASS OK.
    See NOTE-20 (LOW, growth-under-attack concern) and NOTE-21
    (LOW, no LRU cap).

(b) Prisma client singleton: db.ts:8-21 - globalThis.prisma singleton,
    not a leak. PASS OK.

(c) Lazy cached secret: access-auth.ts:20-43 - _SECRET cached once
    in module scope. Not a leak. PASS OK.

(d) No setInterval leaks: the 4 setIntervals are created at module
    load (top-level `if (typeof setInterval !== "undefined")`).
    Each is unref'd so they don't keep the process alive. PASS OK.

(e) NOTE-23 (LOW, dangling fetches): fire-and-forget `import().then()`
    patterns at:
    - contact/route.ts:164-168 (notifyNewContactMessage via Bale)
    - contact/route.ts:171-188 (formsubmit forward via settings.getSetting)
    - chat/route.ts:152-161 (notifyNewChat via Bale)
    - bale/webhook/route.ts:40-42 (sendBaleMessage)
    These spawn fetches that aren't awaited. If the fetch hangs
    (no timeout - see finding #11), the promise stays pending
    indefinitely. Each pending fetch holds a socket + ~10KB of
    internal state. Under high request volume with slow upstreams,
    this can leak memory gradually. LOW (requires upstream failure
    + high volume).

(f) NOTE-24 (LOW, no MaxListeners bump): each setInterval fires
    cleanup which iterates Map entries. No EventEmitter max-
    listeners concern here, but the 4 setIntervals all fire on
    the same 5-min cadence - minor synchronization concern, not
    a leak.

(g) NOTE-25 (LOW, db.securityLog and db.pageView unbounded growth):
    Both tables are append-only with no retention policy. Over
    months/years, they can grow to GBs, slowing count() and
    findMany queries (see finding #10 i, l). Not a memory leak
    per se, but a storage-growth DoS amplifier. The
    /api/admin/security-dashboard POST "clear_logs" action
    (sec-dash/route.ts:76-79) is the only manual mitigation,
    and it's destructive (no filter).

EXTRA FINDINGS (NOT IN 12-ITEM SCOPE BUT ENCOUNTERED)
================================================================

NOTE-26 (HIGH, /api/track has NO rate limit):
src/app/api/track/route.ts:9-34 - POST endpoint, public, NO rate
limit (not in RATE_LIMIT_PATHS at middleware.ts:21). Every POST
writes a row to db.pageView. Body is 1MB-capped, but a single
attacker can POST thousands of requests per second (subject only
to TCP/HTTP limits). Each request:
  - Creates a db.pageView row (1 INSERT)
  - Stores attacker-controlled `path`, `referrer`, `lang`
    (track/route.ts:22-27) - only `path` has a `String(body.path ||
    "/")` coercion, no length cap on path/referrer/lang values.
    Prisma will store whatever string is sent (SQLite TEXT is
    unbounded).
Combined with finding #8 (XFF spoofing), the IP stored is also
spoofed.
This is a HIGH DoS vector - unbounded DB writes, unbounded table
growth, no rate limit, public endpoint. Should be added to
RATE_LIMIT_PATHS with a per-IP limit (e.g., 60/min).

NOTE-27 (LOW, /api/track path/referrer/lang not length-capped):
track/route.ts:22-27 - `path: String(body.path || "/")`,
`referrer: body.referrer || null`, `lang: body.lang || null`.
None of these are `.slice(0, N)`. A 1MB body could submit a 1MB
`path` string. Stored verbatim in db.pageView.path. LOW practical
risk (storage only).

NOTE-28 (MED, public endpoints with no rate limit):
The following PUBLIC endpoints have NO rate limit and run DB
queries on every request:
- /api/content (content/route.ts:9-63) - 9 parallel findMany
- /api/clips (clips/route.ts:7-19) - 1 findMany
- /rss.xml (rss.xml/route.ts:9-41) - 1 findMany (take: 20) bounded OK
- /sitemap.xml (sitemap.xml/route.ts:9-43) - 3 findMany (no take
  but select: {id, date} only) - LOW
- /api/user/verify (user/verify/route.ts:16-50) - 2 findUnique +
  checkAccess - fast but unauthenticated
- /api/chat/messages GET (chat/messages/route.ts:9-44) - 1
  findMany (see finding #10 k)
- /api/route (api/route.ts:1-5) - returns "Hello, world!" -
  trivial, no concern
- /api/user/logout POST (user/logout/route.ts:7-11) - no DB,
  just clears cookie

An attacker can hammer /api/content to force 9 DB queries per
request. With 100 RPS = 900 DB queries/sec. MED.

NOTE-29 (LOW, /api/contact stores raw user-supplied strings):
contact/route.ts:160 - `data: { name, email, message, ip, userAgent }`.
name is sliced to 100, email to 200, message to 5000 (lines 77-79)
OK. userAgent is NOT sliced - `req.headers.get("user-agent")`
(contact/route.ts:52) can be up to 8KB (HTTP default). Stored
verbatim. LOW.

NOTE-30 (INFO, /api/admin/text GET returns public EN values when
not admin): admin/text/route.ts:18-26 - if checkAdminAuth fails,
the route returns `{ ok: true, texts: result }` with EN values
only. This is intentional (the comment at line 19 says
"Public - return only EN values for display"). However, the
endpoint path is `/api/admin/text` - confusing that a path
under /api/admin/ returns public data. The middleware does NOT
require a session for this route (PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES doesn't
include /api/admin/text, but middleware.ts:188 requires session
for /api/admin/* - so unauthenticated requests get 401 from
middleware BEFORE reaching the route handler). So the
"fall-through to public" branch at admin/text/route.ts:18-26 is
DEAD CODE - middleware always 401s first. INFO.

NOTE-31 (INFO, /api/admin/nav and /api/admin/themes also fall
through to public): same pattern as NOTE-30 - admin/nav/route.ts:10
(`const isAdmin = authCheck.ok; ... where: isAdmin ? {} : { visible:
true }`) and admin/themes/route.ts:14. Same dead-code concern
(middleware 401s unauthenticated requests before they reach the
route handler). The public paths /api/clips and /api/content
exist separately for unauthenticated callers. INFO.
